# FINDINGS ledger — benchmarking / orchestration findings

Each finding has a `cross_stream` pointer to the physics claim(s) it produced (in `CLAIMS.md`). Long-form
detail lives in sibling `FINDING-<YYYYMMDD>-<slug>.md` files **in this directory** — indexed below.

> Corrected 2026-08-06: this header previously pointed detail at `../benchmarking/findings/`, a directory
> that does not exist. An agent following that pointer hit a dead end, which is one reason findings written
> here were not reaching the agents that needed them.

> **BEN id allocation — take ids from your lane's RANGE, not from the shared maximum (set 2026-08-07).**
> Two collisions in one day (041, then 044): concurrent lanes each fetch, each see the same highest id,
> and each increment. Sequential allocation from a shared maximum does not work here. Ranges as Joseph
> assigned them: **the GBDT/P4 lane takes 060+; the PET/nd-unfolding lane takes 070+.** Read the range,
> not the maximum. Committed verifier receipts that cite a pre-renumber id are left as written —
> rewriting a receipt to match a later renumber would falsify it.
>
> **RENUMBERED 2026-08-09: BEN-077→061, 078→062, 079→063, 080→064.** I allocated four ids from the
> shared maximum instead of my lane's range, landing them inside the PET block — the exact mistake
> the paragraph above warns about, made while reading the paragraph above. Caught on a merge that
> brought in PET's BEN-081; no collision had occurred, but the ranges would have stopped meaning
> anything. **Four already-pushed commit messages (`aa220b4`, `34068d0`, `2fdf384`, and the
> stage-6/mechanism commit) cite the OLD ids and are left as written** — same convention as the
> verifier receipts above. Use this mapping when following a commit message into the ledger.
> The lesson generalises the header: reading the range rule is not the same as applying it, and the
> moment of allocation is when to re-read it, because `max(existing)+1` is what a tired agent
> computes by default.

| BEN-035 | **`rc=$?` after a pipeline reports the LAST stage's status, so a diagnostic that pipes its command through `tail`/`grep` cannot detect that command failing.** Hit twice on 2026-08-06. First: an `srun` suite launch whose task-count check keyed on a banner the same command had suppressed, so the check could not fire. Both cost a full diagnostic round trip and, worse, briefly asserted the opposite of the truth. **Rules.** (1) Capture the status of the command you are testing with no pipe in between (`cmd > f 2>&1; rc=$?`), then filter *reads* of `f` — the same shape BEN-026 prescribes for run logs, for the same reason. (2) `set -o pipefail` fixes the exit code but not the reasoning; prefer separating "run and record" from "filter and judge". (3) Corroborate a zero exit with evidence of *work done* (bytes produced, artifact present), because a silent success and a silent hang look identical through a pipe. A confirmation must be able to distinguish success from the specific failure it is meant to catch: the working form asserts three things — no `.git/rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply`, the commit's subject is reachable from `origin/main`, and `HEAD == origin/main`. Joseph flagged the hazard -- the GBDT lane is running in the same checkout and actively pushing, and the stash stack has no per-agent namespace. A concurrent `git stash pop`, or my own `pop` racing their `stash`, silently reassigns uncommitted work between two agents' working trees, and the failure is nearly undiagnosable afterwards: both lanes see edits they did not make and neither has a record of the move. **Why the safe forms are strictly better and not merely safer:** a WIP commit (`git commit -m wip` then `git reset --soft HEAD~1`) is per-branch and leaves a reflog entry, so the intermediate state is RECOVERABLE; a detached `git worktree` gives a genuinely independent checkout, which is also what CLAUDE.md already mandates for audit delegates -- the same isolation argument applies to my own baseline checks. `git stash` is the only one of the three whose state lives outside any branch and outside the reflog's per-branch view. **Rules.** (1) In a checkout that any other agent or session may touch, treat `git stash` as unavailable. (2) To test whether a failure is pre-existing, prefer `git worktree add` on the pre-change commit, or `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null stash create` (which produces a commit object WITHOUT touching the shared stack) and diff against that. (3) The generalization worth carrying: before using any git command that mutates repo-global state (stash, `gc`, `reflog expire`, index locks), ask whether the checkout is single-tenant. On this campaign it has not been single-tenant since 2026-08-05. | -- | EP-2026-08-09-clm012-bugfix |

Every **physics** binding was stable — `central5d_sha256`, `central4d_sha256`, `mask5d_hash`/`mask4d_hash`, `config_hash`, `endpoint_sha256`, `axis_edges` all byte-identical — which is the reassuring half. The provenance half moved: `binary_sha256` `6b60fc51…` → `61d7dfbf…` (`binary_mtime` +290,733 s ≈ 3.4 days), `source_blobs.unfold` `7b65ebcf…` → `dc74c38f…`, `source_blobs.launcher` `559bc3fb…` → `f2a49e7d…`, plus the corresponding `source_commits`. The cause is structural, not a race: `:150-151` hashes `MINERvA101/opt/bin/runEventLoopOmniFold` **as it is on disk at run time**, and `_blob`/`_srccommit` (`:137-141`) hash the **working-tree** copy of each source path. Neither is tied to the artifact being described. **Why it matters:** the ten endpoint ROOTs are dated 2026-07-18 and were produced by the *older* driver blob; after a re-run the manifest asserts today's `unfold` blob and today's binary alongside 07-18 `endpoint_sha256` values, i.e. it claims a producer that demonstrably did not produce them. Nothing is corrupted and no number moves — but the manifest is weaker as evidence exactly where it is meant to be strongest, and an attestation built on it inherits the mis-attribution. This is the standing verifier's **defect 3** ("regenerate evidence only from exact committed blobs … record the commit containing each blob") observed live. **Mitigations, cheapest first:** record the producing blob/binary from the endpoint `.done` receipts rather than re-deriving it from the working tree; or fail closed when `source_commits.unfold` is not an ancestor of the commit that the receipts name; or split the manifest's "what exists now" fields from its "what produced this" fields so the two can never be read as one claim. The 2026-08-07 preflight's regeneration was reverted (`git checkout --`) so the committed manifest still records the 07-18 producers, and a copy of it is preserved at `docs/orchestration/state/p4-standard-attestation/p4_standard_manifest-20260718-preserved.json`. | **OPEN — provenance mis-attribution on re-run; no number affected; part of the six-defect repair-4 scope (BEN-046)** | `nd-unfolding/p4_evidence.py:137-141,150-151`; `docs/orchestration/followup-agent-A-standard-05.md` (defect 3) |
| 24 | **`endpoint_sha256` binds an ARTIFACT, not a derivation — the standard 5D endpoint ROOTs are not bit-reproducible, so hash-based attestation can only ever certify "same file", never "same computation", and any legitimate re-unfold breaks the whole manifest chain.** Measured 2026-08-07 by re-unfolding all ten endpoints from the same merged inputs, same committed driver, same `--seed 42`, same `--bkg-mode purity` (job `56471429`, 10/10, zero failures) and comparing against the 2026-07-18 set: **0 of 10 sha256 match**, while the CONTENTS agree to a worst per-bin relative difference of **1.9e-11** and an integrated cross section of **2.6e-14**. The physics is unchanged; the bytes are not. Cause is reduction order — LightGBM/OpenMP partitioning depends on thread count (07-18 ran CONC=4, the re-run CONC=6) and five OmniFold iterations amplify last-bit differences; `sqrt(N)*eps` for ~1e7 events is `7.0e-13`, the same order as the measured pooled mean `-1.76e-13`. **Why this is a design defect and not a curiosity:** (a) `p4_standard_manifest.json`'s `endpoint_sha256` pins one particular RUN, so it cannot answer "was this produced by the declared computation?"; (b) `endpoint_manifest_hash` is derived from those ten hashes, and the validator's merged-inseparability gate consumes it, so **a correct, authorized re-unfold invalidates the entire chain** — a manifest that breaks on correct behaviour is a defect in the manifest, not in the behaviour; (c) the legacy-attest path (`run_p4_unfold_std.sh`, removed in repair-6) rested on "re-unfold and compare hashes", which **could never have succeeded** — it could only certify that a file had not changed on disk, which is a storage-integrity property, not a provenance one. **What should replace it:** content comparison at a declared tolerance, `p4_lib.check_reproducibility` with `REPRO_RTOL_PER_BIN = 1e-9` and `REPRO_RTOL_INTEGRAL = 1e-12` — a SPECIFICATION set by Joseph 2026-08-07, ~2 orders above the measured floor so a CONC change does not force a re-derivation, with `REPRO_MEASURED_FLOOR` recorded separately so re-measuring can never silently move the gate. Keep sha256 for storage integrity (has this file changed since I wrote it?) and stop reading it as derivation identity. | **OPEN — tolerance declared and helper landed; the manifest chain still binds hashes and must be migrated to content comparison** | `nd-unfolding/p4_lib.py` (`check_reproducibility`, `REPRO_*`); `nd-unfolding/ND_OMNIFOLD_RUN_LOG.md` (2026-08-07 re-unfold entry + its correction) |
| J36 | **Global POT scaling discards the per-playlist Data/MC ratio, skewing the MC playlist mixture.** `get_pot_scales` (`2d-unfolding/unfold_2d_omnifold_unbinned.py:114-123`) reads two `hadd`-summed `TParameter<double>` from the merged ROOT and returns one `data_pot/mc_pot`, applied uniformly as `w * pot_scale` in every collector. Verified 2026-08-01 from the 12 per-playlist pairs in `docs/orchestration/state/g2-gate1-all12-validation-20260719.json`: the ratios span **0.1707 (1B) to 0.2371 (1D), max/min − 1 = 38.9 %**, against a global 0.2124. Under global scaling playlist 1M (18.0 % of MC POT) is over-weighted by 17.1 % and 1D+1F (26.4 % combined) under-weighted by ~11 %; POT-weighted mean absolute mixture error **9.4 %**. **The total normalization is NOT biased** — global and per-playlist scaling agree exactly when the MC rate per POT is playlist-independent — so this cannot explain or be excluded by the 2D paper reproduction at 1.011. The error is purely in the playlist *mixture* and propagates only through playlist-dependent flux shape and detector conditions. Note the same `hadd`-summing hazard **is** explicitly defended two functions away for `pTmu_fiducial_nucleons` (`:1320-1329`, "do not trust the merged `TParameter<double>`") and trap #8 below; the POT ratio was never given the same treatment. It is therefore no longer a scoping question about one function — the scope is the class, and the duplication (the ratio is recomputed in every consumer rather than obtained from one vetted producer) is the thing a repair has to address. ## Resolved traps that WILL bite again if forgotten

| # | Trap | Detail lives in |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | **Never bare-`hadd` a `_universes_full` omnifile** — ROOT 100 GB TTree rollover aborts mid-merge leaving a partial missing the data+bkg trees. Use `2d-unfolding/uq/hadd_universes_full.py`. | `2d-unfolding/2D_OMNIFOLD_REFERENCE.md` §Event-loop workflow |

That is **correct for an EXTENSIVE quantity** (POT, event counts, migration censuses — 8 of the 10 default-mode fields that transit a merge) and **wrong for an intensive one, a per-playlist constant, or a 0/1 FLAG**, which becomes a count in [0,12]. Two known instances: `pTmu_fiducial_nucleons` would be inflated 12× (writer retired, reader refuses the merged value, fixed tracker constant 3.2353e30 substituted), and `hasTruthOnlyMisses` reports 12 (reader fixed 2026-08-09; **writer still misnamed**, OPEN). **A fourth case no per-field review can catch:** two extensive fields can each merge correctly while a quantity DERIVED from them does not — that is J36 above, `sum(dataPOT)/sum(mcPOT)`, which sat two functions from the correct `pTmu_fiducial_nucleons` defence. Pass `'f'` explicitly for anything that is not extensive (five fields already do), and name a merged field for its merged meaning. **Complete triaged inventory of all 15 hadd-transiting fields, mechanically regenerable:** `docs/orchestration/FINDING-20260809-tparameter-merge-semantics.md` + `audit_tparameter_merge_semantics.py`. | same, and the finding above |

## Resume-skip validates existence, not completeness (found 2026-07-17, 4D corrected uthrow)
`[[ -s $OUT ]] && skip` resume guards (used across many sbatch launchers) treat any non-empty
output as done. Producers that atomic-save per-unit into one file (e.g. `unified_throw_cov.py
do_throws` per-throw saves) leave VALID-but-partial files when interrupted — the resume then
permanently skips them. Bit us: comb4dCc 55971617 failed on 15/160 missing throws because slabs
31,34-39 were partial leftovers of an interrupted multinode run; all 40 array tasks "COMPLETED".
Caught only by the combine's `--expected-throws` manifest gate. Repair: partials moved to
`uq_4d/corrected/uthrow_slabs_4d/partial_20260716_interrupted/`, regen 56025478 -> combine
56025481 -> adopt 56025483. Fix pattern for future launchers: content-validated resume (open the
file, check unit inventory) or write-to-temp + rename-on-complete. (BEN-023.)

**FIXED REPO-WIDE 2026-08-01** (closes BEN-023 and audit J35 + J10, which are the same defect
found independently in two subtrees). Completion is now an explicit record, not an inference from
size: `lib/resume_guard.sh` provides `rg_skip_if_complete` / `rg_run` / `rg_publish`, which stamp a
`${OUT}.done` marker **only after the producer exits 0** and bind it to the output's size+mtime, so
a later truncation invalidates its own marker. An interrupted producer cannot leave one behind, so
the resume re-runs. 85 guards across 84 shell files converted. The marker convention is deliberately
the one `nd-unfolding/run_p4_unfold_std.sh` already used — that script was the in-repo precedent and
is left alone, as is `run_p4_merge_audit_std.sh`; both already validate content.

On the Python side (J10) `nd-unfolding/pet/atomic_write.py` carries the transaction —
temp sibling → fsync → `os.replace` → marker last — and `train_fullevent_nominal.py:254` uses it
instead of the bare `np.savez_compressed`, plus a no-clobber guard that refuses to replace an
output already marked complete (`--allow-overwrite` opts in) and that fires *before* the eight
GPU-hours. Gate-4 re-issued as
`docs/orchestration/state/p3f-pet-gate4-launch-code-gate-20260801.json` (Step 2b; no physics
re-run). `fullevent_dump_contract.py` was deliberately left byte-identical — it is frozen by the
G2 **dump-provenance** receipt, not a code gate; see that receipt's `not_reissued_deliberately`.

**Two traps in the fix itself.**
1. **Nothing on disk has a marker.** The first resume after this lands re-runs everything.
   Run `lib/backfill_completion_markers.sh --validator {root|npz} --glob '<pattern>'` over the live
   output trees *before* resubmitting — RESTORE-2026-08-03 Step 0b. Read its FAIL list: those are
   the partials the old guard was hiding.
2. **`RESUME_ADOPT_LEGACY=1` is the old bug, opted into.** It adopts on a bare size check and warns
   every time. Prefer a validator.

Regression-pinned by `nd-unfolding/tests/test_resume_guard.py`, whose repo-wide scan fails if
`[[ -s $OUT ]] && skip` reappears anywhere, and `nd-unfolding/tests/test_atomic_write.py`.

## The engine's "Last val loss" prints the FIRST epoch, not the last

`omnifold_nn/omnifold/omnifold.py:303` logs `hist.history['val_loss'][0]` under the label
`Last val loss`. Index 0 is **epoch 1**. Anyone judging convergence from the training log is reading the
first epoch of the fit.

Found 2026-08-06 by a fresh-context review of the D2 powered-closure FAIL (job 56381674), and it had
already done damage: two sessions independently proposed "the fit is optimization-limited, raise
`epochs`" without opening the history pickles. The pickles refute it -- step-2 train loss moves 3.2e-5
across 8 epochs in iteration 2, and that iteration's `val_loss` gets *worse* (0.829560 -> 0.829612, best
at epoch 1). A fit with no remaining gradient signal, mislabelled as a fit starved of steps.

Related, same file: `ModelCheckpoint(save_best_only=True)` (`:272-275`) writes **best-val** weights, while
`reweight` uses the **last-epoch in-memory** model. On-disk checkpoints are therefore not bit-identical to
what a run actually used -- calibrate before trusting an inference-only reproduction from them.

Fixing the label touches `omnifold.py`, which is hash-bound by the Gate-4 launch-code gate, so it must
ride a deliberate re-issue rather than a drive-by edit.

Extended 2026-08-07: the plateau is a property of **all six** trainings of `56381674`, not just iteration
2 (train loss moves 1.13e-3 across 8 epochs on the first, 3.0e-5 on the last; val argmin at {5,5,7,1,6,5}
of 8). Two consequences for anyone reading these logs. `EarlyStopping(patience=10)` **cannot fire** at
`epochs=8`, and Keras 2.15 restores best weights *only* inside its stop branch (`on_train_end` merely
prints) -- so every run on this campaign has used last-epoch weights, and the `ModelCheckpoint` mismatch
noted above is therefore the norm rather than an edge case. `ReduceLROnPlateau` is at `patience=1000`
(`:263-265`) and `get_optimizer` returns a bare Adam at a flat LR (`:376-380`, `num_steps` accepted and
unused), so no schedule ever engages either. Table and consequences:
`docs/orchestration/FINDING-20260807-d2-underfitting-probe.md` §1.

## The FPS extractor divides the cross section by a reco efficiency it must not divide by

**RESOLVED 2026-08-06** (option A, authorized by Joseph; fix reviewed by an independent fresh-context
session before commit). Left here rather than deleted: the *reason it survived* is the reusable part.

**Severity, CORRECTED.** The first write-up of this entry said "2.36x on the integral and 398x in the
lowest `p_parallel` bin". Both numbers were wrong and both were too small:

* `2.36 = 1/<a>` is what you would get dividing the *aggregate* by the *global* acceptance. The code
  divided **cell by cell**, so by Jensen the integral inflates far more:
  `sum_b m_b/a_b / sum_b m_b = **122.6**` from the committed acceptance map, and **48-177x** per pT row
  over the rows carrying >99% of the truth mass.
* `398 = 1/0.00251` is the `p_parallel` **marginal slice** [0, 0.75], not a cell. The worst single
  **cell** is `a_b = 0.0012397`, i.e. **807x**.

Recomputed independently this turn from `products/pet/fullevent_fps/acceptance_map_fullevent_fps.json`.
Legs 1-3 below were verified in source before the finding was relayed.

1. `extract_fullevent_fps.py:390-404` `completeness_2d` computes
   `c = sum_w(pass_truth & pass_reco) / sum_w(pass_truth)` -- **reco efficiency**. Its docstring says
   "Verbatim `PETxsec5D._comp`".
2. `xsec_nd.py:79` places it in the **denominator**: `denom = completeness * flux * n_nucleons * pot * vol`.
3. `extract_fullevent_fps.py:431-434` histograms `(w_truth * push)` over **all** `pass_truth` rows,
   including truth-only misses, whose `push` is the `nu_k` OmniFold step 2 assigns them
   (`omnifold.py:218-220`). `counts` is therefore **already acceptance-corrected**, so dividing by
   efficiency is a **double correction**.

On this exact 285-cell grid the correct completeness is **identically 1**: the validated GBDT FPS unfolds
carry `globalCompleteness = 1.0000000000000002` with all 266 nonzero `hCompletenessND_flat` bins at
1.000000, and `unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py:993-999` defines completeness as a **coverage** correction,
not an efficiency. `PETxsec5D` only ever survived carrying an efficiency there because
`pet_systematics_5d.py:127-141` overrides its own value with the GBDT one; the FPS port deliberately
dropped that anchor (`extract_fullevent_fps.py:459-461`, "NONE -- no such anchor exists for this domain").
**That comment is false** -- the anchor exists in this repo, on this grid, and it is the constant 1.

**Two tests look like coverage and provide none:**

- `tests/test_fullevent_extract.py:351-376` recomputes the formula by calling `ex.completeness_2d` **itself**
  and asserts bit-equality (`rtol=0, atol=0`). It verifies the extractor calls the helpers it calls, and has
  **zero power** over whether the quantity is the right physics. This is the self-agreement antipattern of
  `AUDIT-FINDINGS-20260729-B.md` section 4.
- `tests/test_fullevent_extract.py:331-342` **pins the reco-efficiency semantics as intended behaviour**, so
  anyone repairing the double-correction must first break a test that reads as authoritative.

**FIXED via (A): the division is gone.** Joseph authorized (A) on 2026-08-06. The argument recorded in
the extractor is now **structural rather than empirical**: `extract_cross_section_nd`'s `completeness`
argument means *coverage of the truth denominator by the OmniFold input*
(`unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py:992-999` builds it as `of_in/denom_nd`), and this extractor has no
separate truth denominator -- the declared fiducial domain **is** `pass_truth` -- so coverage is **1 by
construction**. The GBDT `globalCompleteness = 1.0000000000000002` is corroboration, not the reason;
leading with the measurement is what invites a future re-anchoring. Option (B) (mask `counts` to
`pass_truth & pass_reco`) was rejected: it would delete the FPS extension the campaign exists to add.

`comp` keeps one role, **as a reporting mask only**. It subsumes `denom > 0` by construction, so the
reported domain is set entirely by the reco efficiency; this **preserves** the pre-fix domain, since
`comp == 0` already forced those cells to 0. It is a **floor**, not the acceptance-supported vs
model-dependent tiering decision, which remains open at `docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md:430-438` and covers far more
truth mass (25.93% below `a_b < 0.01`) than this mask's 4 cells (4.6e-7 of truth mass).

Coverage = 1 is now **guarded, not assumed**: `assert_truth_denominator_coverage` fails closed, mirroring
`unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py:747-752`, which raises rather than assuming its analogue.

**Step 4b is unblocked.** Step 4 was never affected.

## The same construction exists in `pointcloud_projection.py`, off the gated path

`nd-unfolding/pet/pointcloud_projection.py:236-241` has the identical shape -- `counts` over
`pass_truth`, `comp = ofin/denom`, passed as the divisor. It is **not** on the gated publication product
path, so it is recorded rather than fixed, so that it is not rediscovered as a new finding. Anything
promoting that path to a product must settle it first.

## The closure driver persists no inference contract

`closure_powered_truth_reweight.py:287` saves only `dump_rows_a/b`, `weights_push`, `mc_indices`.
Architecture comes from `meta` (`:261-263`) and the input normalization is derived inside
`build_fullevent_loaders` at run time, so **there is no stored normalization to assert against** when
reproducing a run by inference. The nominal driver stores its norms; the closure driver does not. Any
inference-only reproduction must reproduce the same row population (`dump_rows_b` makes that possible) and
must treat the spectrum reproduction as its only falsification handle.

## The PET covariance summaries carry no estimator stamp — the fact lives only in the launcher

`products/pet/bkgsub/pet_cstat_bkgsub_5d.summary.json` and its siblings record `n_replicas`,
`replica_ids`, `n_reported_bins`, the sqrt-trace and per-bin ratios — and **nothing about the estimator
that produced them**: no `niter`, no schema/feature set, no commit, no job id. Their producers
(`pet/combine_cstat_bkgsub.py`, `pet/assemble_ctotal_bkgsub.py`) do not record it either, because they
combine replica outputs and never see the training config.

**Correction, 2026-08-06:** an earlier version of this entry said the fact "was never written down."
That is wrong, and wrong in the direction that matters. `pet/sbatch_pet_nominal_bkgsub.sh:42` pins
`NITER="${PET_NITER:-2}"`, its header at `:29` states `iters = 2` in as many words, and `:14` carries
the banner **"QUARANTINED RECOIL-ONLY CROSS-CHECK LAUNCHER — NOT a publication path"**, with `:15-17`
naming the recoil loader and the bkgsub purity target and noting that "C_stat, C_ml, and systematic
blocks all reference THIS nominal." So the provenance is recorded — just not in the artifact a reader
of the covariance would open.

That makes the classification **stronger**, not weaker. These components are disqualified from the
`niter=3` budget by three *positive* facts, not by an absence: they were built at **`niter=2`**, on a
path the repo itself labels **non-publication**, over a **10550-bin recoil domain** (against 10694 for
the 5D lane re-rolled in `uq_5d/rescaled_20260806/j28_reroll_20260806.json`). This satisfies
`PLAN-20260806-niter3-budget-and-J28-reroll.md` rule 5, which demands a stated reason rather than the
absence of a reason to doubt.

The debt that remains is the **stamp**, and it is real: nothing in the artifact chain would have told a
future reader any of the above, and the whole `bkgsub` budget — C_syst, C_retrain, C_stat, C_ml,
C_lateral and the assembled C_total — hangs off that one quarantined nominal.

**Fix forward:** any new covariance component must stamp the estimator config it was computed under
(at minimum `niter`, schema/feature-set identifier, and the producing commit) into its own summary,
the way `train_fullevent_nominal.py` stamps `seed_policy` into its weights artifact. A covariance
without that stamp is unclassifiable from the artifact the moment the estimator moves, and the
estimator has now moved twice (full-event schema 2026-08-01, `niter` 2026-08-06).

## `step1_class_ratio` in the nominal artifact is a stored TARGET, not an achieved measurement

Found 2026-08-07 by making the mistake. Investigating the nominal's fold-forward failure I read
`pet_fullevent_nominal_weights.npz`'s `step1_class_ratio = 1.1240802949941018`, saw it equal Gate-2's R
exactly, and concluded *"not the classic step-1 defect — that signature is the class ratio forced to 1, ours
is exactly R."* **That inference is invalid.** `train_fullevent_nominal.py:464` sets
`class_ratio = target_meta.get("step1_class_ratio")` — from the loader's target metadata — and stores it
verbatim at `:505`. `fullevent_fps_dataloader.step1_class_ratio_from_dump` derives R from the dump's data/MC
yields. So the field is **the target R, re-stored**; it can never disagree with R and therefore carries **zero
information** about what step 1 achieved. Agreement is tautological.

The trap is the name. A field called `step1_class_ratio` sitting beside genuine measurements
(`cap_saturation_frac`, `fold_forward_sum_w_push_reco`) reads as "the class ratio step 1 produced". It is a
copy of the input. **Consequence:** the step-1 under-achievement hypothesis is *not* ruled out for the
2026-08-07 nominal, and it is now the leading candidate — the historical defect drives the effective ratio
toward 1, and a folded-forward ratio of 0.7465 against a required 1.1241 is the right direction for it.

**Fix forward, two parts.** (1) Rename or re-document the stored field so it cannot be read as an outcome —
`step1_class_ratio_target` would have prevented this. (2) The achieved value has now been measured by
trajectory job `56525829`: iteration 0 is correct-sign and within 9.74% of R, while iterations 1 and 2
are wrong-signed. The defect is therefore in post-feedback iteration dynamics, not an initial class-ratio
normalization failure. Detail and exact numbers: `docs/orchestration/FINDING-20260807-step1-under-achieves.md`.

Found 2026-08-07 while working plan Step 4. The cluster suite collected **764** tests against the local

- `nd-unfolding/tests/test_cstat_100rep.py` — **5 tests**, **still untracked**, because it imports
  `combine_cstat_bkgsub_100rep`, and **that module is untracked too**. Committing the test alone would

91:| BEN-035 | **`rc=$?` after a pipeline reports the LAST stage's status, so a diagnostic that pipes its command through `tail`/`grep` cannot detect that command failing.** Hit twice on 2026-08-06. 103:| BEN-042 | **A decomposition's "scatter penalty" is not what removing the bias would cost, and quoting it against the criterion's headroom inverts the answer twice.** Diagnosing D2 I found that `FINDING-20260806-niter4-decision.md` 2b compares its scatter penalty `E_w[|1-r|] - |1-E_w[r]| = 0.08443` — weight-NORMALISED, a fraction of the gap — against `residual_budget_abs = 0.046854`, an ABSOLUTE L1 (`0.20 x gap`). (2) The general form: **an error's magnitude in its own units is not its magnitude in the units of the claim it threatens**, and the conversion factor is a physical property of the system that has to be measured, not assumed to be O(1). (3) When a large error and a small tolerance sit in the same region, the cheap resolution is usually to MEASURE the propagation rather than to argue about it — this took one pass over files already on disk and closed a question that had been argued twice. (4) Cost of getting it wrong in the safe direction: nothing, one measurement. In the unsafe direction: a published sentence withdrawn on an unquantified premise. Measure first. **Provenance note: this is the third mechanism proposed from the directing side and refuted in this lane** (lateral-replacement, W-mixing, mixture-error-threatens-983), against zero confirmed; Joseph's own instruction is to weight accordingly and keep TESTING proposed mechanisms rather than implementing them. Recording the base rate is the point — a proposer with a 0/3 record is still worth listening to, because each refutation cost one bounded measurement and two of the three produced better results than a confirmation would have. | — | EP-2026-08-07-gbdt-closeout |

30:| 24 | **`endpoint_sha256` binds an ARTIFACT, not a derivation — the standard 5D endpoint ROOTs are not bit-reproducible, so hash-based attestation can only ever certify "same file", never "same computation", and any legitimate re-unfold breaks the whole manifest chain.** Measured 2026-08-07 by re-unfolding all ten endpoints from the same merged inputs, same committed driver, same `--seed 42`, same `--bkg-mode purity` (job `56471429`, 10/10, zero failures) and comparing against the 2026-07-18 set: **0 of 10 sha256 match**, while the CONTENTS agree to a worst per-bin relative difference of **1.9e-11** and an integrated cross section of **2.6e-14**.    114	#
   115	#   worst per-bin deviation observed        1.831e-11     <- the fully COHERENT ceiling: if every

   117	#                                                            would move by about this much

   119	#                                                            round-off with random signs

   121	#
   122	# READ 103.4x CORRECTLY: it is the leg's DYNAMIC RANGE -- a property of the instrument, derived
   123	# from one endpoint's worst per-bin deviation and sqrt(N). It is NOT a spread, and it is not the

   126	# from nothing in particular, and an earlier draft of this reasoning did quote a "~110x span" as
   127	# though it were an observed spread -- it was three maxima taken from three different

   153	#   (2) PER-BIN CORRELATION with the central value. Round-off is uncorrelated with bin content;
   154	#       a physics or normalisation change scales with it.
   155	# A breach that is sign-biased near 0.4594 AND uncorrelated with content is the round-off tail:

   158	INTEGRAL_LEG_COHERENT_CEILING = 1.831e-11   # worst observed per-bin deviation; see above
   159	INTEGRAL_LEG_INCOHERENT_FLOOR = 1.770e-13   # ceiling / sqrt(10694)

   161	
   162	def diagnose_integral_breach(a, b, central=None):
   163	    """PRE-SPECIFIED breach diagnostic (2026-08-09). Written BEFORE any breach, so the criterion
   164	    cannot be chosen to fit the number that triggers it. Returns measurements only; it does not
   165	    decide, because the decision is stated above and does not depend on anything it returns."""
   166	    a = np.asarray(a, float); b = np.asarray(b, float)
   167	    m = np.abs(b) > 0
   168	    d = a[m] - b[m]
   169	    nz = d != 0
   170	    n = int(nz.sum())
   171	    frac_pos = float(np.mean(d[nz] > 0)) if n else float("nan")
   172	    out = {"n_deviating_bins": n, "frac_positive": frac_pos}
   173	    if n:
   174	        se_roundoff = math.sqrt(0.4594 * (1 - 0.4594) / n)
   175	        out["sigma_from_roundoff_bias"] = (frac_pos - 0.4594) / se_roundoff
   176	        out["sigma_from_half"] = (frac_pos - 0.5) / math.sqrt(0.25 / n)
   177	    if central is not None:
   178	        c = np.asarray(central, float)[m]
   179	        rel = d / np.abs(b[m])
   180	        if np.std(c) > 0 and np.std(rel) > 0:
   181	            out["corr_reldev_vs_central"] = float(np.corrcoef(rel, c)[0, 1])
   182	    return out
   183	
   184	
   185	# MEASURED floor, recorded separately from the declared tolerance on purpose: re-measuring it
   186	# must never silently move the gate. Job 56471429 (CONC=6) vs the 2026-07-18 set (CONC=4),
   187	# ten endpoints, 65856 bins each, 106940 reported bins pooled:
   188	#   worst relative bin difference   1.9e-11
   189	#   integral agreement              2.6e-14
   190	#   pooled mean deviation          -1.76e-13   (sd 1.96e-12)
   191	#   fraction of bins deviating +    0.4594     -- 26.6 sigma from 0.5, i.e. a REAL systematic
   192	#                                                 sign preference, which is the expected
   193	#                                                 signature of a deterministic rounding path
   194	#                                                 and NOT evidence of symmetric noise.
   195	# sqrt(N)*eps for ~1e7 events is 7.0e-13, the same order as the pooled mean.
   196	REPRO_MEASURED_FLOOR = {
   197	    "job": "56471429", "conc_new": 6, "conc_reference": 4,
   198	    "worst_rel_bin": 1.9e-11, "integral_rel": 2.6e-14,
   199	    "pooled_mean": -1.76e-13, "pooled_sd": 1.96e-12,
   200	    "frac_positive": 0.4594, "frac_positive_sigma_from_half": 26.6,
   201	    "n_reported_bins_pooled": 106940,
   202	}
   203	
   204	
   205	def check_reproducibility(a, b, rtol_bin=REPRO_RTOL_PER_BIN, rtol_int=REPRO_RTOL_INTEGRAL):
   206	    """Compare two runs of the same endpoint by CONTENT, not by bytes.
   207	
   208	    Returns the measured (max per-bin relative difference, integral relative difference).
   209	    Fails closed if either exceeds the declared tolerance."""
   210	    a = np.asarray(a, float); b = np.asarray(b, float)
   211	    require(a.shape == b.shape, f"reproducibility: shape {a.shape} != {b.shape}")
   212	    m = np.abs(b) > 0
   213	    require(m.any(), "reproducibility: reference has no positive bins")
   214	    rel = np.max(np.abs(a[m] - b[m]) / np.abs(b[m]))
   215	    sa, sb = float(a.sum()), float(b.sum())
   216	    rel_int = abs(sa / sb - 1.0) if sb != 0 else float("inf")
   217	    require(rel <= rtol_bin,
   218	            f"reproducibility: max per-bin relative difference {rel:.3e} > {rtol_bin:.0e}")
   219	    require(rel_int <= rtol_int,
   220	            f"reproducibility: integral relative difference {rel_int:.3e} > {rtol_int:.0e}")
   221	    return {"max_rel_bin": float(rel), "rel_integral": float(rel_int)}

   238	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- config / hashes
   239	class P4Config:
   240	    """Frozen unfold configuration; its hash pins seed/axes/iters/estimator so a
   241	    covariance can never be built from mismatched-config endpoints."""
   242	    def __init__(self, axes="eavail,q3,W", iters=5, seed=42, estimator="lgbm",
   243	                 use_weights=True, universe=None, bkg_mode=STANDARD_BKG_MODE):
   244	        self.axes = axes; self.iters = int(iters); self.seed = int(seed)
   245	        self.estimator = estimator; self.use_weights = bool(use_weights)
   246	        self.universe = universe          # MUST be None for active endpoints
   247	        self.bkg_mode = bkg_mode          # G-1: never inherited from the driver default
   248	    def as_dict(self):
   249	        # repair-4 (D3a): `full_phase_space_reported_grid` used to be bolted onto
   250	        # man["config"] in p4_evidence.py AFTER config_hash was computed, so the recorded hash
   251	        # did not cover the recorded configuration -- the declared config was not hash-bound.
   252	        # It belongs in the config object, where as_dict() and hash() both see it.
   253	        return {"axes": self.axes, "iters": self.iters, "seed": self.seed,
   254	                "estimator": self.estimator, "use_weights": self.use_weights,
   255	                "universe": self.universe, "bkg_mode": self.bkg_mode,
   256	                "full_phase_space_reported_grid": GRID_NBINS}
   257	    def hash(self):
   258	        return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(self.as_dict(), sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
   259	    def footing(self):
   260	        """The nested footing block as the PRODUCER emits it. Consumers must read this
   261	        shape, not a flattened copy of it -- a fixture shaped like the consumer is how
   262	        BEN-040's gate stayed green while failing on every real input."""
   263	        f = dict(STANDARD_REQUIRED_FOOTING)
   264	        f.update({"estimator": self.estimator, "seed": self.seed, "iters": self.iters,
   265	                  "use_weights": self.use_weights, "bkg_mode": self.bkg_mode})
   266	        return f
   267	    def validate(self):
   268	        require(self.universe is None, "active endpoint config must not set --universe")
   269	        require(self.seed == 42, f"standard P4 requires fixed seed 42 (got {self.seed})")
   270	        require(self.use_weights, "standard P4 requires --use-weights")
   271	        require(self.iters == 5, f"standard P4 production uses 5 iters (got {self.iters})")
   272	        require(self.axes == "eavail,q3,W", f"standard P4 requires axes=eavail,q3,W (got {self.axes})")
   273	        require(self.estimator == "lgbm", f"standard P4 requires estimator=lgbm (got {self.estimator})")
   274	        require(self.bkg_mode in KNOWN_BKG_MODES,
   275	                f"unknown bkg_mode {self.bkg_mode!r} (known: {list(KNOWN_BKG_MODES)})")
   276	        require(self.bkg_mode == STANDARD_BKG_MODE,
   277	                f"standard P4 is quoted on {STANDARD_BKG_MODE!r} by the 2026-08-07 decision "
   278	                f"(got {self.bkg_mode!r}); changing it re-opens RUNBOOK-20260807 §2 reading (B) "
   279	                f"and invalidates the J28-corrected covariance")
   280	        return True

   283	# ------------------------------------------------------- footing evidence from logs (G-1)
   284	# The driver announces its background mode on the NEGWEIGHT branches only
   285	# (unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py:842,895 -> "[INFO] bkg-mode=<mode>: ..."); the purity
   286	# branch (:883) prints nothing about mode and instead calls build_measured_training_nd,
   287	# whose verbose line is "[INFO] measured training: sum=... zero=.../...".
   288	#
   289	# So in this two-branch print, SILENCE IS A BRANCH: a log with the measured-training line
   290	# and no bkg-mode line positively identifies purity rather than leaving it unknown. That is
   291	# exactly the inference BEN-041 records failing to make. Both the flag and both
   292	# announcements landed together in cf8a4a6 (2026-07-11), before the 2026-07-18 endpoint
   293	# ROOTs, so an absent announcement is informative and not a version gap.
   294	_BKG_MODE_ANNOUNCE = "[INFO] bkg-mode="
   295	_PURITY_SIGNATURE = "[INFO] measured training:"
   296	
   297	
   298	def classify_log_bkg_mode(text):
   299	    """Return (mode, reason) for one unfold log. mode is a member of KNOWN_BKG_MODES, or
   300	    None when the log cannot decide -- which callers must treat as UNPROVABLE, not as
   301	    'probably fine'."""
   302	    announced = None
   303	    for line in text.splitlines():
   304	        i = line.find(_BKG_MODE_ANNOUNCE)
   305	        if i >= 0:
   306	            tail = line[i + len(_BKG_MODE_ANNOUNCE):]
   307	            tok = tail.split(":", 1)[0].strip()
   308	            if tok in KNOWN_BKG_MODES:
   309	                if announced is not None and announced != tok:
   310	                    return None, f"log announces conflicting modes {announced!r} and {tok!r}"
   311	                announced = tok
   312	            else:
   313	                return None, f"log announces unrecognized bkg-mode {tok!r}"
   314	    if announced is not None:
   315	        if announced == "purity":
   316	            # the purity branch never announces; an announcement claiming purity means the
   317	            # log did not come from this driver's known print set.
   318	            return None, "log announces bkg-mode=purity, which this driver's purity branch never prints"
   319	        return announced, f"driver announced bkg-mode={announced}"
   320	    if _PURITY_SIGNATURE in text:
   321	        return "purity", ("no bkg-mode announcement + build_measured_training_nd signature "
   322	                          "present => purity branch (the silent branch)")
   323	    return None, ("no bkg-mode announcement and no measured-training signature; the run may "
   324	                  "have been non-verbose, so the branch is unprovable from this log")

   327	def require_standard_footing(manifest, required_bkg_mode=STANDARD_BKG_MODE):
   328	    """Fail closed unless the manifest carries a complete footing block that matches the
   329	    standard requirement. Mirrors fps_provenance.require_footing's semantics -- absent is
   330	    'unprovable' and fails, exactly like mismatched -- without importing or mutating it."""
   331	    foot = manifest.get("footing")
   332	    require(isinstance(foot, dict) and foot,
   333	            "manifest has no footing block (unprovable): the standard lane must record its "
   334	            "background footing, not inherit the driver default")
   335	    for k, v in STANDARD_REQUIRED_FOOTING.items():
   336	        require(foot.get(k) == v, f"footing.{k}={foot.get(k)!r} != {v!r}")
   337	    require("bkg_mode" in foot, "footing has no bkg_mode (unprovable)")
   338	    require(foot["bkg_mode"] in KNOWN_BKG_MODES,
   339	            f"footing.bkg_mode={foot['bkg_mode']!r} is not a known mode")
   340	    if required_bkg_mode is not None:
   341	        require(foot["bkg_mode"] == required_bkg_mode,
   342	                f"footing.bkg_mode={foot['bkg_mode']!r} != required {required_bkg_mode!r}")
   343	    return True

   373	    """SELF-DECLARING REJECTION (2026-08-09). A candidate built without a verifier PASS carries
   374	    its own refusal, the pattern fps_control_manifest.json already uses, so the artifact declares

   388	def require_adoptable(prov):
   389	    """Refuse a self-declared non-adoptable candidate. Truthiness is the right test here and
   390	    the recorded-fields sweep's flag on it is a shape match, not a defect: the truthy value
   391	    means REFUSE, so a literal True is fail-closed. The failure mode worth guarding is the key
   392	    going absent, which no comparison operator would catch either -- the guard is the
   393	    both-directions test in tests/test_p4_repair.py."""
   394	    require(not prov.get(NON_ADOPTABLE_KEY),
   395	            f"this candidate declares {NON_ADOPTABLE_KEY}=true -- it was built without a "
   396	            f"verifier PASS and is not adoptable. {prov.get('non_adoptable_reason', '')}")

   399	def require_candidate_path(path):
   400	    """Positive allowlist + negative denylist: a candidate MUST live under the
   401	    candidate subdir and MUST NOT match any adopted/protected token. Prevents both
   402	    the round-2 self-rejection (candidate name containing '_final') and any write
   403	    onto an adopted/central path."""
   404	    # repair-5 (defect 4a). History: this was first a bare substring test, then a
   405	    # normpath component match -- and the verifier defeated the second one too, because a
   406	    # component match succeeds ANYWHERE the sequence appears, so
   407	    # `/evil/active_universe_5d/standard/candidate/out.root` passed, and normpath does not
   408	    # resolve symlinks. Containment must be RESOLVED and anchored to this repository:
   409	    # realpath both sides, then require commonpath(candidate_root, target) == candidate_root.
   410	    cand_root = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(ND_ROOT, CANDIDATE_SUBDIR))
   411	    # Callers pass repo-relative ("nd-unfolding/active_universe_5d/...") or ND-relative
   412	    # ("active_universe_5d/...") paths depending on where they cd to, so resolve a relative
   413	    # path against BOTH known roots and accept it if either lands inside. An absolute path is
   414	    # taken as given. Resolution is realpath, so symlinks cannot smuggle a target out.
   415	    if os.path.isabs(path):
   416	        cands = [path]
   417	    else:
   418	        cands = [os.path.join(ND_ROOT, path), os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, path)]
   419	    resolved, inside = None, False
   420	    for c in cands:
   421	        t = os.path.realpath(c)
   422	        if resolved is None:
   423	            resolved = t
   424	        try:
   425	            if os.path.commonpath([cand_root, t]) == cand_root and t != cand_root:
   426	                resolved, inside = t, True
   427	                break
   428	        except ValueError:                 # different drives / unrelated roots
   429	            continue
   430	    require(inside,
   431	            f"candidate must resolve inside {cand_root} (got {path} -> {resolved})")
   432	    for t in _ADOPTED_TOKENS:
   433	        require(t not in path, f"refusing candidate onto adopted/protected path (token {t!r})")
   434	    return True

   437	def prove_identity(A, B, rtol, label):
   438	    """Fail-closed max-relative-difference identity gate (no subtraction hidden)."""
   439	    A = np.asarray(A, dtype=float); B = np.asarray(B, dtype=float)
   440	    require(A.shape == B.shape, f"{label}: shape {A.shape} != {B.shape}")
   441	    denom = max(1e-300, float(np.max(np.abs(A))))
   442	    err = float(np.max(np.abs(A - B)) / denom)
   443	    require(err <= rtol, f"{label}: identity broken (rel {err:.2e} > {rtol:.0e})")
   444	    return err

   447	def edges_bin_volume_hash(edges):
   448	    """Hash the ordered 5-axis edge arrays + the C-order per-bin volume vector."""
   449	    import numpy as _np
   450	    parts = []
   451	    for e in edges:
   452	        a = _np.asarray(e, dtype=float); require(a.ndim == 1 and a.size >= 2, "bad edge array")
   453	        parts.append(a.tobytes())
   454	    edge_hash = hashlib.sha256(b"|".join(parts)).hexdigest()
   455	    widths = [(_np.asarray(e, float)[1:] - _np.asarray(e, float)[:-1]) for e in edges]
   456	    vol = widths[0]
   457	    for w in widths[1:]:
   458	        vol = _np.multiply.outer(vol, w).ravel()   # C-order product of bin widths
   459	    vol_hash = hashlib.sha256(vol.astype(float).tobytes() + b"|C").hexdigest()
   460	    return {"edge_hash": edge_hash, "bin_volume_hash": vol_hash, "n_bins": int(vol.size)}

   463	def validate_orchestrator_merged_receipt(recdir, live_stat):
   464	    """Consume the owner-neutral merged-hash receipt: require COMPLETE + the four
   465	    files, recompute live size/integer-mtime vs the inventory, and return the
   466	    committed hash-list digest bound into our manifest. live_stat: dict path->(size,mtime)."""
   467	    import os as _os
   468	    for f in ("COMPLETE", "summary.tsv", "validation.tsv", "standard.sha256", "standard.inventory.tsv"):
   469	        require(_os.path.exists(_os.path.join(recdir, f)), f"orchestrator receipt missing {f}")
   470	    sha_lines = [l for l in open(_os.path.join(recdir, "standard.sha256")).read().splitlines() if l.strip()]
   471	    require(len(sha_lines) == N_ENDPOINTS, f"receipt standard.sha256 has {len(sha_lines)} != 10 lines")
   472	    merged = {}
   473	    for l in sha_lines:
   474	        h, p = l.split(None, 1); merged[p.strip()] = h
   475	    # recompute live size + integer mtime against the committed inventory
   476	    inv = {}
   477	    for l in open(_os.path.join(recdir, "standard.inventory.tsv")).read().splitlines():
   478	        if not l.strip() or l.startswith("#"):
   479	            continue
   480	        cols = l.split("\t")
   481	        if len(cols) >= 3:                       # orchestrator format: size<TAB>mtime<TAB>path
   482	            inv[cols[2]] = (int(cols[0]), int(float(cols[1])))
   483	    for p, (sz, mt) in inv.items():
   484	        require(p in live_stat, f"inventory path not live: {p}")
   485	        lsz, lmt = live_stat[p]
   486	        require(lsz == sz and int(lmt) == mt, f"live size/mtime drift for {p}")
   487	    digest = hashlib.sha256("\n".join(sorted(f"{merged[p]}  {p}" for p in merged)).encode()).hexdigest()
   488	    return {"merged_sha256": merged, "hash_list_digest": digest, "n": len(merged)}

   493	# ROOT-key/dimension check. Receipt tag, ROOT sha, merged sha, central sha, config hash and

   499	# does NOT re-hash them; it compares the receipt's recorded merged sha against the
   500	# owner-neutral orchestrator receipt's committed hash, whose own live size+integer-mtime check
   501	# is what detects a changed input. Same reuse p4_evidence.py already relies on. The ROOT and

   540	def standard_p4_execution_surface(entrypoints=None, max_depth=6):
   541	    """Every tracked first-party module reachable from the chain's entrypoints, by IMPORT.
   542	
   543	    Derived, not curated: the previous surface was a filename-prefix glob and silently omitted
   544	    the modules that do the work. Falls back to the glob surface if git is unavailable, and the
   545	    caller must treat an empty result as a refusal rather than an empty scope."""
   546	    import ast
   547	    tracked = set()
   548	    try:
   549	        tracked = set(subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files"], cwd=REPO_ROOT,
   550	                                              text=True).splitlines())
   551	    except Exception:
   552	        return sorted(tracked_files_matching(STANDARD_P4_SURFACE_GLOBS))
   553	
   554	    def resolve(mod):
   555	        for d in _IMPORT_SEARCH_DIRS:
   556	            cand = f"{d}/{mod.replace('.', '/')}.py".lstrip("./")
   557	            if cand in tracked:
   558	                return cand
   559	        return None
   560	
   561	    seen, frontier = set(), list(entrypoints or STANDARD_P4_ENTRYPOINTS)
   562	    for _ in range(max_depth):
   563	        nxt = []
   564	        for rel in frontier:
   565	            if rel in seen or rel not in tracked:
   566	                continue
   567	            seen.add(rel)
   568	            try:
   569	                tree = ast.parse((REPO_ROOT_PATH / rel).read_text(errors="replace"))
   570	            except Exception:
   571	                continue
   572	            for node in ast.walk(tree):
   573	                names = []
   574	                if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
   575	                    names = [a.name for a in node.names]
   576	                elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module and node.level == 0:
   577	                    names = [node.module]
   578	                for n in names:
   579	                    r = resolve(n)
   580	                    if r and r not in seen:
   581	                        nxt.append(r)
   582	        if not nxt:
   583	            break
   584	        frontier = nxt
   585	    # the shell drivers are executed, not imported, so add them explicitly
   586	    seen.update(p for p in tracked if p.startswith("nd-unfolding/run_p4_") and p.endswith(".sh"))
   587	    return sorted(seen)
   588	
   589	
   590	def tracked_files_matching(globs, rev="HEAD"):
   591	    """Tracked paths at `rev` matching any glob. Sorted, so the result is order-stable."""
   592	    out = set()
   593	    for g in globs:
   594	        try:
   595	            r = subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", rev],
   596	                                        cwd=REPO_ROOT, text=True,
   597	                                        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).splitlines()
   598	        except Exception:
   599	            return []
   600	        import fnmatch
   601	        out.update(p for p in r if fnmatch.fnmatch(p, g))
   602	    return sorted(out)
   603	
   604	
   605	def paths_unchanged_between(rev_a, rev_b, paths):
   606	    """Every path in `paths` has the same blob at rev_a and rev_b.
   607	
   608	    Returns (ok, [differing paths]). Fails CLOSED: if git cannot answer for a path, that path
   609	    counts as differing, because an unverifiable claim is not a satisfied one."""
   610	    differing = []
   611	    for p in paths:
   612	        try:
   613	            a = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", f"{rev_a}:{p}"], cwd=REPO_ROOT,
   614	                                        text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
   615	        except Exception:
   616	            a = None
   617	        try:
   618	            b = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", f"{rev_b}:{p}"], cwd=REPO_ROOT,
   619	                                        text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
   620	        except Exception:
   621	            b = None
   622	        if a is None or b is None or a != b:
   623	            differing.append(p)
   624	    return (not differing), differing
   625	
   626	
   627	def code_rev_in_history(rev, head=None):
   628	    """True iff `rev` is reachable from HEAD in this repository (ancestor of, or equal to).
   629	
   630	    Deliberately reachability rather than equality -- see the note in validate_endpoint_receipt.
   631	    Fails CLOSED: if git cannot answer, the answer is False, because an unverifiable provenance
   632	    claim is not a satisfied one."""
   633	    if not isinstance(rev, str) or not rev.strip():
   634	        return False
   635	    try:
   636	        subprocess.check_call(["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", rev.strip(), head or "HEAD"],
   637	                              cwd=REPO_ROOT, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
   638	        return True
   639	    except Exception:
   640	        return False
   641	
   642	
   643	def validate_endpoint_receipt(rec, *, tag, root_sha256, merged_sha256,
   644	                              central5d_sha256, config_hash, bkg_mode,
   645	                              code_rev, unfold_blob):
   646	    """Fail closed unless the receipt is complete AND every recorded identity matches the
   647	    live/committed one. Returns True, or raises P4GateError naming the first mismatch.
   648	
   649	    REPAIR-5 (defect 2). The previous version required `code_rev` to be a NON-EMPTY STRING and
   650	    compared it to nothing, and the receipt recorded no source identity at all -- so an
   651	    endpoint produced under a changed unfold driver was still skipped. That is the third
   652	    instance in this chain of "assert presence, never compare": the first is the
   653	    `P4_VERIFIER_PASS` non-emptiness gate (KNOWN_ISSUES #21), the second is the `identities`
   654	    block whose members were literal `True`. Presence is not evidence; both `code_rev` and the
   655	    producing driver's committed blob are now COMPARED."""
   656	    require(isinstance(rec, dict) and rec, f"receipt for {tag} is not a JSON object")
   657	    missing = [k for k in RECEIPT_REQUIRED_KEYS if k not in rec]
   658	    require(not missing, f"receipt {tag} missing required keys {missing} (incomplete legacy format)")
   659	    require(rec["mode"] in RECEIPT_MODES, f"receipt {tag} unknown mode {rec['mode']!r}")
   660	    require(rec["tag"] == tag, f"receipt tag {rec['tag']!r} != {tag!r} (receipt/ROOT pair mismatch)")
   661	    require(rec["root_sha256"] == root_sha256,
   662	            f"receipt {tag} root_sha256 drift: recorded {rec['root_sha256']} vs live {root_sha256}")
   663	    require(rec["merged_sha256"] == merged_sha256,
   664	            f"receipt {tag} merged_sha256 drift vs the orchestrator receipt")
   665	    require(rec["central5d_sha256"] == central5d_sha256,
   666	            f"receipt {tag} central5d_sha256 drift (the central moved under this endpoint)")
   667	    require(rec["config_hash"] == config_hash,
   668	            f"receipt {tag} config_hash drift: produced under a different unfold configuration")
   669	    require(rec["bkg_mode"] == bkg_mode,
   670	            f"receipt {tag} bkg_mode {rec['bkg_mode']!r} != declared {bkg_mode!r}")
   671	    # D2: compared, not merely present.
   672	    require(isinstance(rec["code_rev"], str) and rec["code_rev"],
   673	            f"receipt {tag} has no code_rev")
   674	    require(isinstance(code_rev, str) and code_rev,
   675	            f"cannot validate receipt {tag}: no live code_rev to compare against")
   676	    # REPAIR-6b. This used to require code_rev == HEAD, and that was WRONG in the same way
   677	    # KNOWN_ISSUES #24 describes: it broke on correct behaviour. Any commit anywhere in the repo
   678	    # -- including another lane's, touching nothing this chain reads -- expired all ten receipts
   679	    # while the code that produced them was byte-identical. Caught by the self-check on the first
   680	    # production run: the PET lane advanced main by 8 commits mid-run, HEAD moved
   681	    # 42268b6 -> 203ff01, `git diff` on the unfold driver was EMPTY, and the gate rejected all ten.
   682	    #
   683	    # The producing-code binding is `unfold_blob`, which IS strictly compared below. `code_rev` is
   684	    # repository context, so the honest check is REACHABILITY, not equality: the receipt must come
   685	    # from this history. That still catches a receipt carried in from a foreign branch or a
   686	    # rewritten history, and does not expire on unrelated work.
   687	    require(code_rev_in_history(rec["code_rev"]),
   688	            f"receipt {tag} code_rev {rec['code_rev']} is not an ancestor of HEAD ({code_rev}): "
   689	            f"this receipt did not come from this repository's history")
   690	    require(isinstance(unfold_blob, str) and unfold_blob,
   691	            f"cannot validate receipt {tag}: no committed unfold-driver blob to compare against")
   692	    require(rec[RECEIPT_SOURCE_KEY] == unfold_blob,
   693	            f"receipt {tag} unfold_blob {rec[RECEIPT_SOURCE_KEY]} != committed {unfold_blob}: the "
   694	            f"unfold driver changed since this endpoint was produced")
   695	    return True
   696	
   697	
   698	def cmask_order_hash_4d(mask):
   699	    """4D reported-mask + C-order fingerprint (repair-4, defect 5c).
   700	
   701	    `mask_order_hash` fails closed on GRID_NBINS, which is the 5D grid, so the 4D mask had no
   702	    hash helper and the projector compared only the reported COUNT. A count is not an ordering:
   703	    a permuted 4D mask with the same population passed. Same construction as the 5D helper --
   704	    C-order indices of the selected bins -- so the two are comparable by eye in a manifest.
   705	    Deliberately NOT size-pinned: the 4D grid is a marginal of the 5D one and the standard lane
   706	    has no pinned canonical 4D target (see RUNBOOK-20260807 §7.4)."""
   707	    idx = np.nonzero(np.asarray(mask))[0].astype(np.int64)
   708	    require(idx.size > 0, "4D reported mask is empty")
   709	    return hashlib.sha256(idx.tobytes() + b"|C").hexdigest()
   710	
   711	
   712	def matrix_content_hash(M):
   713	    """Deterministic digest of a matrix's CONTENTS (repair-4, defect 5d).
   714	
   715	    The projection receipt recorded only `M_shape`, which two different projectors of the same
   716	    dimensions share. Hashes C-contiguous float64 bytes plus the shape, so a changed weight is
   717	    caught and a transposed/reshaped M cannot collide with the original."""
   718	    A = np.ascontiguousarray(np.asarray(M, dtype=np.float64))
   719	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   720	    h.update(repr(A.shape).encode()); h.update(b"|C|f8|"); h.update(A.tobytes())
   721	    return h.hexdigest()
   722

   724	def check_full_total_identity(Ccomb, Csyst, Cstat, Cml, rtol=1e-9):
   725	    """PROVE C_combined = C_syst + C_stat + C_ML by comparing the residual to the actual
   726	    stat and ML blocks. Returns the measured max-relative error.
   727	
   728	    REPAIR-5 (defect 4b / 6). Repair-4 checked only that `C_combined - C_syst` was symmetric
   729	    PSD and called that the full-total identity, in a gate name, a receipt field and a test
   730	    name. PSD is NECESSARY but nowhere near SUFFICIENT: every covariance-shaped residual passes
   731	    it, including one built from the wrong stat block, a doubled ML block, or a residual that
   732	    simply is not stat+ML at all. Naming a weak check after a strong claim is the same
   733	    "strong name over weak check" pattern as the test that passed because argparse rejected an
   734	    argument before the guard it named ever ran (verifier defect 6b). This compares."""
   735	    resid = np.asarray(Ccomb, float) - np.asarray(Csyst, float)
   736	    expect = np.asarray(Cstat, float) + np.asarray(Cml, float)
   737	    require(resid.shape == expect.shape,
   738	            f"full-total identity: residual {resid.shape} != stat+ML {expect.shape}")
   739	    # PSD of the residual is retained as a SEPARATE, weaker sanity check -- not as the identity.
   740	    check_symmetric_psd(resid)
   741	    return prove_identity(resid, expect, rtol, "C_combined - C_syst == C_stat + C_ML")
   742	
   743	
   744	def check_declared_migration_policy(policy, census_abs, band, nonzero_bands, zero_bands):
   745	    """Compare the DECLARED migration policy against the OBSERVED census.
   746	
   747	    REPAIR-5 (pattern sweep). `check_merged_metadata` required `migration_policy` to be
   748	    truthy and compared it to nothing -- a declared policy no consumer ever checked, which is
   749	    the same presence-not-comparison pattern as defect 2's `code_rev`. A merged file could
   750	    declare any policy string, or the wrong one, and pass."""
   751	    require(isinstance(policy, str) and policy.strip(), "declared migration policy missing")
   752	    require(band in nonzero_bands or band in zero_bands,
   753	            f"band {band} is in neither the nonzero- nor the zero-migration set")
   754	    n = int(census_abs)
   755	    if band in nonzero_bands:
   756	        require(n > 0, f"{band} declares selection-complete migration but census is {n}")
   757	        require("selection" in policy.lower(),
   758	                f"{band} migrates ({n}) but declares policy {policy!r}, which does not claim "
   759	                f"selection completeness")
   760	    else:
   761	        require(n == 0, f"{band} is declared bin-migration-only but census is {n}")
   762	        # REPAIR-6: the zero side never validated the policy TEXT, so a band could migrate zero
   763	        # events while declaring a selection-complete policy and pass.
   764	        require("selection" not in policy.lower() or "only" in policy.lower(),
   765	                f"{band} has zero selection migration but declares policy {policy!r}, which "
   766	                f"claims selection completeness")
   767	    return True

   770	def require_exact_endpoint_tags(tags):
   771	    """Reject BOTH missing and EXTRA tags. The old inventory only looked for the ten expected
   772	    names, so an eleventh product in the directory was invisible to it."""
   773	    got, want = set(tags), {f"{b}_{e}" for b in BANDS for e in ENDPOINTS}
   774	    require(not (want - got), f"missing endpoint tags: {sorted(want - got)}")
   775	    require(not (got - want), f"unexpected extra endpoint tags: {sorted(got - want)}")
   776	    return True

   779	def sha256_file(path, _bufsz=1 << 20):
   780	    """Durable file digest (login-computable; no ROOT)."""
   781	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   782	    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
   783	        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(_bufsz), b""):
   784	            h.update(chunk)
   785	    return h.hexdigest()

   788	def canonical_endpoints():
   789	    """The exact 10 (band, endpoint) logical tasks, in fixed order."""
   790	    return [(b, ep) for b in BANDS for ep in ENDPOINTS]

   793	def endpoint_manifest_hash(entries):
   794	    """entries: iterable of (band, endpoint, fingerprint). Hash is order-independent
   795	    over the SET but requires the exact 10-endpoint inventory (fail-closed)."""
   796	    seen = {}
   797	    for band, ep, fp in entries:
   798	        require(band in BANDS, f"unknown band {band!r}")
   799	        require(ep in ENDPOINTS, f"bad endpoint {ep!r}")
   800	        seen[(band, int(ep))] = str(fp)
   801	    require(len(seen) == N_ENDPOINTS,
   802	            f"expected exactly {N_ENDPOINTS} endpoints, got {len(seen)} "
   803	            f"(missing {sorted(set(canonical_endpoints())-set(seen))})")
   804	    blob = json.dumps({f"{b}_{e}": seen[(b, e)] for (b, e) in canonical_endpoints()},
   805	                      sort_keys=True)
   806	    return hashlib.sha256(blob.encode()).hexdigest()

   809	def mask_order_hash(mask):
   810	    """Hash of the reported-bin mask + C-order. mask: 1-D bool/int array over the
   811	    full grid. Pins which bins are reported and their order so a projection or a
   812	    component sum can never silently mix masks."""
   813	    m = np.asarray(mask)
   814	    require(m.ndim == 1, "mask must be 1-D (C-order ravel over the 5D grid)")
   815	    require(m.size == GRID_NBINS, f"mask size {m.size} != grid {GRID_NBINS}")
   816	    idx = np.nonzero(m.astype(bool))[0].astype(np.int64)
   817	    require(idx.size > 0, "mask selects zero reported bins")
   818	    return hashlib.sha256(idx.tobytes() + b"|C").hexdigest(), int(idx.size)

   822	def require_complete_unfold_set(present_tags):

   829	    require(present == need, f"unexpected unfold tags: {sorted(present - need)}")

   846	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- covariance gates
   847	def check_symmetric_psd(C, rtol_sym=1e-9, psd_atol_ratio=1e-12):
   848	    C = np.asarray(C, dtype=float)
   849	    require(C.ndim == 2 and C.shape[0] == C.shape[1], "covariance must be square 2-D")
   850	    require(np.all(np.isfinite(C)), "covariance has non-finite entries")
   851	    denom = max(1e-300, np.max(np.abs(C)))
   852	    asym = np.max(np.abs(C - C.T)) / denom
   853	    require(asym <= rtol_sym, f"covariance not symmetric (rel {asym:.2e})")
   854	    ev = np.linalg.eigvalsh(0.5 * (C + C.T))
   855	    require(ev[0] >= -psd_atol_ratio * abs(ev[-1]),
   856	            f"covariance not PSD (min/max eig {ev[0]/max(1e-300,abs(ev[-1])):.2e})")
   857	    d = np.diag(C)
   858	    # REPAIR-6, folding in BEN-044 from the PET lane ("an absolute tolerance inherited into a
   859	    # problem whose natural scale is ~1e-80 makes a gate that cannot fail"). This read
   860	    # `d >= -1e-30` ABSOLUTELY. The standard 5D covariance has sqrt(tr) ~ 5.3e-38 over 10694
   861	    # reported bins, so a typical diagonal entry is ~1e-79 -- the old bound sat ~49 orders of
   862	    # magnitude above what it was supposed to bound, and a diagonal of -1e-31 (a corruption
   863	    # ~48 orders larger than the signal) passed it. Now relative to the matrix's own scale.
   864	    # Power-proved in tests/test_p4_guard_mutations.py at the real 1e-79 scale, per BEN-044's
   865	    # rule that a gate must be shown able to fail in the commit that writes it.
   866	    require(np.all(np.isfinite(d)), "non-finite diagonal")
   867	    require(np.all(d >= -psd_atol_ratio * denom),
   868	            f"negative diagonal beyond tolerance (min {np.min(d):.3e} vs "
   869	            f"-{psd_atol_ratio:.0e} * max|C| = {-psd_atol_ratio * denom:.3e})")
   870	    return {"rel_asymmetry": float(asym), "min_eig": float(ev[0]), "max_eig": float(ev[-1]),
   871	            "diag_tol_absolute": float(psd_atol_ratio * denom)}
   872	
   873	
   874	def require_exact_bands(band_covs):
   875	    """band_covs: dict band -> cov. Must be EXACTLY the 5 kinematic bands."""
   876	    got = set(band_covs)
   877	    require(got == set(BANDS),
   878	            f"active-lateral bands mismatch: got {sorted(got)}, need {sorted(BANDS)}")
   879	    return True

   882	def component_traces_positive_finite(band_covs):
   883	    tr = {}
   884	    for b in BANDS:
   885	        require(b in band_covs, f"missing component band {b}")
   886	        C = np.asarray(band_covs[b], dtype=float)
   887	        require(np.all(np.isfinite(C)), f"component {b} has non-finite entries")
   888	        t = float(np.trace(C))
   889	        require(np.isfinite(t) and t > 0.0, f"component {b} trace not positive-finite ({t})")
   890	        tr[b] = t
   891	    return tr
   892	
   893	
   894	def check_component_sum(total, band_covs, rtol=1e-9):
   895	    """total must equal the EXACT sum of the 5 per-band component covariances."""
   896	    require_exact_bands(band_covs)
   897	    total = np.asarray(total, dtype=float)
   898	    s = np.zeros_like(total)
   899	    for b in BANDS:
   900	        Cb = np.asarray(band_covs[b], dtype=float)
   901	        require(Cb.shape == total.shape, f"component {b} shape {Cb.shape} != total {total.shape}")
   902	        s = s + Cb
   903	    denom = max(1e-300, np.max(np.abs(total)))
   904	    err = np.max(np.abs(total - s)) / denom
   905	    require(err <= rtol, f"component sum mismatch (rel {err:.2e}) — total != sum of bands")
   906	    return float(err)
   907	
   908	
   909	def check_support_comparison(active_cov, support_cov):
   910	    """Complete support comparison: both present, same shape/mask/order. Returns
   911	    sqrt-trace ratio (active/support). Fail-closed if the support block is absent."""
   912	    require(active_cov is not None, "active lateral block missing")
   913	    require(support_cov is not None, "support-limited comparison block missing")
   914	    A = np.asarray(active_cov, dtype=float); S = np.asarray(support_cov, dtype=float)
   915	    require(A.shape == S.shape, f"active/support shape mismatch {A.shape} vs {S.shape}")
   916	    sta = float(np.sqrt(max(0.0, np.trace(A)))); sts = float(np.sqrt(max(0.0, np.trace(S))))
   917	    require(sts > 0, "support block has zero trace")
   918	    return {"sqrt_tr_active": sta, "sqrt_tr_support": sts, "ratio": sta / sts}
   919

   921	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- deterministic projection map
   922	def build_projection_M(edges, drop_axis, mask_high, mask_low):
   923	    """Deterministic 5D->4D map by WIDTH-WEIGHTED marginalization of one axis.
   924	    edges: ordered per-axis edge arrays (pt,pz,eavail,q3,W). drop_axis: axis index to
   925	    marginalize (W=4). mask_high/mask_low: reported-bin bool masks over the full high/low
   926	    grids (C-order). Returns dense M (n_low_reported x n_high_reported) with
   927	    M[a,b] = width_drop[k] when high bin b decomposes to low bin a + dropped index k.
   928	    density convention: x_low = M @ x_high, C_low = M C_high M^T."""
   929	    nb = [np.asarray(e).size - 1 for e in edges]
   930	    require(len(nb) == 5, "expected 5 axes")
   931	    total_high = int(np.prod(nb))
   932	    require(int(np.asarray(mask_high).size) == total_high, "mask_high size != high grid")
   933	    wdrop = np.asarray(edges[drop_axis], float)[1:] - np.asarray(edges[drop_axis], float)[:-1]
   934	    nb_low = [n for i, n in enumerate(nb) if i != drop_axis]
   935	    total_low = int(np.prod(nb_low))
   936	    require(int(np.asarray(mask_low).size) == total_low, "mask_low size != low grid")
   937	    strides_h = np.array([int(np.prod(nb[i + 1:])) for i in range(5)])          # C-order strides
   938	    strides_l = np.array([int(np.prod(nb_low[i + 1:])) for i in range(4)])
   939	    mh = np.nonzero(np.asarray(mask_high).astype(bool))[0]
   940	    ml = np.nonzero(np.asarray(mask_low).astype(bool))[0]
   941	    low_pos = {int(g): r for r, g in enumerate(ml)}                              # low global -> reported row
   942	    M = np.zeros((ml.size, mh.size), dtype=float)
   943	    for col, g in enumerate(mh):
   944	        midx = [(g // strides_h[i]) % nb[i] for i in range(5)]                   # 5D multi-index
   945	        k = midx[drop_axis]
   946	        low_multi = [midx[i] for i in range(5) if i != drop_axis]
   947	        glow = int(np.dot(low_multi, strides_l))
   948	        row = low_pos.get(glow)
   949	        require(row is not None, f"high reported bin {g} maps to non-reported low bin {glow}")
   950	        M[row, col] = wdrop[k]
   951	    # BOTH DIRECTIONS (2026-08-09, BEN-064). The loop above validates coverage one way only --
   952	    # every reported HIGH bin lands in a reported LOW bin -- and says nothing about reported LOW
   953	    # bins that no HIGH bin reaches. Those rows of M are all-zero, so they survive to the central
   954	    # check as an exact 0 against a nonzero frozen value, i.e. `rel = 1.0` exactly.
   955	    #
   956	    # That is not merely a missed case, it is a MASKING defect: on the real products 5 orphan bins
   957	    # carrying 0.0000% of the 4D total produced `projection mutates central (max rel 1.00e+00)`,
   958	    # and that message hid the actual result (62% of bins over tolerance at a median of 4.4%)
   959	    # behind a number contributed by bins nobody would care about. An error that is loudest about
   960	    # the least important thing is worse than no error, because it redirects the investigation.
   961	    #
   962	    # Fail here, at construction, where the diagnosis is the orphan list itself.
   963	    empty = np.nonzero(~M.any(axis=1))[0]
   964	    require(empty.size == 0,
   965	            f"{empty.size} reported LOW bin(s) receive no contribution from any reported HIGH bin "
   966	            f"(global indices {[int(ml[r]) for r in empty[:10]]}"
   967	            f"{' ...' if empty.size > 10 else ''}); the two reported supports are inconsistent. "
   968	            f"These rows would be all-zero and would reach a central comparison as exact zeros, "
   969	            f"reporting a relative error of 1.0 regardless of how small the bins are.")
   970	    return M
   971	
   972	
   973	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- projection gates
   974	def project(C_high, M):
   975	    """5D->4D (or any) projection C_low = M C_high M^T (preserves density/order)."""
   976	    C_high = np.asarray(C_high, dtype=float); M = np.asarray(M, dtype=float)
   977	    require(M.shape[1] == C_high.shape[0], f"M cols {M.shape[1]} != C dim {C_high.shape[0]}")
   978	    return M @ C_high @ M.T
   979	
   980	
   981	# RE-SPECIFIED 2026-08-09 (Joseph). The previous form GATED on `max |M@x5 - x4| / |x4| <= 3%`,
   982	# i.e. it required the 5D->4D marginal to reproduce the INDEPENDENTLY-UNFOLDED 4D central bin by
   983	# bin. That is the equivalence convention the campaign DECLINED on 2026-08-07: the adopted
   984	# position is that 4D IS the marginal and the independent 4D unfold is a CROSS-CHECK. The gate
   985	# therefore tested a proposition the analysis does not assert.
   986	#
   987	# THIS IS A GATE REMOVAL, NOT A TOLERANCE WIDENING, and the distinction is the whole point. The
   988	# measurement stays exactly as it was and is reported in full; what is withdrawn is the pass/fail
   989	# verdict attached to it. Nothing here makes a failing number pass -- see the measured values in
   990	# FINDING-20260809-stage6-central-gate-cannot-pass.md, which are unchanged by this edit.
   991	#
   992	# What IS gated is projection validity, which the analysis does assert: symmetry, PSD, exact
   993	# agreement of M C M^T against a direct block-sum recomputation, and shape/coverage. Those are
   994	# recomputation identities and hold at ~1e-14, the standard the stage-4 identities already meet.
   995	def check_projection_validity(C_high, M, rtol_identity=1e-9):
   996	    """GATE: the projection itself is valid. Recomputation identities only -- nothing here
   997	    compares against an independently-produced product.
   998	
   999	      * C_low = M C_high M^T is symmetric and PSD;
  1000	      * that product equals a direct block-sum recomputation to `rtol_identity`.
  1001	
  1002	    The second is not redundant with the first: `project()` is one matrix expression and a bug in
  1003	    it would produce a matrix that is still symmetric and still PSD. Recomputing the same quantity
  1004	    by an independent route is what makes this a check rather than a restatement."""
  1005	    C_low = project(C_high, M)
  1006	    stats = check_symmetric_psd(C_low)
  1007	    # independent route: accumulate row-block by row-block rather than as one M C M^T
  1008	    direct = np.zeros_like(C_low)
  1009	    MH = M @ np.asarray(C_high, dtype=float)
  1010	    for i in range(C_low.shape[0]):
  1011	        direct[i, :] = MH[i, :] @ M.T
  1012	    scale = max(1e-300, float(np.max(np.abs(C_low))))
  1013	    err = float(np.max(np.abs(C_low - direct)) / scale)
  1014	    require(err <= rtol_identity,
  1015	            f"projection identity M C M^T != direct block sum (rel {err:.3e} > {rtol_identity:.0e})")
  1016	    stats["projection_identity_relerr"] = err
  1017	    return C_low, stats
  1018	
  1019	
  1020	def crosscheck_marginal_vs_independent(M, x_high, x_low_independent):
  1021	    """REPORT ONLY -- no pass/fail, by specification. Compares the 5D->4D marginal against the
  1022	    independently-unfolded lower-dimensional central.
  1023	
  1024	    This is a cross-check between two DIFFERENT estimators, not a consistency requirement. Under
  1025	    the adopted convention the marginal is the deliverable and this comparison characterises the
  1026	    independent unfold; it does not constrain the marginal. Returns the full distribution rather
  1027	    than a max, because on the real products the max is owned by a handful of near-empty bins and
  1028	    is actively misleading about the body of the comparison (BEN-064)."""
  1029	    proj = M @ np.asarray(x_high, dtype=float)
  1030	    xind = np.asarray(x_low_independent, dtype=float)
  1031	    require(proj.shape == xind.shape,
  1032	            f"cross-check shape {proj.shape} != independent {xind.shape}")
  1033	    denom = np.where(np.abs(xind) > 0, np.abs(xind), 1.0)
  1034	    rel = (proj - xind) / denom
  1035	    a = np.abs(rel)
  1036	    out = {"n_bins": int(a.size),
  1037	           "median_abs_rel": float(np.median(a)),
  1038	           "p90_abs_rel": float(np.percentile(a, 90)),
  1039	           "p99_abs_rel": float(np.percentile(a, 99)),
  1040	           "max_abs_rel": float(a.max()),
  1041	           "frac_marginal_above": float(np.mean(rel > 0)),
  1042	           "signed_mean_rel": float(np.mean(rel)),
  1043	           "integral_ratio": float(proj.sum() / xind.sum()) if xind.sum() else float("nan"),
  1044	           "note": "cross-check between two estimators; NO pass/fail by specification "
  1045	                   "(2026-08-09). The marginal is the deliverable."}
  1046	    for t in (0.03, 0.10, 0.20):
  1047	        out[f"n_over_{int(t*100)}pct"] = int((a > t).sum())
  1048	    return out

   286	# branch (:883) prints nothing about mode and instead calls build_measured_training_nd,
