   113	    sys.exit(main())
     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Mechanical sweep of the standard P4 lane (repair-6 item 2).
     3	
     4	Two enumerations, grep-level, no judgement in the extraction step:
     5	  A. every field WRITTEN into a manifest/receipt, and whether its name ever appears
     6	     in a comparison context anywhere in the lane;
     7	  B. every named PASS-gate label, and what the gate's body actually does.
     8	
     9	The point is that the list exists as a checkable artifact. Last round's sweep was a pass I
    10	performed and it missed an item on its own list.
    11	"""
    12	import json, re, subprocess, sys
    13	from pathlib import Path
    14	
    15	ND = Path(__file__).resolve().parent   # re-runnable from any checkout
    16	MODULES = ["p4_lib.py", "p4_evidence.py", "p4_validate_active_lateral.py",
    17	           "p4_build_components.py", "p4_project_4d.py", "p4_adopt_standard.py",
    18	           "p4_check_receipt.py", "p4_lateral_replace.py"]
    19	SHELL = ["run_p4_standard.sh", "run_p4_unfold_std.sh", "run_p4_merge_audit_std.sh"]
    20	
    21	src = {m: (ND / m).read_text() for m in MODULES if (ND / m).exists()}
    22	sh = {s: (ND / s).read_text() for s in SHELL if (ND / s).exists()}
    23	allsrc = "\n".join(src.values()) + "\n" + "\n".join(sh.values())
    24	
    25	# ---------- A. fields written into products ----------
    26	written = {}          # field -> set(files that write it)
    27	# python:  man["x"] = ... / out["x"] = ... / rec["x"] = ... / prov["x"] = ... / "x": value
    28	for f, s in src.items():
    29	    for m in re.finditer(r'\b(?:man|out|rec|prov|foot|ids)\["([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)"\]\s*=', s):
    30	        written.setdefault(m.group(1), set()).add(f)
    31	    # dict literals assigned into those products
    32	    for m in re.finditer(r'"([A-Za-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{2,})"\s*:', s):
    33	        written.setdefault(m.group(1), set()).add(f)
    34	# shell: printf JSON keys
    35	for f, s in sh.items():
    36	    for m in re.finditer(r'"([a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{2,})":"', s):
    37	        written.setdefault(m.group(1), set()).add(f)
    38	
    39	# ---------- is the field ever COMPARED? ----------
    40	# a comparison = the name appears adjacent to ==, !=, <=, >=, or inside require/need with a
    41	# second operand; presence-only = only `in`, `is not None`, or bare truthiness.
    42	def classify(field):
    43	    compared, presence = [], []
    44	    for f, s in {**src, **sh}.items():
    45	        for line in s.splitlines():
    46	            if field not in line:
    47	                continue
    48	            if line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
    49	                continue
    50	            has_cmp = bool(re.search(r'(==|!=|<=|>=|<|>)', line))
    51	            pres_only = bool(re.search(
    52	                rf'(is not None|is None|"{field}" (?:not )?in |\.get\("{field}"\)\s*[,)])', line))
    53	            if has_cmp:
    54	                compared.append((f, line.strip()[:110]))
    55	            elif pres_only:
    56	                presence.append((f, line.strip()[:110]))
    57	    return compared, presence
    58	
    59	IGNORE = {"note", "reason", "title", "help", "type", "default", "action", "required",
    60	          "gates", "result", "endpoints", "merged", "census", "identities", "config",
    61	          "footing", "tree_entries", "band_meta", "sha256"}
    62	
    63	rows = []
    64	for field in sorted(written):
    65	    if field in IGNORE or len(field) < 4:
    66	        continue
    67	    comp, pres = classify(field)
    68	    if comp:
    69	        continue                      # compared somewhere -> not an instance
    70	    rows.append((field, sorted(written[field]), pres[:2]))
    71	
    72	# ---------- B. named PASS-gate labels ----------
    73	gates = []
    74	for f, s in src.items():
    75	    for m in re.finditer(r'gates"\]\.append\("([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)"\)', s):
    76	        gates.append((m.group(1), f))
    77	    for m in re.finditer(r'^def (check_[a-z0-9_]+|require_[a-z0-9_]+|prove_[a-z0-9_]+)',
    78	                         s, re.M):
    79	        gates.append((m.group(1) + "()", f))
    80	
    81	def summary():
    82	    """Machine-readable snapshot -- see the note in tools_p4_sweep_pipeline_rc.summary()."""
    83	    return {"tool": "tools_p4_sweep_recorded_fields",
    84	            "n_fields": len(rows),
    85	            "n_gates": len(set(gates)),
    86	            "fields": sorted(f for f, _, _ in rows),
    87	            "gates": sorted(n for n, _ in set(gates))}
    88	
    89	
    90	if __name__ != "__main__":
    91	    # importable for the CI guard without printing the whole report
    92	    pass
    93	
    94	print("=" * 78)
    95	print("A. FIELDS WRITTEN INTO A PRODUCT AND NEVER COMPARED ANYWHERE")
    96	print("=" * 78)
    97	print("""
    98	  READING RULE (2026-08-09). This list is a list of SHAPES, not of defects; polarity decides.
    99	  A recorded boolean read only for truthiness is a defect when its truthy value means "this
   100	  was verified" -- the producer writes a literal, the consumer reads a constant, and the gate
   101	  is fail-OPEN. That was `identities.pure_addition`. The same shape is HARMLESS, and in fact
   102	  correct, when the truthy value means "refuse this" -- a literal that can only ever cause a
   103	  refusal is fail-CLOSED, and the failure mode to guard is the field going ABSENT, which a
   104	  comparison against it could not catch either. That is `publication_gate_rejects_this`; its
   105	  guard is the both-directions test in tests/test_p4_repair.py, not an operator on this line.
   106	  Fields ending in _reason / _requires are prose carried for a human reader and gate nothing.
   107	""")
   108	for field, files, pres in rows:
   109	    print(f"\n  {field}")
   110	    print(f"    written by : {', '.join(files)}")
   111	    if pres:
   112	        for f, l in pres:
   113	            print(f"    presence   : {f}: {l}")
   114	    else:
   115	        print("    presence   : (recorded only; no check of any kind)")
   116	print(f"\n  TOTAL: {len(rows)} fields")
   117	
   118	print()
   119	print("=" * 78)
   120	print("B. NAMED GATES / PASS LABELS")
   121	print("=" * 78)
   122	for name, f in sorted(set(gates)):
   123	    print(f"  {name:52s} {f}")
   124	print(f"\n  TOTAL: {len(set(gates))} named gates")

     1	# Standard P4 lane — mechanical inventory of recorded-but-unchecked fields and named gates
     2	
     3	**Why this file exists.** "Records a value, never checks it" and "names a weak check strongly"
     4	have now appeared five times in this chain: `P4_VERIFIER_PASS` (#21), `code_rev`,
     5	`C_syst_eq_retained_plus_active_relerr`, `complete_support_comparison`, and the
     6	full-total-identity overclaim. Repair-5's sweep was **a pass I performed**, and it missed an
     7	item on its own list. So the list is now an artifact produced by a script, checked in, and
     8	re-runnable — not a judgement I assert I made.
     9	
    10	**Generator:** the sweep is grep-level over `p4_lib.py`, `p4_evidence.py`,
    11	`p4_validate_active_lateral.py`, `p4_build_components.py`, `p4_project_4d.py`,
    12	`p4_adopt_standard.py`, `p4_check_receipt.py`, `p4_lateral_replace.py` and the three shell
    13	drivers. **99 fields** written into a product with no same-line comparison, and **25 named
    14	gates**.
    15	
    16	> **These counts are now GUARDED, not typed** (repair-7 item 4). The document previously said
    17	> 66 fields / 22 gates while its own generator reported 82 / 24, and the pipeline section said
    18	> 22/324 while the tool said 23/326 — the artifact drifted from its generator *inside the round
    19	> that created it*, and the verifier found it rather than the author. Both sweeps now emit a
    20	> machine-readable `summary()`, the result is committed at
    21	> `state/p4-sweep-snapshots.json`, and `tests/test_p4_sweep_snapshots.py` regenerates and
    22	> compares. **Staleness is now a red test on the author's machine instead of a finding on
    23	> someone else's.** The snapshot also names any NEW unchecked field rather than only counting
    24	> them, because counts alone let one appear as another disappears. Update with
    25	> `python3 tests/test_p4_sweep_snapshots.py --update` and commit the diff, so a number change
    26	> lands in review where it can be seen.
    27	>
    28	> **REPAIR-7 ITEM 4 STATUS, checked 2026-08-09 and PARTLY DEFERRED with a reason.** The item was
    29	> "generate the inventory in CI". **This repository has no CI**: no `.github/workflows`, no
    30	> `.gitlab-ci.yml`, no pre-commit config, no Makefile target — verified by `git ls-files`. So the
    31	> literal form is not deferred by choice, it is unimplementable without first standing up CI, which
    32	> is out of scope for this lane and would be a repo-wide decision.
    33	>
    34	> **What IS implemented is the property the item wanted:** the sweeps emit `summary()`, the result
    35	> is committed at `state/p4-sweep-snapshots.json`, and `tests/test_p4_sweep_snapshots.py`
    36	> regenerates and compares on every suite run — so staleness is a red test rather than a silent
    37	> drift, which is the whole point. It has already caught two real drifts it was not written for: my
    38	> own new fields, and a change made by the PET lane entirely (two new shell files moving the
    39	> pipeline corpus 330 → 332).
    40	>
    41	> **What is genuinely deferred:** enforcement for someone who never runs the suite. Today the guard
    42	> binds an author who runs `pytest`; it does not bind a commit. If CI is ever added, the named fix
    43	> is one job invoking `pytest nd-unfolding/tests/test_p4_sweep_snapshots.py`. Recorded here rather
    44	> than closed silently, because "done" and "done in the only form the repo supports" are different
    45	> claims and the second is the true one.
    46	>
    47	> Current snapshot: **99 fields / 25 gates**; pipeline **23 candidates across 332 shell
    48	> files, 0 live**.
    49	
    50	### Reading rule: this is a list of SHAPES, and polarity decides (2026-08-09)
    51	
    52	Adding the self-declaring rejection marker put three fields on list A
    53	(`publication_gate_rejects_this`, `non_adoptable_reason`, `adoption_requires`) and that is the
    54	right outcome — the sweep should flag them — but only one of the three is even a gate, and it is
    55	not a defect. The distinction the list cannot draw for you:
    56	
    57	- A recorded boolean read only for truthiness is a **defect** when its truthy value means *this
    58	  was verified*. The producer writes a literal, the consumer reads a constant, the gate is
    59	  **fail-open**. That was `identities.pure_addition`, and it was the strictest gate in the chain.
    60	- The same shape is **correct** when the truthy value means *refuse this*. A literal that can
    61	  only ever cause a refusal is **fail-closed**. That is `publication_gate_rejects_this`. The
    62	  failure mode worth guarding is not a wrong value but the key going **absent** — which no
    63	  comparison operator on that line would catch either. Its guard is therefore a both-directions
    64	  test (`tests/test_p4_repair.py::NonAdoptableMarker`), which demonstrates that a marked manifest
    65	  is refused *and* that an unmarked one is not refused on that ground.
    66	- Fields ending `_reason` / `_requires` are prose carried for a human reader and gate nothing.
    67	- **A third category, added the same day:** `diagnose_integral_breach` returns
    68	  `n_deviating_bins`, `frac_positive`, `sigma_from_roundoff_bias`, `sigma_from_half` and
    69	  `corr_reldev_vs_central`, and checks none of them — **on purpose**, because the criterion that
    70	  consumes them is pre-specified in prose at `p4_lib.REPRO_RTOL_INTEGRAL` and applied by a human
    71	  in front of a red gate. A measurement produced for a stated decision rule is not an unchecked
    72	  field; it is the input to a check that deliberately does not live in the same function, so that
    73	  the number cannot be re-interpreted by whoever is looking at it. What makes that defensible
    74	  rather than an excuse is that the rule was written *before* any breach and that both of its
    75	  branches are demonstrated against synthetic round-off and a synthetic coherent shift
    76	  (`tests/test_p4_repair.py::IntegralLegIsADiscriminator`). Absent that test it would be exactly
    77	  the pattern this inventory exists to catch.
    78	- **The same category again, 2026-08-09:** `crosscheck_marginal_vs_independent` returns
    79	  `median_abs_rel`, `p90_abs_rel`, `p99_abs_rel`, `max_abs_rel`, `frac_marginal_above`,
    80	  `signed_mean_rel`, `integral_ratio` and `n_over_*pct`, and checks **none** of them. That is the
    81	  specification: Joseph removed the pass/fail on this comparison on 2026-08-09 because it tested a
    82	  proposition the analysis does not assert. The fields are a reported distribution, not a gate, and
    83	  the function's docstring says so. Distinguishing this from a Pattern-A defect is exactly the
    84	  judgement this inventory is for: *a recorded-and-unchecked field is a defect when something was
    85	  supposed to check it.* Here nothing was, deliberately, and the removal is documented at the call
    86	  site in `p4_project_4d.py`.
    87	
    88	That test earned its place immediately: it found that `require_adoptable` sat *after* the
    89	input-identity loop in `p4_adopt_standard.py`, so a marked manifest missing any other key died on
    90	a `KeyError` and the refusal never surfaced. The check now runs before the other gates, which is
    91	what its comment had claimed all along.
    92	
    93	## The sweep's own two failure modes, stated up front
    94	
    95	Both were found by running it, and both matter for reading the table:
    96	
    97	1. **It missed uppercase-initial keys on the first run** — the key-literal regex was
    98	   `"([a-z]...)"`, so `C_syst_eq_retained_plus_active_relerr`, `C_combined_eq_syst_stat_ml_relerr`,
    99	   `M_content_sha256` and `M_shape` were invisible. That is *the exact field the verifier caught
   100	   repair-5 missing*, missed a second time by the tool built to stop missing it. Fixed to
   101	   `[A-Za-z]`; the count went 62 → 66. **A mechanical sweep is only as good as its pattern, and
   102	   the pattern needs its own test.**
   103	2. **It is line-based, so it cannot see a check performed in a loop.** Where a consumer does
   104	   `for k in (...): require(ids[k] <= rtol)`, the field name appears only in the tuple and the
   105	   comparison only in the body. Those show as `SWEEP-FP` below and were hand-verified.
   106

   157	## E. The 22 named gates

   159	Twelve are library functions whose names match their bodies (`check_symmetric_psd`,
   160	`prove_identity`, `check_component_sum`, `require_exact_bands`, `require_exact_endpoint_tags`,
   161	`require_complete_unfold_set`, `require_standard_footing`, `require_candidate_path`,
   162	`check_projection_nonmutation`, `check_full_total_identity`, `check_declared_migration_policy`,
   163	`check_merged_metadata`).
   164	
   165	Ten are PASS labels recorded in the validator receipt. Nine are accurate. **One is not:**
   166	`complete_support_comparison` — see section A. `full_total_identity_recomputed` is accurate as
   167	of repair-5 and was **not** before, which is why the label is in this inventory rather than
   168	assumed correct.
   169	
   170	---
   171	
   172	## E-bis. A THIRD pattern, found while fixing the first two: **a gate nothing calls**
   173	
   174	`p4_lib.check_merged_metadata` is a complete, well-tested fail-closed gate — tree completeness,
   175	POT positivity, census counters, native-miss metadata, migration policy — and a repo-wide grep
   176	for callers returns **only its own tests**. `p4_evidence.py` re-implements the same checks
   177	inline with `need()` instead of invoking it.
   178	
   179	So it has been exercised solely by fixtures since it was written. Everything repair-5 and
   180	repair-6 "fixed" in it — the migration-policy comparison, the native-miss comparison — improved
   181	a function **that does not run in production**. That is worth stating plainly rather than
   182	letting the round's diff imply a live repair.
   183	
   184	This is a distinct failure mode from the other two and belongs on the shared list:
   185	
   186	- Pattern A: *records a value, never checks it.*
   187	- Pattern B: *names a weak check strongly.*
   188	- **Pattern C: a gate that is never invoked.** Coverage looks green, the code reads as
   189	  defence-in-depth, and it protects nothing. It is the natural end state of maintaining a
   190	  library gate and an inline copy side by side — the inline copy is what runs, the library copy
   191	  is what gets improved.
   192	
   193	**On BEN-046 vs the code (raised in A+, and correct):** `run_p4_standard.sh:41` still contains
   194	`if [[ -z "${P4_VERIFIER_PASS}" ]]`. BEN-046 is about the *runbook's state table omitting a
   195	standing BLOCK*, not about that gate, and A1 is deliberately OPEN because the token gate is
   196	Joseph's human checkpoint — changing it mid-round would alter the instrument being used to
   197	authorise the round. `329d230` was a renumber and touched only prose. **Neither the ledger row
   198	nor the renumber should be read as a repair of #21.**
   199	
   200	**Marked FIX, but deliberately NOT in this round:** collapsing the duplication means changing
   201	`p4_evidence.py`'s accumulate-`need()` semantics into `require()`-raises, which changes when the
   202	evidence stage stops and what it reports on a bad input. That is a behavioural change worth its
   203	own commit and its own verifier pass, not a rider on this one. A detection test would be: assert
   204	every `check_*`/`require_*` in `p4_lib` has at least one non-test caller.
   205	
   206	## A++. QUEUED — BEN-070 second site, `p4_validate_active_lateral_fps.py:70`
   207	
   208	**Found by the PET lane, verified by Joseph, assigned to this lane, and deliberately NOT started
   209	yet** — it is queued behind the receipts/verifier chain so a shared-library edit cannot collide
   210	with a run in flight.
   211	
   212	- **Defect:** line 70 bounds the diagonal with an absolute `-1e-30` while lines **66/67/68 of
   213	  the same function** are all relative. Same shape as the `p4_lib.py` instance repair-6 fixed.
   214	- **Severity, measured by Joseph, not assumed:** the PSD check at line 68 has an effective
   215	  threshold of ~`1e-89` at this product's scale, against line 70's `1e-30` — it **subsumes the
   216	  diagonal check by ~59 orders**. **Latent, not exploitable. The adopted FPS lateral is fine.**
   217	  This is the same "redundant behind a live relative check" conclusion the `p4_lib` instance
   218	  reached, now independently confirmed on the FPS product.
   219	- **Why my sweep missed it:** the file's git history is the FPS repair rounds, not this lane's,
   220	  so it fell outside the module list the sweep enumerates. **The sweep's scope was drawn by
   221	  provenance rather than by prefix** — a `p4_`-prefixed file that this lane owns was not in a
   222	  list this lane generated. Third failure mode of the sweep, after lowercase-only keys and
   223	  line-based blindness to loops.
   224	- **When and how:** after the verifier pass, and **with a mutation test**, not as a bare
   225	  one-liner — the guard has to be shown to reject what the absolute bound accepts, at the real
   226	  ~1e-86 scale, the same way `BEN044_AbsoluteToleranceAtRealScale` does.
   227	
   228	### The heuristic this third occurrence earns
   229	
   230	Three instances now of **a guard written in different units from its immediate neighbours**:
   231	`p4_lib.check_symmetric_psd` (symmetry and PSD relative, diagonal absolute), this FPS twin
   232	(66/67/68 relative, 70 absolute), and BEN-044's origin (`combine_cstat_bkgsub_100rep.py`, where
   233	`max(max_eig, 1.0)` pinned a relative tolerance to an absolute floor).
   234	
   235	**Adopt the PET lane's detector: read a validator's checks AGAINST EACH OTHER, not just against
   236	the data.** A single absolute threshold is ambiguous — it might be right for its quantity. A
   237	threshold that is absolute while its *siblings in the same function* are relative is a defect on
   238	sight, because the author demonstrably knew the relative idiom and did not apply it there. This
   239	is cheaper and more reliable than reasoning about scale from first principles, and it is
   240	mechanically checkable: flag any `require`/`need` in a function where some thresholds are
   241	normalised and at least one is not.
   242	
   243	**Note it also predicts severity, which is why all three came out "latent".** If the relative
   244	siblings are the *stronger* check, the absolute one is redundant and the finding is hygiene; if
   245	the absolute one is the only check of its kind in the function, it is live. Ask which before
   246	writing the severity down — twice now the first draft overstated it.
   247	
   248	## E-ter. Third mechanical sweep: BEN-035's pipeline exit-status trap
   249	
   250	Generator: `nd-unfolding/tools_p4_sweep_pipeline_rc.py`, over **330 tracked shell files**. Flags
   251	three shapes -- a pipeline through `tail/head/grep/...` used as an `if` condition, the same in a
   252	`&&`/`||` chain, and one followed by `rc=$?`.
   253	
   254	**Result: 23 candidate instances, and every single one is in a file that sets `set -o pipefail`.**
   255	Under pipefail the first failing element propagates, so the shape is benign there. **There are no
   256	live instances in the tracked shell corpus.**
   257	
   258	**Which relocates the finding, and is the useful part.** The trap has now bitten five times, and
   259	the most recent -- `selfcheck_receipts.sh` reporting `pass=10 fail=0` beside ten REJECT lines --
   260	was in an **ad-hoc script that was never committed and had no `pipefail`**. All three tracked P4
   261	drivers set it; my throwaway helper did not. So the danger zone is not the reviewed corpus, it is
   262	the scripts nobody commits and nobody sweeps.
   263	
   264	**Rule this earns:** *every* shell script sets `set -o pipefail`, including one-off helpers and
   265	anything written into a scratch directory. A sweep over tracked files cannot see the place this
   266	defect actually lives, which is the same blind spot as A++ (a `p4_`-prefixed file absent from a
   267	list drawn by provenance) -- **twice now a mechanical sweep has been correct about what it looked
   268	at and wrong about what it looked at.**

+## 2026-08-09 — TEST COUNTS BEFORE 2026-08-09 ARE OVERSTATED FOR BOTH LANES. Read this before comparing any two.

+`tests/test_p3f_pet_fullevent_launcher.py` executed `TEXT = open(LAUNCHER).read()` at MODULE

+2026-08-09 by excluding the module at collection level from `tests/conftest.py`.

+**The fix did not only restore hygiene. It UNMASKED 7 real, pre-existing failures**, all
+environment-dependent PET-lane tests (`test_fullevent_gate2.py` ×6 — `/pscratch` paths and

+×1 — canonical NumPy DataLoader source missing). Those failures did not appear on 08-09. They had
+been invisible for as long as the collection abort existed, because a directory that will not
+collect reports nothing at all.
+
+**Consequence for the record, and the reason this is its own entry:**
+
+- Any off-cluster test count taken **before** 2026-08-09 counted only the modules that happened to
+  collect before the abort, and is therefore **an undercount of the total and an overcount of the
+  pass rate.** The post-fix numbers are 932 passing / 7 failing / 1 skipped.
+- **Do not read the 7 as a regression.** Comparing a pre-fix count to a post-fix count will show
+  failures appearing out of nowhere and tests appearing out of nowhere, and neither happened.
+- This affects **both lanes**, not only the one that fixed it: the aborted collection took the
+  GBDT/P4 suites down with the PET ones, and vice versa. A green report from either lane before
+  this date is scoped to whatever collected.
+- The general form: **a collection-time failure is not a test failure, it is a measurement
+  outage.** A suite that cannot collect does not report red — it reports nothing, and nothing
+  reads like fine. Judge suite health by collected count as well as pass count.

    61	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    62	# corpus
    63	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    64	EXTS = (".py", ".cpp", ".cxx", ".cc", ".C", ".h", ".hpp")
    65	
    66	
    67	def tracked_files(root):
    68	    out = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    69	    return [f for f in out.splitlines() if f.endswith(EXTS)]
    70	
    71	
    72	def strip_comments(text, is_py):
    73	    """Remove comments and (for python) string literals, so prose about TParameter does not
    74	    register as a use. Deliberately crude and deliberately over-eager: a false NEGATIVE here
    75	    would hide a write site, so string literals are blanked rather than dropped, preserving
    76	    offsets and line numbers."""
    77	    if is_py:
    78	        # blank out triple-quoted blocks, keep newlines so line numbers survive
    79	        def _blank(m):
    80	            return re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", m.group(0))
    81	        text = re.sub(r'"""(?:.|\n)*?"""', _blank, text)
    82	        text = re.sub(r"'''(?:.|\n)*?'''", _blank, text)
    83	        text = re.sub(r"(?m)#.*$", lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), text)
    84	    else:
    85	        text = re.sub(r"/\*(?:.|\n)*?\*/",
    86	                      lambda m: re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", m.group(0)), text)
    87	        text = re.sub(r"(?m)//.*$", lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), text)
    88	    return text
    89	
    90	
    91	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    92	# writes
    93	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    94	# C++:      new TParameter<int>("name", v, 'f')      /  TParameter<double>("name", v).Write()
    95	# PyROOT:   ROOT.TParameter("double")("name", v)     /  ROOT.TParameter("int")("name", v, 'f')
    96	CPP_WRITE = re.compile(
    97	    r"TParameter\s*<\s*(?P<type>[A-Za-z_][\w: ]*?)\s*>\s*\(\s*"
    98	    r"(?P<name>\"[^\"]+\"|[A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*,(?P<rest>[^;]*)")
    99	PY_WRITE = re.compile(
   100	    r"TParameter\s*\(\s*[\"'](?P<type>\w+)[\"']\s*\)\s*\(\s*"
   101	    r"(?P<name>[^,]+?)\s*,(?P<rest>[^\n]*)")
   102	MERGE_MODE = re.compile(r"[,(]\s*'(?P<mode>[+flmM])'")
   103	
   104	
   105	def _literal(tok):
   106	    tok = tok.strip()
   107	    if tok.startswith(('"', "'")) and tok.endswith(('"', "'")):
   108	        return tok[1:-1], True
   109	    return tok, False           # f-string / variable / concatenation
   110	
   111	
   112	def find_writes(root, files):
   113	    writes = {}                                     # name -> dict
   114	    dynamic = []                                    # non-literal names, reported separately
   115	    for rel in files:
   116	        path = os.path.join(root, rel)
   117	        try:
   118	            raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   119	        except OSError:
   120	            continue
   121	        if "TParameter" not in raw:
   122	            continue
   123	        is_py = rel.endswith(".py")
   124	        text = strip_comments(raw, is_py)
   125	        for rx in (CPP_WRITE, PY_WRITE):
   126	            for m in rx.finditer(text):
   127	                name, literal = _literal(m.group("name"))
   128	                line = text[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1
   129	                mode = MERGE_MODE.search(m.group("rest"))
   130	                rec = {"type": m.group("type").strip(),
   131	                       "mode": mode.group("mode") if mode else "+",
   132	                       "mode_explicit": bool(mode),
   133	                       "site": f"{rel}:{line}"}
   134	                if not literal:
   135	                    dynamic.append(dict(rec, name=name))
   136	                    continue
   137	                writes.setdefault(name, []).append(rec)
   138	    return writes, dynamic
   139	
   140	
   141	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   142	# reads
   143	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   144	def find_reads(root, files, names):
   145	    """A read is the field's literal name appearing in executable code in a file that does not
   146	    write it. Name-based and therefore over-inclusive; that is the correct direction of error
   147	    for an inventory whose job is to make sure nothing is missed."""
   148	    reads = {n: [] for n in names}
   149	    for rel in files:
   150	        path = os.path.join(root, rel)
   151	        try:
   152	            raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   153	        except OSError:
   154	            continue
   155	        if not any(n in raw for n in names):
   156	            continue
   157	        text = strip_comments(raw, rel.endswith(".py"))
   158	        for i, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
   159	            for n in names:
   160	                if f'"{n}"' in line or f"'{n}'" in line:
   161	                    if "TParameter" in line:
   162	                        continue                     # that is the write site
   163	                    reads[n].append(f"{rel}:{i}")
   164	    return reads
   165	
   166	
   167	MEANING = {
   168	    # '+' is the DEFAULT and is correct for extensive quantities; the tool cannot tell extensive
   169	    # from intensive, so it states the mechanism and leaves the verdict to the triaged table.
   170	    "+": ("SUM over merged inputs (12 playlists here). Correct for an EXTENSIVE quantity (POT, "
   171	          "counts, censuses); WRONG for a per-playlist constant, a ratio, or a 0/1 flag (which "
   172	          "becomes a count in [0,12])"),
   173	    "f": "FIRST input's value -- hadd-safe, means what the writer meant",
   174	    "l": "LAST input's value -- hadd-safe but order-dependent",
   175	    "m": "MIN over merged inputs",
   176	    "M": "MAX over merged inputs",
   177	}
   178	
   179	
   180	def summary(root="."):
   181	    files = tracked_files(root)
   182	    writes, dynamic = find_writes(root, files)
   183	    reads = find_reads(root, files, set(writes))
   184	    rows = []
   185	    for name in sorted(writes):
   186	        recs = writes[name]
   187	        modes = sorted({r["mode"] for r in recs})
   188	        rows.append({"name": name,
   189	                     "types": sorted({r["type"] for r in recs}),
   190	                     "mode": modes[0] if len(modes) == 1 else "MIXED:" + ",".join(modes),
   191	                     "mode_explicit": any(r["mode_explicit"] for r in recs),
   192	                     "post_hadd_meaning": MEANING.get(modes[0], "AMBIGUOUS -- written both ways")
   193	                                          if len(modes) == 1 else "AMBIGUOUS -- written both ways",
   194	                     "written_at": [r["site"] for r in recs],
   195	                     "read_at": reads.get(name, [])})
   196	    return {"tool": "audit_tparameter_merge_semantics",
   197	            "n_files_scanned": len(files),
   198	            "n_fields": len(rows),
   199	            "n_summing": sum(1 for r in rows if r["mode"] == "+"),
   200	            "n_hadd_safe": sum(1 for r in rows if r["mode"] != "+"),
   201	            "dynamic_names": dynamic,
   202	            "fields": rows}
   203	
   204	
   205	def main():
   206	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   207	    ap.add_argument("--root", default=".")
   208	    ap.add_argument("--power", action="store_true", help="assert the two live controls")
   209	    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
   210	    a = ap.parse_args()
   211	    root = os.path.abspath(a.root)
   212	    s = summary(root)
   213	
   214	    if a.json:
   215	        print(json.dumps(s, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
   216	    else:
   217	        print("=" * 100)
   218	        print(f"TParameter merge semantics -- {s['n_fields']} fields over "
   219	              f"{s['n_files_scanned']} tracked source files")
   220	        print(f"  {s['n_summing']} SUM across merged inputs (default '+'), "
   221	              f"{s['n_hadd_safe']} declare a hadd-safe mode")
   222	        print("=" * 100)
   223	        for r in s["fields"]:
   224	            flag = "  " if r["mode"] != "+" else "!!"
   225	            print(f"\n{flag} {r['name']}   <{'/'.join(r['types'])}>   mode={r['mode']}"
   226	                  f"{'' if r['mode_explicit'] else ' (implicit)'}")
   227	            print(f"     post-hadd : {r['post_hadd_meaning']}")
   228	            print(f"     written   : {', '.join(r['written_at'])}")
   229	            print(f"     read      : {', '.join(r['read_at']) if r['read_at'] else '(no read site found)'}")
   230	        if s["dynamic_names"]:
   231	            print("\n" + "-" * 100)
   232	            print("NAMES BUILT AT RUNTIME (f-string / variable) -- not resolvable statically, "
   233	                  "check by hand:")
   234	            for d in s["dynamic_names"]:
   235	                print(f"  {d['site']}: {d['name']}  <{d['type']}> mode={d['mode']}")
   236	
   237	    if a.power:
   238	        by = {r["name"]: r for r in s["fields"]}
   239	        bad = []
   240	        if by.get("hasTruthOnlyMisses", {}).get("mode") != "+":
   241	            bad.append("hasTruthOnlyMisses should parse as '+' (it is why this sweep exists)")
   242	        if by.get("hasFullEventSchema", {}).get("mode") != "f":
   243	            bad.append("hasFullEventSchema should parse as 'f' (the mitigated control)")
   244	        if bad:
   245	            print("\nPOWER TEST FAILED:")
   246	            for b in bad:
   247	                print("  " + b)
   248	            sys.exit(1)
   249	        print("\nPOWER TEST PASSED: both live controls classified correctly "
   250	              "(hasTruthOnlyMisses '+', hasFullEventSchema 'f')")
   251	    return 0
   252	
   253	
   254	if __name__ == "__main__":
   255	    sys.exit(main())
     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Find every quantity DERIVED from two or more `hadd`-summed extensive TParameters.
     3	
     4	THE CLASS THIS SWEEPS, and why it needs its own tool.
     5	
     6	`FINDING-20260809-tparameter-merge-semantics.md` established that `hadd` sums `TParameter` by
     7	default, and that summing is CORRECT for an extensive quantity (POT, event counts, censuses) and
     8	wrong only for an intensive one or a flag. Twelve of the fifteen fields that transit a merge are
     9	extensive and merge correctly.
    10	
    11	That result has a blind spot, and it is the reason this second sweep exists:
    12	
    13	    TWO EXTENSIVE FIELDS CAN EACH MERGE CORRECTLY WHILE A QUANTITY DERIVED FROM THEM DOES NOT.
    14	
    15	    sum(dataPOTUsed) / sum(mcPOTUsed) is NOT the playlist-mixture-correct Data/MC ratio. Both
    16	    operands are impeccable. Per-field merge-sensitivity review asks "is this field
    17	    merge-sensitive?", gets `no` for both, and passes the quotient without ever looking at it.
    18	
    19	That is J36 (`KNOWN_ISSUES`): per-playlist Data/MC ratios span 0.1707-0.2371, **38.9% max/min-1**,
    20	against a global 0.2124, giving a **9.4% POT-weighted mean absolute mixture error**. It has been
    21	open since 2026-08-01 as a "scoping decision owed", and it sits **two functions away** from an
    22	explicit, correct, well-commented defence of trap #8 for `pTmu_fiducial_nucleons`. The defence
    23	did not generalise to it because a per-field question cannot reach a two-field answer.
    24	
    25	**Nobody has swept this class.** J36 is its only known member, and one member is not a size.
    26	
    27	WHAT COUNTS AS A HIT. A binary operation in which at least one operand carries taint from a read
    28	of a merged extensive field. Reported by shape, because the shapes fail differently:
    29	
    30	  RATIO_OF_TWO_MERGED   both sides tainted, operator `/`, and the two sides' field sets are
    31	                        DISJOINT. **This is the J36 shape and the only one that is a defect by
    32	                        construction:** `sum(A)/sum(B)` for different A and B is a POT-weighted
    33	                        mean over the merged inventory, not the per-playlist ratio a reader
    34	                        expects, and nothing cancels.
    35	  RATIO_COMMON_SCALE    both sides tainted, operator `/`, but the SAME field appears on both
    36	                        sides -- a POT-scaled histogram over another POT-scaled histogram. The
    37	                        scale cancels. Real taint, different semantics, not this class. Reported
    38	                        rather than suppressed so the distinction is visible and auditable.
    39	  SCALED_BY_MERGED      one side tainted, `*` or `/`. A normalisation; correct iff the other
    40	                        operand spans the same inventory as the merged total.
    41	  DIFF_/OFFSET_BY_MERGED  `+`/`-` involving a tainted operand. Usually benign; listed for
    42	                        completeness because a difference of two sums over DIFFERENT inventories
    43	                        is not.
    44	
    45	TAINT, and its honest bound. AST-based, intraprocedural, **flow-sensitive with kill-on-reassign**:
    46	  * a read is any expression containing a string literal naming a merged extensive field
    47	    (`f.Get("dataPOTUsed")`, `d["mcPOT"]`, ...);
    48	  * assignment propagates taint to the target name; reassignment from an untainted expression
    49	    KILLS it;
    50	  * taint flows through `.GetVal()`, `float(...)`, subscripts, tuples and simple calls.
    51	
    52	The first version was flow-INsensitive, on the reasoning that over-reporting is the safe error
    53	when sizing a class. That was wrong in a way worth recording: in a 200-line `main()` a short name
    54	(`mc`, `d`, `m`) is bound to a POT scalar early and REBOUND to a histogram array later, and sticky
    55	taint then reported `dat / mc` -- an ordinary data/MC histogram ratio -- as a merged-POT quotient.
    56	It produced 17 "ratios" of which 11 were that. Two-thirds noise does not size a class, it
    57	transfers the triage (BEN-071 rule 2). Killing taint on reassignment and requiring disjoint field
    58	sets took it to 8, all genuine.
    59	
    60	It does NOT cross function boundaries, so a helper returning a ratio and a caller consuming it are
    61	two sites and only the first is found; and it cannot see taint arriving through a dict passed as
    62	an argument. Both make this an UNDER-count, which is the direction to be wrong in when the
    63	question is "is this class bigger than one?".
    64	
    65	POWER (`--power`): the sweep must find `get_pot_scales` in
    66	`2d-unfolding/unfold_2d_omnifold_unbinned.py` as a RATIO_OF_TWO_MERGED. That is J36, it is live in
    67	the tree, and if a future repair fixes it the power test fails loudly and forces this table to be
    68	regenerated rather than passing forever against a synthetic control.
    69	
    70	Usage:
    71	    python3 docs/orchestration/audit_derived_from_merged_extensives.py [--root .] [--power] [--json]
    72	"""
    73	import argparse
    74	import ast
    75	import json
    76	import os
    77	import re
    78	import subprocess
    79	import sys
    80	
    81	# The extensive fields that transit a hadd, from the per-field sweep. Flags and intensives are
    82	# excluded deliberately: they are already defects on their own and are covered by the other tool.
    83	# `POTUsed` is included because it is the same quantity under an older name.
    84	MERGED_EXTENSIVE = {
    85	    "dataPOTUsed", "mcPOTUsed", "POTUsed",
    86	    "dataPOT", "mcPOT",                      # the python-side names written by the unfold drivers
    87	    "activeUniverseTruthEntrants", "activeUniverseTruthExits",
    88	    "activeUniverseRecoEntrants", "activeUniverseRecoExits",
    89	    "nTruthOnlyMisses",
    90	}
    91	
    92	
    93	def tracked_py(root):
    94	    out = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    95	    return [f for f in out.splitlines() if f.endswith(".py")]
    96	
    97	
    98	def _strings(node):
    99	    """Every string literal anywhere inside an expression."""
   100	    return {n.value for n in ast.walk(node)
   101	            if isinstance(n, ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value, str)}
   102	
   103	
   104	def _names(node):
   105	    return {n.id for n in ast.walk(node) if isinstance(n, ast.Name)}
   106	
   107	
   108	class Scan(ast.NodeVisitor):
   109	    """One pass per function; taint is a set of local names."""
   110	
   111	    def __init__(self, rel, src):
   112	        self.rel, self.src = rel, src
   113	        self.hits = []
   114	
   115	    def _fields_read(self, node):
   116	        return _strings(node) & MERGED_EXTENSIVE
   117	
   118	    def visit_FunctionDef(self, fn):
   119	        # FLOW-SENSITIVE, with kill-on-reassign. The first version of this tool was
   120	        # flow-insensitive over two passes, on the theory that over-reporting is the safe error
   121	        # for a class being sized. It is not: in a 200-line `main()` a short name like `mc` or `d`
   122	        # is bound to a POT value early and REBOUND to a histogram array later, and sticky taint
   123	        # then flagged `dat / mc` -- a data/MC histogram ratio -- as a merged-POT quotient. Eleven
   124	        # of seventeen "ratios" were that. A hit list that is two-thirds noise transfers the
   125	        # triage instead of doing it (BEN-071), so taint is now killed when a name is reassigned
   126	        # from an untainted expression, and sites are visited in source order.
   127	        tainted = {}
   128	        events = []
   129	        for node in ast.walk(fn):
   130	            if isinstance(node, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign, ast.AugAssign, ast.BinOp)):
   131	                events.append(node)
   132	        events.sort(key=lambda n: (n.lineno, n.col_offset))
   133	
   134	        for node in events:
   135	            if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
   136	                op = type(node.op).__name__
   137	                if op not in ("Div", "Mult", "Sub", "Add"):
   138	                    continue
   139	
   140	                def side(e):
   141	                    return self._fields_read(e) | {f for n in _names(e) if n in tainted
   142	                                                   for f in tainted[n]}
   143	                L, R = side(node.left), side(node.right)
   144	                if not (L or R):
   145	                    continue
   146	                # THE DISCRIMINATOR for the J36 shape, and the one judgement in this tool.
   147	                # J36 is `sum(A) / sum(B)` where A and B are DIFFERENT merged fields: each side
   148	                # carries exactly one field and the two differ, so nothing cancels and the
   149	                # quotient is a POT-weighted mean masquerading as a per-playlist ratio. When both
   150	                # sides carry the SAME field, that field is a common scale applied to both
   151	                # operands (a POT-scaled histogram divided by another POT-scaled histogram) and
   152	                # it cancels -- real taint, different semantics, not this class.
   153	                disjoint = bool(L and R and not (L & R))
   154	                if L and R:
   155	                    if op == "Div":
   156	                        shape = "RATIO_OF_TWO_MERGED" if disjoint else "RATIO_COMMON_SCALE"
   157	                    else:
   158	                        shape = "DIFF_OF_TWO_MERGED"
   159	                else:
   160	                    shape = "SCALED_BY_MERGED" if op in ("Div", "Mult") else "OFFSET_BY_MERGED"
   161	                self.hits.append({
   162	                    "file": self.rel, "line": node.lineno, "function": fn.name,
   163	                    "op": op, "shape": shape,
   164	                    "fields": sorted(L | R),
   165	                    "lhs_fields": sorted(L), "rhs_fields": sorted(R),
   166	                    "both_sides": bool(L and R),
   167	                    "source": self.src.splitlines()[node.lineno - 1].strip()[:130],
   168	                })
   169	                continue
   170	
   171	            val = node.value
   172	            if val is None:
   173	                continue
   174	            got = self._fields_read(val) | {f for n in _names(val) if n in tainted
   175	                                            for f in tainted[n]}
   176	            if isinstance(node, ast.AugAssign):
   177	                targets = [node.target]
   178	            elif isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign):
   179	                targets = [node.target]
   180	            else:
   181	                targets = node.targets
   182	            for t in targets:
   183	                for nm in ast.walk(t):
   184	                    if isinstance(nm, ast.Name):
   185	                        if got:
   186	                            tainted.setdefault(nm.id, set()).update(got)
   187	                        elif not isinstance(node, ast.AugAssign):
   188	                            tainted.pop(nm.id, None)          # KILL: rebound to something else
   189	        self.generic_visit(fn)
   190	
   191	    visit_AsyncFunctionDef = visit_FunctionDef
   192	
   193	
   194	CPP_EXTS = (".cpp", ".cxx", ".cc", ".C", ".h", ".hpp")
   195	
   196	
   197	def scan_cpp(root):
   198	    """C++ pass (2026-08-09, added because an unswept language is where a count hides).
   199	
   200	    Deliberately NOT an AST pass. Only ONE tracked C++ file reads a merged extensive at all
   201	    (`ExtractCrossSection.cpp` -- everything else WRITES them), so the population is small enough
   202	    to enumerate by identifier and verify by eye, and a clang-level tool would be more machinery
   203	    than the corpus justifies. Two stages: find every C++ read of a merged-extensive TParameter,
   204	    then find every `/` on a line mentioning two identifiers bound from those reads.
   205	
   206	    Bound, stated plainly: this finds ratios formed on ONE line from locally-named values. A ratio
   207	    split across lines, or hidden behind a helper, is not found. Like the Python pass it is a
   208	    floor."""
   209	    out = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
   210	    files = [f for f in out.splitlines() if f.endswith(CPP_EXTS)]
   211	    reads, ratios = [], []
   212	    for rel in files:
   213	        try:
   214	            raw = open(os.path.join(root, rel), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   215	        except OSError:
   216	            continue
   217	        if not any(f in raw for f in MERGED_EXTENSIVE):
   218	            continue
   219	        local = set()
   220	        lines = raw.splitlines()
   221	        for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
   222	            code = line.split("//")[0]
   223	            if not code.strip():
   224	                continue
   225	            hit = [f for f in MERGED_EXTENSIVE if f'"{f}"' in code]
   226	            # A READ is a GetIngredient/Get of the name, not a construction. The construction is
   227	            # frequently SPLIT across lines --
   228	            #     auto pNMisses = new TParameter<long>(
   229	            #         "nTruthOnlyMisses", nTruthOnlyMisses);
   230	            # -- so testing the current line alone reported five writes as reads. Look back over
   231	            # the preceding continuation lines until a statement boundary.
   232	            if hit:
   233	                j, is_write = i - 2, False
   234	                while j >= 0:
   235	                    prev = lines[j].split("//")[0]
   236	                    # ONLY `new TParameter` marks a construction. An earlier version also keyed
   237	                    # on `TParameter<`, which matches `GetIngredient<TParameter<double>>` -- i.e.
   238	                    # the READ idiom -- and silently reclassified a real read as a write, taking
   239	                    # the count from 2 to 1 and the ratios from 2 to 0. Over-correcting a false
   240	                    # positive into a false negative is the worse of the two errors here.
   241	                    if "new TParameter" in prev:
   242	                        is_write = True
   243	                    if prev.rstrip().endswith(";") or not prev.strip():
   244	                        break
   245	                    j -= 1
   246	                if is_write or "new TParameter" in code:
   247	                    hit = []
   248	            if hit:
   249	                reads.append({"file": rel, "line": i, "fields": sorted(hit),
   250	                              "source": code.strip()[:130]})
   251	                for nm in re.findall(r"\b([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*=", code):
   252	                    local.add(nm)
   253	            if "/" in code and local:
   254	                present = [n for n in local if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(n)}\b", code)]
   255	                if len(present) >= 2 and re.search(r"\b\w+\s*/\s*\w+", code):
   256	                    ratios.append({"file": rel, "line": i, "locals": sorted(present),
   257	                                   "source": code.strip()[:130]})
   258	    return {"reads": reads, "ratios": ratios}

   261	def summary(root="."):
   262	    hits = []
   263	    for rel in tracked_py(root):
   264	        path = os.path.join(root, rel)
   265	        try:
   266	            src = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   267	        except OSError:
   268	            continue
   269	        if not any(f in src for f in MERGED_EXTENSIVE):
   270	            continue
   271	        try:
   272	            tree = ast.parse(src)
   273	        except SyntaxError:
   274	            continue
   275	        sc = Scan(rel, src)
   276	        sc.visit(tree)
   277	        hits.extend(sc.hits)
   278	    order = {"RATIO_OF_TWO_MERGED": 0, "SCALED_BY_MERGED": 1, "RATIO_COMMON_SCALE": 2,
   279	             "DIFF_OF_TWO_MERGED": 3, "OFFSET_BY_MERGED": 4}
   280	    hits.sort(key=lambda h: (order.get(h["shape"], 9), h["file"], h["line"]))
   281	    by_shape = {}
   282	    for h in hits:
   283	        by_shape[h["shape"]] = by_shape.get(h["shape"], 0) + 1
   284	    cpp = scan_cpp(root)
   285	    return {"tool": "audit_derived_from_merged_extensives",
   286	            "n_sites": len(hits), "by_shape": by_shape,
   287	            "cpp": cpp, "n_cpp_reads": len(cpp["reads"]), "n_cpp_ratios": len(cpp["ratios"]),
   288	            "n_files": len({h["file"] for h in hits}),
   289	            "sites": hits}

 \label{sec:tension}
 
 \paragraph{The paradox.}
 The central values agree well: $\sigma_{\tot}^{\ours}/\sigma_{\tot}^{\paper}
 = 1.011$, median bin ratio $1.006$, and the \emph{per-bin pull RMS}
 against the paper covariance is only $0.598$ (\S\ref{sec:pull}).
 A diagonal-only $\chi^{2}$ --- ignoring all off-diagonal correlations ---
 is therefore
 \begin{equation}
 \chi^{2}_{\diag}/\mathrm{ndf}
 = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i}\frac{\Delta_{i}^{2}}{C_{ii}}
 = \mathrm{RMS}(\mathrm{pull})^{2} + \mathrm{mean}(\mathrm{pull})^{2}
 \approx 0.366,
 \end{equation}
 yet the full-covariance $\chi^{2}/\mathrm{ndf}=3.661$. The tension is a
 $10\times$ inflation that lives \emph{entirely} in the off-diagonal /
 small-eigenvalue structure of the published \texttt{TotalCov}
 (\texttt{diagnose\_tension.py}). The rest of this section dissects it.
 
 \paragraph{Eigenmode decomposition.}
 Diagonalize the reported-block paper covariance,
 $\mathbf{C}=\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}\mathbf{u}_{k}\mathbf{u}_{k}\T$
 ($\lambda_{1}\!\ge\!\cdots\!\ge\!\lambda_{n}$), and project the residual
 $\boldsymbol{\Delta}$ onto each eigenvector, $c_{k}=\mathbf{u}_{k}\T\boldsymbol{\Delta}$.
 Then
 \begin{equation}
 \chi^{2}=\boldsymbol{\Delta}\T\mathbf{C}^{+}\boldsymbol{\Delta}
 =\sum_{k}\frac{c_{k}^{2}}{\lambda_{k}},
 \qquad
 \text{``eigen-pull''}_{k}\equiv\frac{c_{k}}{\sqrt{\lambda_{k}}},
 \end{equation}
 verified to reproduce the \texttt{pinv} $\chi^{2}=750.49$ to $3\times10^{-9}$.
 The decomposition shows the tension is \textbf{neither a few pathological
 null directions nor the absolute smallest eigenvalues}:
 \begin{itemize}[nosep]
   \item The top contributing modes sit at $\lambda_{k}/\lambda_{\max}\sim
         10^{-4}$--$10^{-5}$ --- the lower-middle of the spectrum by
         magnitude, but still $\sim7$--$8$ decades above the cond-floor
         ($\lambda/\lambda_{\max}\sim10^{-12}$) --- with standardized-component
         magnitudes $5$--$6$. These are descriptive coordinates in the published
         covariance basis, not calibrated significances for two independent results.
   \item The ten \emph{smallest}-$\lambda$ modes carry only $3\%$ of the
         $\chi^{2}$; about $90$ modes are needed to reach $90\%$. The
         $\chi^{2}$ is broadly distributed, not localized to the
         ill-conditioned tail.
 \end{itemize}
 
 \paragraph{Regularization robustness.}
 A \texttt{pinv}-rcond scan confirms the tension is not a numerical artifact:
 retaining only the $73$ best-determined directions
 ($\lambda_{k}/\lambda_{\max}>10^{-4}$) still gives $\chi^{2}/\mathrm{ndf}=1.42$;
 $139$ directions ($>10^{-6}$) give $2.79$. A rank-truncation scan keeping the
 $r$ largest-$\lambda$ modes rises smoothly $0.69\,(r{=}50)\to2.35\,(100)\to
 3.30\,(180)\to3.66\,(205)$ --- no late jump, i.e.\ the tension does not ride on
 the last few least-determined modes.
 
 \paragraph{It is shape, not normalization.}
 Splitting $\boldsymbol{\Delta}$ into a component along the measured
 spectrum $\mathbf{x}^{\paper}$ (an overall scale) and the orthogonal
 remainder, the scale piece contributes $\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{norm}}=0.10$ and the
 shape piece $\chi^{2}_{\text{shape}}=750.1$. The $+1.1\%$ normalization
 offset is statistically irrelevant to the tension; it is a correlated
 \emph{shape} difference. (Consistent with the Jacobian shape-only
 $\chi^{2}/\mathrm{ndf}=3.60$, \S\ref{sec:shape}.)
 
 \paragraph{Where it lives.}
 Mapping the dominant eigenvectors and the per-bin contribution
 $\Delta_{i}(\mathbf{C}^{+}\boldsymbol{\Delta})_{i}$ back onto the
 $14\times16$ grid (\texttt{tension\_mode\_maps.png},
 \texttt{tension\_chi2\_map.png}) localizes the tension to the
 \textbf{low-$\pT$ cross-section peak ridge} ($\pT\lesssim0.4$ GeV/c,
 $\pT$-bins 2/7/10 carry $16/11/12\%$) and the low-$\pPar$ near-edge
 cells ($\pPar$-bins 0/1/8). The carrier modes are sign-alternating
 \emph{shape} oscillations across the peak, not vertical $\pT$-columns
 (which a flux $1/\Phi(\pT)$ normalization error would produce) and not
 the $\theta_{\mu}<20^{\circ}$ acceptance boundary. This is exactly where
 the flux and Muon\_Energy bands --- the two largest, and the only named
 cross-band correlation (Bashyal, \S\ref{sec:rank}) --- dominate the
 covariance: tight bin-to-bin correlation there leaves little freedom to
 absorb a coherent $\sim1$--$2\%$ shape difference, so a small
-OmniFold-vs-IBU shape difference becomes a large $\chi^{2}$.
+OmniFold-vs-IBU shape difference becomes a large $\chi^{2}$.%
+\footnote{The pipeline applies one global $\mathrm{POT}_{\mathrm{data}}/\mathrm{POT}_{\mathrm{MC}}$
+ratio rather than a per-playlist ratio (KNOWN\_ISSUES J36), and the per-playlist ratios span
+$0.1707$--$0.2371$. Because this statement asserts sensitivity at the $1$--$2\%$ level, the
+mixture error was measured directly against it: comparing $R_{\mathrm{glob}}\sum_p \mathrm{MC}_p$
+with $\sum_p R_p\,\mathrm{MC}_p$ over the twelve playlists changes the reco shape by at most
+$0.07\%$ in $\pT$ and $0.14\%$ in $\pPar$ (and $0.03\%$ across the low-$\pT$ ridge), with the
+residual $+0.12\%$ appearing as normalization rather than shape. The twelve playlists are nearly
+shape-identical, so a large reweighting of them is almost pure normalization. The statement above
+is therefore unaffected at the $14$--$30\times$ level.}
 
 \paragraph{A methodological component (estimator and iteration).}
 Part of the tension is regularization-dependent --- the same data, same
 normalization ($\Sigma\sigma$ within $0.1\%$), unfolded with a different
 GBDT backend moves the paper-cov $\chi^{2}$ by $\sim1$ unit while central
 values barely change (iteration count, by contrast, is negligible):
 \begin{center}
 \begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}
 \toprule
 OmniFold configuration & paper-cov $\chi^{2}/\mathrm{ndf}$ & pull RMS \\
 \midrule
 exact-GBT, 5 iter (frozen production) & $3.66$ & $0.598$ \\
 HistGBT, 5 iter (10-seed mean) & $2.70\pm0.04$ & $0.56$ \\
 LightGBM, 5 iter & $2.65$ & $0.563$ \\
 LightGBM, 10 iter & $2.66$ & $0.565$ \\
 \bottomrule
 \end{tabular}
 \end{center}
 Two things separate cleanly. (i) \textbf{Iteration count is negligible}:
 LightGBM $5\to10$ iters moves the $\chi^{2}$ by $+0.01$ ($2.645\to2.657$),
 so OmniFold is well-converged at $5$ iters and the tension is \emph{not}
 an under-iteration artifact. (ii) \textbf{The GBDT estimator carries a
 $\sim1$-unit band}: the frozen exact-GBT production ($3.66$) is the
 outlier, while both histogram-binned backends agree at $2.65$--$2.70$
 (HistGBT is a $10$-seed mean, range $2.63$--$2.74$; the $\pm0.04$ ML-seed
 jitter is $\sim25\times$ smaller than the $0.96$ exact$\to$hist gap, so
 that gap is genuinely the estimator, not seed noise). The exact-gradient
 trees fit finer shape structure (less implicit smoothing) and so deviate
 more from the paper's IBU-regularized result. This is direct evidence
 that $\sim1$ $\chi^{2}$-unit of the tension is OmniFold's implicit
 regularization rather than a physical data--MC disagreement
 (\texttt{tension\_iter/}).
 
 \paragraph{Conclusion.}
 The tension is (i) a genuine, broadly-distributed, \emph{correlated shape}
 difference --- not a normalization offset and not a small-$\lambda$
 inversion artifact --- concentrated in the low-$\pT$ peak where the
 flux/Muon\_Energy bands dominate, plus (ii) a $\sim1$-$\chi^{2}$-unit
 methodological band from the GBDT estimator/iteration regularization.
 Both point to the same structure: the Bashyal
 flux\,$\leftrightarrow$\,Muon\_Energy joint block (rederived at
 $\rho=\rhoFluxMuon$, \S\ref{sec:rank}) is exactly the covariance structure
 governing the region that carries the tension.
 
 \subsection{Pull diagnostics and the open 2D coverage test}
 \label{sec:coverage}
 
 \paragraph{What it estimates.}
 The existing closure-toy ensemble supports a same-ensemble standardized-pull
 calculation that checks whether the toy distribution is approximately
 Gaussian. It does not support a valid 2D coverage claim: the MC bootstrap also
 fluctuates the stored \texttt{hTruthXSec2D}, so the all-toy truth mean is not an
 independent reference. A future disjoint calibration/evaluation test must use
 an independently stored unfluctuated truth (or a redesigned toy ensemble).
 
 \paragraph{Procedure (\texttt{sbatch\_coverage\_toys\_MEFHC\_200.sh}).}
 Generate $N_{\text{toy}}=200$ closure unfolds, each one combining two
 existing modes of \texttt{unfold\_2d\_omnifold\_unbinned.py}:
 \begin{itemize}[nosep]
   \item \texttt{-{}-closure}: pseudo-data are MC reco events
         (weighted); a truth marginal is written to
         \texttt{hTruthXSec2D} in every output file.
   \item \texttt{-{}-bootstrap-seed $k$} (seeds chosen to avoid
         collision with the production replicas): per-event Poisson(1)
         draws, same as the production bootstrap.
 \end{itemize}
 Toy seeds are independent and bins within a toy are correlated. Because the
 MC bootstrap multiplies \texttt{w\_truth}, the stored truth marginal also
 varies from toy to toy and cannot serve as the independent coverage target.
 
 \paragraph{Math.}
 Stack the toys into an $N_{\text{toy}}\times14\times16$ array
 $\mathbf{U}^{(t)}$. Here $\bar X^{\text{truth}}$ is the all-toy mean used only
 to center this same-ensemble diagnostic. For each reported bin (where
 $\bar X^{\text{truth}}_{i}>0$, $i$ indexing the $205$ reported cells):
 \begin{align}
 \sigma_{i}
 \;&=\;
 \mathrm{std}\big(\mathbf{U}^{(t)}_{i}; \,\text{ddof}=1\big)
 \quad\text{(spread across toys)},

   946	        $\chi^{2}$ is broadly distributed, not localized to the
   947	        ill-conditioned tail.

        This routine should be called exactly once.
    
        We determine whether or not a candidate temp dir is usable by
        trying to create and write to a file in that directory.  If this
        is successful, the test file is deleted.  To prevent denial of
        service, the name of the test file must be randomized."""
    
        namer = _RandomNameSequence()
        dirlist = _candidate_tempdir_list()
    
        for dir in dirlist:
            if dir != _os.curdir:
                dir = _os.path.abspath(dir)
            # Try only a few names per directory.
            for seq in range(100):
                name = next(namer)
                filename = _os.path.join(dir, name)
                try:
                    fd = _os.open(filename, _bin_openflags, 0o600)
                    try:
                        try:
                            _os.write(fd, b'blat')
                        finally:
                            _os.close(fd)
                    finally:
                        _os.unlink(filename)
                    return dir
                except FileExistsError:
                    pass
                except PermissionError:
                    # This exception is thrown when a directory with the chosen name
                    # already exists on windows.
                    if (_os.name == 'nt' and _os.path.isdir(dir) and
                        _os.access(dir, _os.W_OK)):
                        continue
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
                except OSError:
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory

        """Calculate the default directory to use for temporary files.
        This routine should be called exactly once.
    
        We determine whether or not a candidate temp dir is usable by
        trying to create and write to a file in that directory.  If this
        is successful, the test file is deleted.  To prevent denial of
        service, the name of the test file must be randomized."""

        dirlist = _candidate_tempdir_list()

                dir = _os.path.abspath(dir)
            # Try only a few names per directory.
            for seq in range(100):
                name = next(namer)
                filename = _os.path.join(dir, name)
                try:
                    fd = _os.open(filename, _bin_openflags, 0o600)
                    try:
                        try:
                            _os.write(fd, b'blat')
                        finally:
                            _os.close(fd)
                    finally:
                        _os.unlink(filename)
                    return dir

                    pass

    def _get_default_tempdir():
        """Calculate the default directory to use for temporary files.
        This routine should be called exactly once.
    
        We determine whether or not a candidate temp dir is usable by
        trying to create and write to a file in that directory.  If this
        is successful, the test file is deleted.  To prevent denial of
        service, the name of the test file must be randomized."""
    
        namer = _RandomNameSequence()
        dirlist = _candidate_tempdir_list()
    
        for dir in dirlist:
            if dir != _os.curdir:
                dir = _os.path.abspath(dir)
            # Try only a few names per directory.
            for seq in range(100):
                name = next(namer)
                filename = _os.path.join(dir, name)
                try:
                    fd = _os.open(filename, _bin_openflags, 0o600)
                    try:
                        try:
                            _os.write(fd, b'blat')
                        finally:
                            _os.close(fd)
                    finally:
                        _os.unlink(filename)
                    return dir
                except FileExistsError:
                    pass
                except PermissionError:
                    # This exception is thrown when a directory with the chosen name
                    # already exists on windows.
                    if (_os.name == 'nt' and _os.path.isdir(dir) and
                        _os.access(dir, _os.W_OK)):
                        continue
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
                except OSError:
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory

    def _get_default_tempdir():
        """Calculate the default directory to use for temporary files.
        This routine should be called exactly once.
    
        We determine whether or not a candidate temp dir is usable by
        trying to create and write to a file in that directory.  If this
        is successful, the test file is deleted.  To prevent denial of
        service, the name of the test file must be randomized."""
    
        namer = _RandomNameSequence()
        dirlist = _candidate_tempdir_list()
    
        for dir in dirlist:
            if dir != _os.curdir:
                dir = _os.path.abspath(dir)
            # Try only a few names per directory.
            for seq in range(100):
                name = next(namer)
                filename = _os.path.join(dir, name)
                try:
                    fd = _os.open(filename, _bin_openflags, 0o600)
                    try:
                        try:
                            _os.write(fd, b'blat')
                        finally:
                            _os.close(fd)
                    finally:
                        _os.unlink(filename)
                    return dir
                except FileExistsError:
                    pass
                except PermissionError:
                    # This exception is thrown when a directory with the chosen name
                    # already exists on windows.
                    if (_os.name == 'nt' and _os.path.isdir(dir) and
                        _os.access(dir, _os.W_OK)):
                        continue
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
                except OSError:
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
>       raise FileNotFoundError(_errno.ENOENT,
                                "No usable temporary directory found in %s" %

    def _get_default_tempdir():
        """Calculate the default directory to use for temporary files.
        This routine should be called exactly once.
    
        We determine whether or not a candidate temp dir is usable by
        trying to create and write to a file in that directory.  If this
        is successful, the test file is deleted.  To prevent denial of
        service, the name of the test file must be randomized."""
    
        namer = _RandomNameSequence()
        dirlist = _candidate_tempdir_list()
    
        for dir in dirlist:
            if dir != _os.curdir:
                dir = _os.path.abspath(dir)
            # Try only a few names per directory.
            for seq in range(100):
                name = next(namer)
                filename = _os.path.join(dir, name)
                try:
                    fd = _os.open(filename, _bin_openflags, 0o600)
                    try:
                        try:
                            _os.write(fd, b'blat')
                        finally:
                            _os.close(fd)
                    finally:
                        _os.unlink(filename)
                    return dir
                except FileExistsError:
                    pass
                except PermissionError:
                    # This exception is thrown when a directory with the chosen name
                    # already exists on windows.
                    if (_os.name == 'nt' and _os.path.isdir(dir) and
                        _os.access(dir, _os.W_OK)):
                        continue
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
                except OSError:
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
>       raise FileNotFoundError(_errno.ENOENT,
                                "No usable temporary directory found in %s" %
                                dirlist)

    def _get_default_tempdir():
        """Calculate the default directory to use for temporary files.
        This routine should be called exactly once.
    
        We determine whether or not a candidate temp dir is usable by
        trying to create and write to a file in that directory.  If this
        is successful, the test file is deleted.  To prevent denial of
        service, the name of the test file must be randomized."""
    
        namer = _RandomNameSequence()
        dirlist = _candidate_tempdir_list()
    
        for dir in dirlist:
            if dir != _os.curdir:
                dir = _os.path.abspath(dir)
            # Try only a few names per directory.
            for seq in range(100):
                name = next(namer)
                filename = _os.path.join(dir, name)
                try:
                    fd = _os.open(filename, _bin_openflags, 0o600)
                    try:
                        try:
                            _os.write(fd, b'blat')
                        finally:
                            _os.close(fd)
                    finally:
                        _os.unlink(filename)
                    return dir
                except FileExistsError:
                    pass
                except PermissionError:
                    # This exception is thrown when a directory with the chosen name
                    # already exists on windows.
                    if (_os.name == 'nt' and _os.path.isdir(dir) and
                        _os.access(dir, _os.W_OK)):
                        continue
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
                except OSError:
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory

    def test_pooled_floor_uses_leak_noise_not_gain_noise(self):

        Constructed so the two differ starkly and in the direction that mattered: the extended

    def _get_default_tempdir():
        """Calculate the default directory to use for temporary files.
        This routine should be called exactly once.
    
        We determine whether or not a candidate temp dir is usable by
        trying to create and write to a file in that directory.  If this
        is successful, the test file is deleted.  To prevent denial of
        service, the name of the test file must be randomized."""
    
        namer = _RandomNameSequence()
        dirlist = _candidate_tempdir_list()
    
        for dir in dirlist:
            if dir != _os.curdir:
                dir = _os.path.abspath(dir)
            # Try only a few names per directory.
            for seq in range(100):
                name = next(namer)
                filename = _os.path.join(dir, name)
                try:
                    fd = _os.open(filename, _bin_openflags, 0o600)
                    try:
                        try:
                            _os.write(fd, b'blat')
                        finally:
                            _os.close(fd)
                    finally:
                        _os.unlink(filename)
                    return dir
                except FileExistsError:
                    pass
                except PermissionError:
                    # This exception is thrown when a directory with the chosen name
                    # already exists on windows.
                    if (_os.name == 'nt' and _os.path.isdir(dir) and
                        _os.access(dir, _os.W_OK)):
                        continue
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
                except OSError:
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
>       raise FileNotFoundError(_errno.ENOENT,
                                "No usable temporary directory found in %s" %
                                dirlist)
E       FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No usable temporary directory found in ['/var/folders/gn/_qj5k2lj0cgfdp5p263yqcm80000gn/T/', '/tmp', '/var/tmp', '/usr/tmp', '/Users/josephbailey/local-research/MINERvA-OmniFold/.claude/worktrees/gbdt-closeout']

    def test_two_files_one_seed_is_rejected(self):

    def test_undertrained_extended_arm_invalidates_the_point(self):
        """gain = extended - leak collapses whether the leak rose or the extended arm died.
    
        The driver's positive control runs the BASE arm, so it passes in both cases. Without this
        gate the second reads as a real crossing.
        """
        broken = three_points()
        broken[3] = point(2.0, corr=0.60, leak=0.360, extended=0.10)   # control still fine
        other = three_points(0.002)
        other[3] = point(2.0, corr=0.60, leak=0.362, extended=0.10)
>       out = self.summarize([run_file(0, broken), run_file(7, other)])

    def _get_default_tempdir():
        """Calculate the default directory to use for temporary files.
        This routine should be called exactly once.
    
        We determine whether or not a candidate temp dir is usable by
        trying to create and write to a file in that directory.  If this
        is successful, the test file is deleted.  To prevent denial of
        service, the name of the test file must be randomized."""
    
        namer = _RandomNameSequence()
        dirlist = _candidate_tempdir_list()
    
        for dir in dirlist:
            if dir != _os.curdir:
                dir = _os.path.abspath(dir)
            # Try only a few names per directory.
            for seq in range(100):
                name = next(namer)
                filename = _os.path.join(dir, name)
                try:
                    fd = _os.open(filename, _bin_openflags, 0o600)
                    try:
                        try:
                            _os.write(fd, b'blat')
                        finally:
                            _os.close(fd)
                    finally:
                        _os.unlink(filename)
                    return dir
                except FileExistsError:
                    pass
                except PermissionError:
                    # This exception is thrown when a directory with the chosen name
                    # already exists on windows.

                        _os.access(dir, _os.W_OK)):
                        continue
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory

                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory

    def test_cli_pub_builder_receipt_gate_still_closes_when_endpoints_valid():
        """Ordering guard, paired with test_cli_pub_builder_aggregates_missing.
    
        That test proves ten ABSENT outputs report "negweight output missing" rather than
        the downstream "receipt: required file absent: COMPLETE" symptom -- i.e. that the
        merged-input receipt gate is resolved lazily, below PASS 1. This test proves the
        gate was only DEFERRED, not weakened: with all ten outputs present and their
        configs valid, the builder must still refuse to emit a manifest.
    
        Together they pin the ordering from both sides. Hoisting fvm.verify() back above
        PASS 1 breaks the other test; deleting the gate breaks this one.
    
        Deliberately platform-portable. fps_verify_merged_receipt.REPO is a hardcoded
        /pscratch literal, so verify() RAISES off-Perlmutter ("required file absent") but
        SUCCEEDS on Perlmutter, where the empty temp --merged-dir then fails the receipt
        membership check instead ("merged input not in validated receipt"). Both are the
        gate doing its job, so either message satisfies this test; what must hold on every
        platform is that no manifest is written and that aggregation did not short-circuit.
        """
>       d = tempfile.mkdtemp()

    def _get_default_tempdir():
        """Calculate the default directory to use for temporary files.
        This routine should be called exactly once.
    
        We determine whether or not a candidate temp dir is usable by
        trying to create and write to a file in that directory.  If this
        is successful, the test file is deleted.  To prevent denial of
        service, the name of the test file must be randomized."""
    
        namer = _RandomNameSequence()
        dirlist = _candidate_tempdir_list()
    
        for dir in dirlist:
            if dir != _os.curdir:
                dir = _os.path.abspath(dir)
            # Try only a few names per directory.
            for seq in range(100):
                name = next(namer)
                filename = _os.path.join(dir, name)
                try:
                    fd = _os.open(filename, _bin_openflags, 0o600)
                    try:
                        try:
                            _os.write(fd, b'blat')
                        finally:
                            _os.close(fd)
                    finally:
                        _os.unlink(filename)
                    return dir
                except FileExistsError:
                    pass
                except PermissionError:
                    # This exception is thrown when a directory with the chosen name
                    # already exists on windows.
                    if (_os.name == 'nt' and _os.path.isdir(dir) and
                        _os.access(dir, _os.W_OK)):
                        continue
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
                except OSError:
                    break   # no point trying more names in this directory
>       raise FileNotFoundError(_errno.ENOENT,
                                "No usable temporary directory found in %s" %
                                dirlist)
