   228	## 2f. DRAFT — reported estimator dependence (for the note, pending Joseph's review)
   229	
   230	Written against the outcome the test actually produced. **This is a draft, not a landed claim**, and
   231	it deliberately does not assert a mechanism.
   232	
   233	> **Estimator dependence of the 4D result.** The 4D cross section is reported as the exact
   234	> marginal of the 5D unfold over W. An independent direct 4D unfold, retained as a cross-check,
   235	> agrees with that marginal in normalisation to **0.56 %** (integral ratio 1.005578) but differs
   236	> bin-by-bin at a **median of 4.4 %** (p90 20.8 %, p99 33.9 %, max 72.8 %; 3009 of 4825 reported
   237	> bins above 3 %). The difference is **not** a statistical fluctuation of either unfold — it is
   238	> uncorrelated with bin content (Spearman +0.06) — and is **structured**: the signed difference
   239	> swings from −9.1 % to +4.3 % across `E_avail` and from +9.8 % to −9.2 % across `q3`, while
   240	> remaining flat at −2 to −3 % across `p_T` and `p_z`.
   241	>
   242	> We tested and excluded the natural explanation that a 4D unfold mixes W-populations with
   243	> differing migration: the difference *falls* with the number of W bins a 4D cell spans
   244	> (Spearman −0.22), and W-width varies most strongly along `p_T`, the axis on which the difference
   245	> is flattest. W is in any case largely determined by `(E_avail, q3)` — 69 % of reported 4D cells
   246	> span two or fewer W bins — leaving little W-mixing for a 4D unfold to misestimate. A
   247	> phase-space-boundary effect is also excluded (edge cells agree better than interior cells).
   248	>
   249	> We therefore report this as an **unexplained estimator dependence of the 4D shape**, not as a
   250	> quantified bias of either estimator, and we note that it is concentrated in the `(E_avail, q3)`
   251	> region where the data-minus-generator excess is reported. The marginal is quoted because the 4D
   252	> result is *defined* as the 5D marginal; the size of this dependence is a systematic-adjacent
   253	> uncertainty on any 4D shape statement and is reported in full rather than summarised by a
   254	> single number.
   255	
   256	**Open, and it should be flagged as open:** whether this dependence should enter the 4D shape
   257	uncertainty budget, and whether the `(E_avail, W)` excess claim needs a corresponding statement.
   258	`app_statmethods.tex` already argues that a coherent 1–2 % OmniFold-vs-IBU shape difference becomes
   259	a large χ² in this region; a 4.4 % median estimator dependence is larger than that and sits in the
   260	same place.
   261	
   262	## 3. Why this is a specification question, not a bug to fix
   263	
   264	**The gate encodes the opposite of the convention adopted 2026-08-07.** That decision — pre-settled
   265	and explicitly not to be reopened — is that **4D is the exact 5D→4D marginal, and the independent
   266	4D unfold is a cross-check.** Under that convention the marginal is *definitional*: it is the
   267	answer, and there is nothing for it to reproduce. This gate instead treats the independent 4D as
   268	ground truth and the marginal as a candidate that must match it, which is the convention we did
   269	not adopt.
   270	
   271	The gate predates the decision. Nothing was wrong with writing it then; it simply was never
   272	revisited, and because stages 4-6 never ran, nothing forced the contradiction into the open.
   273	
   274	**Two readings, and I am not choosing between them:**
   275	
   276	1. *The gate is mis-specified.* Under the adopted convention it should not exist in this form —
   277	   at most it should RECORD the marginal-vs-independent difference as a cross-check statistic,
   278	   with a bar set from what two OmniFold estimators at different dimensionality are actually
   279	   expected to agree to, which is plainly not 3 % per bin.
   280	2. *The disagreement is itself worth attention.* Median 4.4 % / p90 21 % between the deliverable
   281	   and its cross-check is a real number about the analysis, whichever way the convention falls,
   282	   and it has not been quoted anywhere before because this comparison had never run.
   283	
   284	Both may be true. **Raising the tolerance is not on the table** — a 3 % gate that fails at a median
   285	of 4.4 % is not repaired by widening it to 100 %, and "never raise a tolerance to clear a
   286	mismatch" is a standing rule on this campaign.
   287	
   288	## 4. A separate, smaller defect in the same stage
   289	
   290	`p4_lib.build_projection_M` checks coverage in **one direction only**: every reported 5D bin must
   291	map to a reported 4D bin (`"high reported bin {g} maps to non-reported low bin {glow}"`). It never
   292	checks the converse — that every reported 4D bin receives at least one 5D contributor. Hence the
   293	5 orphan bins, which reach the central check as exact zeros and produce a `rel = 1.0` that
   294	completely masks the 62 %-of-bins result behind it.
   295	
   296	This is independent of the convention question and is a defect either way: a one-directional
   297	coverage guard on a bijection-shaped requirement. The right form fails at `build_projection_M`
   298	with the count and the identity of the orphan bins, rather than surfacing 4 830 bins later as a
   299	single misleading `max rel`.
   300	
   301	**Rule.** When a guard reports `max`, the maximum is chosen by the worst bin, and a handful of
   302	degenerate bins will always win it. Report a distribution — median, p90, count-over-tolerance —
   303	beside any max, or the max becomes a mask for the finding. Here the max said "one bin is 100 %
   304	off" when the truth was "62 % of bins are over tolerance".
   305

   322	## 6. The re-specification, as landed 2026-08-09
   323	
   324	`check_projection_nonmutation` is replaced by two functions with disjoint jobs:
   325	
   326	- **`check_projection_validity(C_high, M)` — GATE.** Symmetry, PSD, and `M C M^T` against a direct
   327	  block-sum recomputation at `1e-9`. All recomputation identities; nothing compares against a
   328	  separately-produced product. The block-sum leg is not a restatement of the PSD leg: `project()`
   329	  is one matrix expression and a bug in it yields a matrix that is still symmetric and still PSD,
   330	  so an independent route is what makes it a check.
   331	- **`crosscheck_marginal_vs_independent(M, x_high, x_indep)` — REPORT, no pass/fail.** Returns
   332	  median, p90, p99, max, sign fraction, signed mean, integral ratio and counts over 3/10/20 %, and
   333	  is written so it cannot raise. Tested on a comparison the retired 3 % gate would have rejected.
   334	
   335	`CENTRAL_REL` is **deleted, not raised.** There is deliberately no tolerance constant left to
   336	re-tune, because the correct value is *none*, not *larger*.
   337

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Endpoint-receipt gate for run_p4_unfold_std.sh's resume path (repair-4, verifier defect 2).
     3	
     4	Exit 0 iff the receipt is complete and every recorded identity matches the live/committed one;
     5	otherwise print `RECEIPT-REJECT :: <reason>` and exit 1, which makes the launcher re-run the
     6	endpoint transactionally instead of skipping it.
     7	
     8	Deliberately a separate CLI rather than inline `python3 -c` in the launcher: the previous skip
     9	logic was an unreadable one-liner, and a gate that cannot be unit-tested is the defect this
    10	whole repair round exists to remove. ROOT-free -- content validity of the ROOT itself is the
    11	launcher's `valid_root`, this is the provenance half.
    12	
    13	Usage:
    14	  p4_check_receipt.py --receipt R.done --tag BAND_EP --root OUT.root --merged MERGED.root
    15	"""
    16	import argparse, json, os, sys
    17	
    18	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    19	import p4_lib as P
    20	
    21	REPO = P.REPO_ROOT
    22	ND = P.ND_ROOT
    23	CEN5 = f"{ND}/products/5d/xsec_5d_MEFHC_5iter_lgbm.root"
    24	RECDIR = f"{REPO}/docs/orchestration/state/merged-input-hashes/p4-merged-20260718"
    25	UNFOLD_SRC = "nd-unfolding/unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py"
    26	
    27	
    28	def committed_unfold_blob():
    29	    """The unfold driver's blob AS COMMITTED at HEAD (repair-5, defect 2).
    30	
    31	    The receipt gate previously required `code_rev` to be a non-empty string and compared it to
    32	    nothing, and recorded no source identity at all -- so an endpoint produced under a changed
    33	    driver was still skipped. Both are now compared, and this is the value they compare against.
    34	    Fails closed (returns None -> caller rejects) rather than guessing."""
    35	    import subprocess
    36	    try:
    37	        return subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", f"HEAD:{UNFOLD_SRC}"],
    38	                                       cwd=REPO, text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
    39	    except Exception:
    40	        return None
    41	
    42	
    43	def current_code_rev():
    44	    import subprocess
    45	    try:
    46	        return subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    47	                                       cwd=REPO, text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
    48	    except Exception:
    49	        return None
    50	
    51	
    52	def committed_merged_sha(merged_path):
    53	    """The orchestrator receipt's committed hash for this merged file, after its own live
    54	    size+integer-mtime check. Never re-hashes 53.8 GB."""
    55	    live = {}
    56	    for b in P.BANDS:
    57	        for ep in P.ENDPOINTS:
    58	            rel = (f"nd-unfolding/active_universe_5d/standard/merged/"
    59	                   f"runEventLoopOmniFold_5D_MEFHC_active_{b}_{ep}.root")
    60	            ap = f"{REPO}/{rel}"
    61	            st = os.stat(ap)
    62	            live[rel] = (st.st_size, int(st.st_mtime))
    63	    rec = P.validate_orchestrator_merged_receipt(RECDIR, live)
    64	    base = os.path.basename(merged_path)
    65	    for p, h in rec["merged_sha256"].items():
    66	        if os.path.basename(p) == base:
    67	            return h
    68	    raise P.P4GateError(f"{base} not in the orchestrator merged receipt")

    71	def main():
    72	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    73	    ap.add_argument("--receipt", required=True)
    74	    ap.add_argument("--tag", required=True)
    75	    ap.add_argument("--root", required=True)
    76	    ap.add_argument("--merged", required=True)
    77	    a = ap.parse_args()
    78	    try:
    79	        if not os.path.exists(a.receipt) or os.path.getsize(a.receipt) == 0:
    80	            raise P.P4GateError("receipt absent or empty")
    81	        try:
    82	            rec = json.load(open(a.receipt))
    83	        except Exception as e:
    84	            raise P.P4GateError(f"receipt is not valid JSON ({e})")
    85	        cfg = P.P4Config(); cfg.validate()
    86	        blob, rev = committed_unfold_blob(), current_code_rev()
    87	        if not blob:
    88	            raise P.P4GateError(f"cannot resolve the committed blob of {UNFOLD_SRC}; refusing to "
    89	                                f"accept a receipt whose producing source cannot be checked")
    90	        if not rev:
    91	            raise P.P4GateError("cannot resolve HEAD; refusing to accept a receipt whose "
    92	                                "code_rev cannot be compared")
    93	        P.validate_endpoint_receipt(
    94	            rec, tag=a.tag,
    95	            root_sha256=P.sha256_file(a.root),
    96	            merged_sha256=committed_merged_sha(a.merged),
    97	            central5d_sha256=P.sha256_file(CEN5),
    98	            config_hash=cfg.hash(),
    99	            bkg_mode=cfg.bkg_mode,
   100	            code_rev=rev,
   101	            unfold_blob=blob)
   102	    except P.P4GateError as e:
   103	        print(f"RECEIPT-REJECT :: {e}"); sys.exit(1)
   104	    except Exception as e:                      # never let an unexpected error read as PASS
   105	        print(f"RECEIPT-REJECT :: unexpected {type(e).__name__}: {e}"); sys.exit(1)
   106	    print(f"RECEIPT-OK :: {a.tag}")
   107	    sys.exit(0)
   108

   155	        P.require(stat_spec and ml_spec, "component manifest does not bind the stat/ML blocks")
   156	
   157	        def _bound_block(spec, sha_key, label):
   158	            """Load a `path:key` block AFTER re-verifying the sha256 the manifest recorded, so
   159	            the identity cannot be satisfied by substituting a different file."""
   160	            P.require(":" in spec, f"{label} spec {spec!r} is not path:key")
   161	            pth, key = spec.rsplit(":", 1)
   162	            ap = pth if os.path.isabs(pth) else os.path.join(P.ND_ROOT, pth)
   163	            P.require(os.path.exists(ap), f"{label} covariance not found: {pth}")
   164	            P.require(P.sha256_file(ap) == comp.get(sha_key),
   165	                      f"{label} covariance sha256 drift vs the component manifest ({pth})")
   166	            blk = _th2(ap, key)
   167	            P.require(blk is not None, f"{label} covariance key {key} missing in {pth}")
   168	            return blk
   169	
   170	        C_stat = _bound_block(stat_spec, "stat_sha256", "stat")
   171	        C_ml = _bound_block(ml_spec, "ml_sha256", "ML")
   172	        out["full_total_identity_relerr"] = float(
   173	            P.check_full_total_identity(Ccomb, Csyst, C_stat, C_ml, 1e-9))
   174	        out["gates"].append("full_total_identity_recomputed")
   175	
   176	        # REPAIR-6: C_syst itself was never recomputed. The builder recorded
   177	        # C_syst_eq_retained_plus_active_relerr and NEITHER consumer read it, so a wrong-but-PSD
   178	        # C_syst satisfying C_combined = C_syst + C_stat + C_ML passed every gate. It is
   179	        # recomputable because repair-4 (4a) started persisting the retained components into the
   180	        # candidate -- which made the omission worse, not better.
   181	        retained_keys = [k for k in comp.get("candidate_keys", [])
   182	                         if k.startswith("hCov_retained5d_")]
   183	        P.require(retained_keys,
   184	                  "candidate persists no retained components, so C_syst cannot be recomputed "
   185	                  "(pre-repair-4 candidate?)")
   186	        retained_sum = None
   187	        for k in retained_keys:
   188	            blk = _th2(a.candidate, k)
   189	            P.require(blk is not None, f"candidate is missing declared retained component {k}")
   190	            retained_sum = blk if retained_sum is None else retained_sum + blk
   191	        active_total_blk = _th2(a.candidate, P.CANDIDATE_ACTIVE_TOTAL_KEY)
   192	        out["c_syst_identity_relerr"] = float(
   193	            P.prove_identity(Csyst, retained_sum + active_total_blk, 1e-9,
   194	                             "C_syst == sum(retained) + active_total"))
   195	        out["n_retained_components"] = len(retained_keys)
   196	        out["gates"].append("c_syst_recomputed_from_components")
   197	        support_bands = {b: _th2(a.support, f"hCov_universe5d_{b}") for b in P.BANDS}
   198	        P.require(all(support_bands[b] is not None for b in P.BANDS), "support family lateral block incomplete")
   199	        out["support_comparison"] = P.check_support_comparison(active_total, sum(support_bands[b] for b in P.BANDS))
   200	        # REPAIR-6: relabelled. The check compares TRACES and bounds nothing -- any finite ratio
   201	        # passes -- so calling it "complete" claimed more than it delivers, and BEN-043 rule 3
   202	        # adds that an aggregate cannot see a per-bin disagreement that preserves the trace.
   203	        # The ratio stays as a recorded DIAGNOSTIC; the gate name no longer asserts a comparison.
   204	        out["support_ratio_is_diagnostic_not_bounded"] = True
   205	        out["gates"].append("support_trace_ratio_recorded")
   206	        out["result"] = "PASS"
   207	    except P.P4GateError as e:
   208	        out["error"] = str(e); json.dump(out, open(a.out, "w"), indent=2)
   209	        print(f"RESULT FAIL :: {e}"); sys.exit(1)
   210	    json.dump(out, open(a.out, "w"), indent=2)
   211	    print("RESULT PASS — gates:", ",".join(out["gates"]),
   212	          f"support_ratio={out['support_comparison']['ratio']:.3f}")
   213	    sys.exit(0)

   130	    for b in retained:
   131	        Csyst_active = Csyst_active + comp[b]
   132	    Csyst_active = Csyst_active + active_only
   133	    Ccomb_active = Csyst_active + C_stat + C_ml
   134	    # identity gates: active-only == sum(5 active); full == retained + active + stat + ml
   135	    _err_active5 = P.check_component_sum(active_only, active)           # exactly 5 bands
   136	    full_check = sum(comp[b] for b in retained) + active_only + C_stat + C_ml
   137	    _err_full = P.prove_identity(Ccomb_active, full_check, 1e-9,
   138	                                 "candidate full == retained + active + stat + ML")
   139	    # repair-5 (pattern sweep): also prove the identity a DOWNSTREAM reader can re-derive from
   140	    # the candidate plus the stat/ML blocks, and record its measured error rather than a
   141	    # literal True. See the identities block below.
   142	    _err_syst = P.prove_identity(Csyst_active,
   143	                                 sum(comp[b] for b in retained) + active_only, 1e-9,
   144	                                 "C_syst == retained + active")
   145	    _err_fulltotal = P.check_full_total_identity(Ccomb_active, Csyst_active, C_stat, C_ml, 1e-9)
   146	    P.check_symmetric_psd(Csyst_active); P.check_symmetric_psd(Ccomb_active)

   148	    prov = {"support_family": a.support_family, "support_family_sha256": P.sha256_file(a.support_family),
   149	            "stat_cov": a.stat_cov, "stat_sha256": P.sha256_file(sp),
   150	            "ml_cov": a.ml_cov, "ml_sha256": P.sha256_file(mp),
   151	            "all_syst_bands": all_bands, "retained_bands": retained,
   152	            "replaced_lateral_bands": sorted(SUPPORT_LATERAL),
   153	            "component_content_hash": comp_hash, "active_traces": {b: float(np.trace(active[b])) for b in P.BANDS},
   154	            "manifest": a.manifest, "manifest_endpoint_hash": man.get("endpoint_manifest_hash"),
   155	            "reported_mask_hash": man["mask5d_hash"], "n_reported": man["mask5d_nreported"],
   156	            # repair-5 (pattern sweep: "assert presence, never compare"). These four were
   157	            # written as LITERAL `True` -- the proofs ran just above, but the recorded values
   158	            # were constants, so a consumer reading the manifest learned nothing. Two consumers
   159	            # then tested `pure_addition` for truthiness (p4_validate_active_lateral.py and
   160	            # p4_adopt_standard.py), i.e. read a literal and treated it as evidence: a closed
   161	            # loop of self-assertion, the same shape as the P4_VERIFIER_PASS non-emptiness gate
   162	            # (KNOWN_ISSUES #21). Now each records the MEASURED max-relative error from the
   163	            # gate that produced it, and downstream must recompute rather than read.
   164	            "identities": {"active_only_eq_sum5_relerr": float(_err_active5),
   165	                           "C_syst_eq_retained_plus_active_relerr": float(_err_syst),
   166	                           "C_combined_eq_syst_stat_ml_relerr": float(_err_full),
   167	                           "full_total_residual_eq_stat_plus_ml_relerr": float(_err_fulltotal),
   168	                           "identity_rtol": 1e-9,
   169	                           "note": ("measured errors, not assertions; a consumer must RECOMPUTE "
   170	                                    "these from the candidate + stat/ML blocks, not read them")}}
   171	    # repair-4 (defect 4b): the manifest used to be written HERE, before the candidate ROOT
   172	    # existed and with no candidate hash in it -- so a manifest could describe a candidate that
   173	    # was never completed, and nothing bound the two. Inverted below: candidate first, then the
   174	    # manifest LAST carrying the candidate's sha256 and key inventory. Same receipt-last
   175	    # discipline the unfold launcher already uses.
   176	    import ROOT
   177	    n = Ccomb_active.shape[0]; fo = ROOT.TFile.Open(a.out, "RECREATE")
   178	    def wr(name, C, title):
   179	        h = ROOT.TH2D(name, title, n, 0, n, n, 0, n)
   180	        h.SetContent(np.ascontiguousarray(np.pad(C, 1)[0:n + 2, 0:n + 2], dtype=np.float64).ravel())
   181	        h.Write()
   182	    # repair-4 (D4a): the candidate persisted only the five active blocks and three totals, so
   183	    # the RETAINED non-lateral components -- the other half of C_syst, and the half the reader
   184	    # cannot recompute -- existed only as a claim in the manifest. A consumer could not
   185	    # reproduce C_syst from the file it was handed. Every retained pure component is now
   186	    # written, which is also what makes the validator's component-sum check meaningful.
   187	    for b in retained:
   188	        wr(f"hCov_retained5d_{b}", comp[b], f"retained non-lateral component {b}")
   189	    # repair-4 (D1c): key names come from p4_lib so the driver cannot name a key nothing writes
   190	    for b in P.BANDS:
   191	        wr(P.candidate_band_key(b), active[b], f"active MAT band {b}")
   192	    wr(P.CANDIDATE_ACTIVE_TOTAL_KEY, active_only, "active-only total (sum of 5 MAT bands)")
   193	    wr(P.CANDIDATE_SYST_KEY, Csyst_active, "candidate C_syst (retained + active)")
   194	    wr(P.CANDIDATE_TOTAL_KEY, Ccomb_active, "candidate full total (C_syst + stat + ML)")
   195	    fo.Close()
   196	    # candidate is now published; bind it into the manifest and write that LAST
   197	    written_keys = ([f"hCov_retained5d_{b}" for b in retained]
   198	                    + [P.candidate_band_key(b) for b in P.BANDS]
   199	                    + [P.CANDIDATE_ACTIVE_TOTAL_KEY, P.CANDIDATE_SYST_KEY, P.CANDIDATE_TOTAL_KEY])
   200	    # Self-declaring rejection when built without a verifier PASS; see p4_lib for the pattern
   201	    # and why the consumer's truthiness test is the correct shape here.
   202	    P.stamp_non_adoptable(prov)
   203	    prov["candidate"] = os.path.abspath(a.out)
   204	    prov["candidate_sha256"] = P.sha256_file(a.out)
   205	    prov["candidate_keys"] = written_keys
   206	    prov["candidate_total_key"] = P.CANDIDATE_TOTAL_KEY
   207	    tmp_manifest = a.out_manifest + ".tmp"
   208	    json.dump(prov, open(tmp_manifest, "w"), indent=2)
   209	    os.replace(tmp_manifest, a.out_manifest)        # atomic; manifest-last
   210	    print(f"CANDIDATE {a.out}: sqrt_tr_syst={np.sqrt(max(0,np.trace(Csyst_active))):.4e} "
   211	          f"sqrt_tr_full={np.sqrt(max(0,np.trace(Ccomb_active))):.4e} bands={len(all_bands)} "
   212	          f"retained={len(retained)}; prov -> {a.out_manifest}")
   213	    sys.exit(0)

   505	                         "config_hash", "bkg_mode", "code_rev", "unfold_blob", "t")
   506	# The source whose blob decides whether a cached endpoint is still valid. The unfold driver is
   507	# the one that actually produces the ROOT; the others in p4_evidence.SRC describe downstream

   514	# covered have not changed between the reviewed commit and HEAD.
   515	# REPAIR-7 item 2. This was drawn by FILENAME PREFIX, which is a proxy, and it omitted every
   516	# module the chain actually executes -- uq_math, project_cov_nd, unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned,
   517	# xsec_nd, omnifold. A verdict could therefore authorize materially changed execution code.
   518	# Third instance of the corpus-definition error, so the surface is now DERIVED from the import
   519	# graph rather than curated, and a test asserts the previously-missing modules are in it.
   520	STANDARD_P4_SURFACE_GLOBS = (

   522	    "nd-unfolding/run_p4_*.sh",

   535	# Where first-party imports may resolve. Anything outside these is a third-party dependency and

   540	def standard_p4_execution_surface(entrypoints=None, max_depth=6):
   541	    """Every tracked first-party module reachable from the chain's entrypoints, by IMPORT.
   542	
   543	    Derived, not curated: the previous surface was a filename-prefix glob and silently omitted
   544	    the modules that do the work. Falls back to the glob surface if git is unavailable, and the
   545	    caller must treat an empty result as a refusal rather than an empty scope."""
   546	    import ast
   547	    tracked = set()
   548	    try:
   549	        tracked = set(subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files"], cwd=REPO_ROOT,
   550	                                              text=True).splitlines())
   551	    except Exception:
   552	        return sorted(tracked_files_matching(STANDARD_P4_SURFACE_GLOBS))
   553	
   554	    def resolve(mod):
   555	        for d in _IMPORT_SEARCH_DIRS:
   556	            cand = f"{d}/{mod.replace('.', '/')}.py".lstrip("./")
   557	            if cand in tracked:
   558	                return cand
   559	        return None
   560	
   561	    seen, frontier = set(), list(entrypoints or STANDARD_P4_ENTRYPOINTS)
   562	    for _ in range(max_depth):
   563	        nxt = []
   564	        for rel in frontier:
   565	            if rel in seen or rel not in tracked:
   566	                continue
   567	            seen.add(rel)
   568	            try:
   569	                tree = ast.parse((REPO_ROOT_PATH / rel).read_text(errors="replace"))
   570	            except Exception:
   571	                continue
   572	            for node in ast.walk(tree):
   573	                names = []
   574	                if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
   575	                    names = [a.name for a in node.names]
   576	                elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module and node.level == 0:
   577	                    names = [node.module]
   578	                for n in names:
   579	                    r = resolve(n)
   580	                    if r and r not in seen:
   581	                        nxt.append(r)
   582	        if not nxt:
   583	            break
   584	        frontier = nxt
   585	    # the shell drivers are executed, not imported, so add them explicitly
   586	    seen.update(p for p in tracked if p.startswith("nd-unfolding/run_p4_") and p.endswith(".sh"))
   587	    return sorted(seen)
   588

   590	def tracked_files_matching(globs, rev="HEAD"):
   591	    """Tracked paths at `rev` matching any glob. Sorted, so the result is order-stable."""
   592	    out = set()
   593	    for g in globs:
   594	        try:
   595	            r = subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", rev],
   635	    try:
   636	        subprocess.check_call(["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", rev.strip(), head or "HEAD"],
   637	                              cwd=REPO_ROOT, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
   638	        return True
   639	    except Exception:
   640	        return False

   643	def validate_endpoint_receipt(rec, *, tag, root_sha256, merged_sha256,
   644	                              central5d_sha256, config_hash, bkg_mode,
   645	                              code_rev, unfold_blob):
   646	    """Fail closed unless the receipt is complete AND every recorded identity matches the
   647	    live/committed one. Returns True, or raises P4GateError naming the first mismatch.
   648	
   649	    REPAIR-5 (defect 2). The previous version required `code_rev` to be a NON-EMPTY STRING and
   650	    compared it to nothing, and the receipt recorded no source identity at all -- so an
   651	    endpoint produced under a changed unfold driver was still skipped. That is the third
   652	    instance in this chain of "assert presence, never compare": the first is the
   653	    `P4_VERIFIER_PASS` non-emptiness gate (KNOWN_ISSUES #21), the second is the `identities`
   654	    block whose members were literal `True`. Presence is not evidence; both `code_rev` and the
   655	    producing driver's committed blob are now COMPARED."""
   656	    require(isinstance(rec, dict) and rec, f"receipt for {tag} is not a JSON object")
   657	    missing = [k for k in RECEIPT_REQUIRED_KEYS if k not in rec]
   658	    require(not missing, f"receipt {tag} missing required keys {missing} (incomplete legacy format)")
   659	    require(rec["mode"] in RECEIPT_MODES, f"receipt {tag} unknown mode {rec['mode']!r}")
   660	    require(rec["tag"] == tag, f"receipt tag {rec['tag']!r} != {tag!r} (receipt/ROOT pair mismatch)")
   661	    require(rec["root_sha256"] == root_sha256,
   662	            f"receipt {tag} root_sha256 drift: recorded {rec['root_sha256']} vs live {root_sha256}")
   663	    require(rec["merged_sha256"] == merged_sha256,
   664	            f"receipt {tag} merged_sha256 drift vs the orchestrator receipt")
   665	    require(rec["central5d_sha256"] == central5d_sha256,
   666	            f"receipt {tag} central5d_sha256 drift (the central moved under this endpoint)")
   667	    require(rec["config_hash"] == config_hash,
   668	            f"receipt {tag} config_hash drift: produced under a different unfold configuration")
   669	    require(rec["bkg_mode"] == bkg_mode,
   670	            f"receipt {tag} bkg_mode {rec['bkg_mode']!r} != declared {bkg_mode!r}")
   671	    # D2: compared, not merely present.
   672	    require(isinstance(rec["code_rev"], str) and rec["code_rev"],
   673	            f"receipt {tag} has no code_rev")
   674	    require(isinstance(code_rev, str) and code_rev,
   675	            f"cannot validate receipt {tag}: no live code_rev to compare against")
   676	    # REPAIR-6b. This used to require code_rev == HEAD, and that was WRONG in the same way
   677	    # KNOWN_ISSUES #24 describes: it broke on correct behaviour. Any commit anywhere in the repo
   678	    # -- including another lane's, touching nothing this chain reads -- expired all ten receipts
   679	    # while the code that produced them was byte-identical. Caught by the self-check on the first
   680	    # production run: the PET lane advanced main by 8 commits mid-run, HEAD moved
   681	    # 42268b6 -> 203ff01, `git diff` on the unfold driver was EMPTY, and the gate rejected all ten.
   682	    #
   683	    # The producing-code binding is `unfold_blob`, which IS strictly compared below. `code_rev` is
   684	    # repository context, so the honest check is REACHABILITY, not equality: the receipt must come
   685	    # from this history. That still catches a receipt carried in from a foreign branch or a
   686	    # rewritten history, and does not expire on unrelated work.
   687	    require(code_rev_in_history(rec["code_rev"]),
   688	            f"receipt {tag} code_rev {rec['code_rev']} is not an ancestor of HEAD ({code_rev}): "
   689	            f"this receipt did not come from this repository's history")
   690	    require(isinstance(unfold_blob, str) and unfold_blob,
   691	            f"cannot validate receipt {tag}: no committed unfold-driver blob to compare against")
   692	    require(rec[RECEIPT_SOURCE_KEY] == unfold_blob,
   693	            f"receipt {tag} unfold_blob {rec[RECEIPT_SOURCE_KEY]} != committed {unfold_blob}: the "
   694	            f"unfold driver changed since this endpoint was produced")
   695	    return True

   698	def cmask_order_hash_4d(mask):
   699	    """4D reported-mask + C-order fingerprint (repair-4, defect 5c).
   700

   538	class REPAIR7_EndpointContentReproduction(unittest.TestCase):
   539	    """REPAIR-7 item 1: the frozen endpoint-manifest hash is replaced by content comparison.
   540	
   541	    Joseph's success criterion, stated as two tests rather than one: **a legitimate re-unfold
   542	    PASSES and a semantics change FAILS.** A gate that only demonstrates one direction is the
   543	    failure mode this lane has hit repeatedly."""
   544	
   545	    def _endpoint(self, n=10694, seed=0):
   546	        return np.random.default_rng(seed).uniform(1e-40, 1e-38, n)
   547	
   548	    # ---- direction 1: a legitimate re-unfold PASSES ----
   549	    def test_legitimate_rerun_passes(self):
   550	        """Non-bit-identical, scattered at the MEASURED floor -- exactly what a real re-unfold
   551	        produces. The frozen-hash check rejected this; content comparison accepts it."""
   552	        ref = self._endpoint()
   553	        rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
   554	        noise = rng.normal(0, 4e-12, ref.size); noise -= noise.mean()
   555	        rerun = ref * (1 + noise)
   556	        self.assertFalse(np.array_equal(rerun, ref), "must not be bit-identical")
   557	        r = P.check_reproducibility(rerun, ref)
   558	        self.assertLess(r["max_rel_bin"], P.REPRO_RTOL_PER_BIN)
   559	        self.assertLess(r["rel_integral"], P.REPRO_RTOL_INTEGRAL)
   560	
   561	    def test_MUTATION_the_frozen_hash_check_would_have_REJECTED_that_rerun(self):
   562	        """The defect, demonstrated: identical physics, different bytes, hash comparison fails."""
   563	        import hashlib
   564	        ref = self._endpoint()
   565	        rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
   566	        noise = rng.normal(0, 4e-12, ref.size); noise -= noise.mean()
   567	        rerun = ref * (1 + noise)
   568	        h_ref = hashlib.sha256(ref.tobytes()).hexdigest()
   569	        h_new = hashlib.sha256(rerun.tobytes()).hexdigest()
   570	        self.assertNotEqual(h_ref, h_new,
   571	                            "the frozen-hash check rejects a legitimate rerun -- that was the defect")
   572	
   573	    # ---- direction 2: a semantics change FAILS ----
   574	    def test_coherent_normalisation_change_fails(self):
   575	        ref = self._endpoint()
   576	        with self.assertRaises(P4GateError) as cm:
   577	            P.check_reproducibility(ref * 1.001, ref)
   578	        self.assertIn("relative difference", str(cm.exception))
   579	
   580	    def test_small_coherent_shift_inside_the_per_bin_leg_still_fails_on_the_integral(self):
   581	        """The discriminating case: 5e-11 is inside the 1e-9 per-bin leg and outside 1e-11."""
   582	        ref = self._endpoint()
   583	        with self.assertRaises(P4GateError) as cm:
   584	            P.check_reproducibility(ref * (1 + 5e-11), ref)
   585	        self.assertIn("integral relative difference", str(cm.exception))
   586	
   587	    def test_a_single_corrupted_bin_fails(self):
   588	        """A localised semantics change: one bin moved by 1%, integral barely perturbed."""
   589	        ref = self._endpoint(); bad = ref.copy(); bad[17] *= 1.01
   590	        with self.assertRaises(P4GateError) as cm:
   591	            P.check_reproducibility(bad, ref)
   592	        self.assertIn("per-bin relative difference", str(cm.exception))
   593	
   594	    def test_evidence_no_longer_pins_the_endpoint_manifest_to_a_frozen_hash(self):

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""REPAIR-7 item 4: the sweeps cannot go stale against themselves.
     3	
     4	The recorded-fields inventory was committed saying 66 fields / 22 gates while its own generator
     5	reported 82 / 24, and the pipeline document said 22/324 while the tool said 23/326. The artifact
     6	drifted from its generator INSIDE the round that created it -- the exact failure the artifact
     7	existed to prevent, and the verifier found it rather than the author.
     8	
     9	A prose document cannot be diffed against a script, so each sweep now emits a machine-readable
    10	`summary()`, the summary is committed as a snapshot, and these tests regenerate and compare.
    11	Staleness is now a red test on the author's machine instead of a finding on someone else's.
    12	
    13	Updating the snapshot is deliberate: run this file with `--update` and commit the diff, which
    14	puts the number change in the review where a reader can see it.

    17	import sys
    18	import unittest

    27	def _current():
    28	    import importlib
    29	    import tools_p4_sweep_pipeline_rc as pipe
    30	    importlib.reload(pipe)
    31	    # the recorded-fields tool prints at import; capture and discard that

    34	    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
    35	        import tools_p4_sweep_recorded_fields as rec
    36	        importlib.reload(rec)
    37	    return {"pipeline": pipe.summary(), "recorded_fields": rec.summary()}

    74	        self.assertEqual(cur - snap, set(), f"NEW recorded-but-unchecked field(s): {cur - snap}")

    82	        self.assertIn(f"**{nf} fields**", doc,
    83	                      f"the document does not quote the current field count ({nf})")
    84	        self.assertIn(f"**{ng} named\ngates**".replace("\n", " "), doc.replace("\n", " "),
    85	                      f"the document does not quote the current gate count ({ng})")

    89	    SNAPSHOT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    90	    SNAPSHOT.write_text(json.dumps(_current(), indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    91	    print(f"snapshot written: {SNAPSHOT}")

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Mechanical sweep of the standard P4 lane (repair-6 item 2).
     3	
     4	Two enumerations, grep-level, no judgement in the extraction step:
     5	  A. every field WRITTEN into a manifest/receipt, and whether its name ever appears
     6	     in a comparison context anywhere in the lane;
     7	  B. every named PASS-gate label, and what the gate's body actually does.
     8	
     9	The point is that the list exists as a checkable artifact. Last round's sweep was a pass I
    10	performed and it missed an item on its own list.
    11	"""
    12	import json, re, subprocess, sys
    13	from pathlib import Path
    14	
    15	ND = Path(__file__).resolve().parent   # re-runnable from any checkout
    16	MODULES = ["p4_lib.py", "p4_evidence.py", "p4_validate_active_lateral.py",
    17	           "p4_build_components.py", "p4_project_4d.py", "p4_adopt_standard.py",
    18	           "p4_check_receipt.py", "p4_lateral_replace.py"]
    19	SHELL = ["run_p4_standard.sh", "run_p4_unfold_std.sh", "run_p4_merge_audit_std.sh"]
    20	
    21	src = {m: (ND / m).read_text() for m in MODULES if (ND / m).exists()}
    22	sh = {s: (ND / s).read_text() for s in SHELL if (ND / s).exists()}
    23	allsrc = "\n".join(src.values()) + "\n" + "\n".join(sh.values())
    24	
    25	# ---------- A. fields written into products ----------
    26	written = {}          # field -> set(files that write it)
    27	# python:  man["x"] = ... / out["x"] = ... / rec["x"] = ... / prov["x"] = ... / "x": value
    28	for f, s in src.items():
    29	    for m in re.finditer(r'\b(?:man|out|rec|prov|foot|ids)\["([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)"\]\s*=', s):
    30	        written.setdefault(m.group(1), set()).add(f)
    31	    # dict literals assigned into those products
    32	    for m in re.finditer(r'"([A-Za-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{2,})"\s*:', s):
    33	        written.setdefault(m.group(1), set()).add(f)
    34	# shell: printf JSON keys
    35	for f, s in sh.items():
    36	    for m in re.finditer(r'"([a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{2,})":"', s):
    37	        written.setdefault(m.group(1), set()).add(f)
    38	
    39	# ---------- is the field ever COMPARED? ----------
    40	# a comparison = the name appears adjacent to ==, !=, <=, >=, or inside require/need with a
    20	> machine-readable `summary()`, the result is committed at
    21	> `state/p4-sweep-snapshots.json`, and `tests/test_p4_sweep_snapshots.py` regenerates and
    22	> compares. **Staleness is now a red test on the author's machine instead of a finding on
    23	> someone else's.** The snapshot also names any NEW unchecked field rather than only counting
    24	> them, because counts alone let one appear as another disappears. Update with
    25	> `python3 tests/test_p4_sweep_snapshots.py --update` and commit the diff, so a number change
    26	> lands in review where it can be seen.
    27	>
    28	> **REPAIR-7 ITEM 4 STATUS, checked 2026-08-09 and PARTLY DEFERRED with a reason.** The item was
    29	> "generate the inventory in CI". **This repository has no CI**: no `.github/workflows`, no
    30	> `.gitlab-ci.yml`, no pre-commit config, no Makefile target — verified by `git ls-files`. So the
    31	> literal form is not deferred by choice, it is unimplementable without first standing up CI, which
    32	> is out of scope for this lane and would be a repo-wide decision.
    33	>
    34	> **What IS implemented is the property the item wanted:** the sweeps emit `summary()`, the result
    35	> is committed at `state/p4-sweep-snapshots.json`, and `tests/test_p4_sweep_snapshots.py`
    36	> regenerates and compares on every suite run — so staleness is a red test rather than a silent
    37	> drift, which is the whole point. It has already caught two real drifts it was not written for: my
    38	> own new fields, and a change made by the PET lane entirely (two new shell files moving the
    39	> pipeline corpus 330 → 332).
    40	>
    41	> **What is genuinely deferred:** enforcement for someone who never runs the suite. Today the guard
    42	> binds an author who runs `pytest`; it does not bind a commit. If CI is ever added, the named fix
    43	> is one job invoking `pytest nd-unfolding/tests/test_p4_sweep_snapshots.py`. Recorded here rather
    44	> than closed silently, because "done" and "done in the only form the repo supports" are different
    45	> claims and the second is the true one.

    47	> Current snapshot: **99 fields / 25 gates**; pipeline **23 candidates across 332 shell

    55	not a defect. The distinction the list cannot draw for you:
   100	   repair-5 missing*, missed a second time by the tool built to stop missing it. Fixed to
   101	   `[A-Za-z]`; the count went 62 → 66. **A mechanical sweep is only as good as its pattern, and
   102	   the pattern needs its own test.**
   103	2. **It is line-based, so it cannot see a check performed in a loop.** Where a consumer does
   104	   `for k in (...): require(ids[k] <= rtol)`, the field name appears only in the tuple and the
   105	   comparison only in the body. Those show as `SWEEP-FP` below and were hand-verified.

    32	def _th2(path, key):
    33	    import ROOT
    34	    f = ROOT.TFile.Open(path)
    35	    if not f or f.IsZombie():
    36	        raise P.P4GateError(f"cannot open {path}")
    37	    h = f.Get(key)
    38	    if not h:
    39	        f.Close(); return None
    40	    n = h.GetNbinsX()
    41	    arr = np.frombuffer(h.GetArray(), dtype=np.float64, count=(n + 2) * (n + 2)).reshape(n + 2, n + 2)
    42	    C = np.ascontiguousarray(arr[1:n + 1, 1:n + 1]); f.Close(); return C

  1009	class NonAdoptableMarker(unittest.TestCase):
  1010	    """2026-08-09. The CANDIDATE is being produced WITHOUT a verifier PASS, deliberately, so it
  1011	    carries a self-declaring rejection. A marker whose only test is truthiness is worth nothing
  1012	    unless BOTH directions are demonstrated: that a marked manifest is refused, and that an
  1013	    unmarked one is not refused on that ground (otherwise a gate that always fires reads the
  1014	    same as a gate that works). Both are exercised against the real adopter CLI, not the
  1015	    library, because the adopter is what a future adoption step will actually invoke."""
  1016	
  1017	    def _prov(self, marked):
  1018	        env = {"P4_NON_ADOPTABLE": "1"} if marked else {}
  1019	        prov = {"identities": {"active_only_eq_sum5_relerr": 0.0,
  1020	                               "C_combined_eq_syst_stat_ml_relerr": 0.0,
  1021	                               "full_total_residual_eq_stat_plus_ml_relerr": 0.0}}
  1022	        return P.stamp_non_adoptable(prov, env=env)
  1023	
  1024	    def test_producer_stamps_only_under_the_env_var(self):
  1025	        self.assertIs(self._prov(True)[P.NON_ADOPTABLE_KEY], True)
  1026	        self.assertNotIn(P.NON_ADOPTABLE_KEY, self._prov(False))
  1027	        # an unset/other value must not stamp -- a truthy-string bug here would mark every build
  1028	        for v in ("", "0", "true", "yes"):
  1029	            self.assertNotIn(P.NON_ADOPTABLE_KEY,
  1030	                             P.stamp_non_adoptable({}, env={"P4_NON_ADOPTABLE": v}),
  1031	                             f"value {v!r} should not stamp; only the exact string '1' does")
  1032	
  1033	    def test_marked_manifest_is_refused_and_unmarked_is_not(self):
  1034	        import json, subprocess, tempfile
  1035	        outs = {}
  1036	        for marked in (True, False):
  1037	            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
  1038	                mf = Path(d) / "std_component_manifest.json"
  1039	                mf.write_text(json.dumps(self._prov(marked)))
  1040	                val = Path(d) / "val.json"
  1041	                val.write_text(json.dumps({"result": "PASS"}))
  1042	                cand = Path(d) / "cand.root"; cand.write_bytes(b"x")
  1043	                r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ND / "p4_adopt_standard.py"),
  1044	                                    "--candidate", str(cand), "--component-manifest", str(mf),
  1045	                                    "--validation", str(val), "--out", str(Path(d) / "o.root"),
  1046	                                    "--i-understand-adoption"],
  1047	                                   capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=str(ND))
  1048	                outs[marked] = r.stdout + r.stderr
  1049	        self.assertIn(P.NON_ADOPTABLE_KEY, outs[True],
  1050	                      "the adopter did not cite the non-adoptable marker when refusing")
  1051	        self.assertIn("not adoptable", outs[True])
  1052	        # the unmarked one still fails (its inputs are fake) -- but it must NOT fail HERE, or
  1053	        # the refusal is unconditional and proves nothing about the marker
  1054	        self.assertNotIn("not adoptable", outs[False],
  1055	                         "an UNMARKED manifest was refused as non-adoptable; the gate fires "
  1056	                         "unconditionally and would refuse a real candidate too")
  1057	
  1058	    def test_removing_the_marker_from_a_manifest_makes_the_gate_pass(self):
  1059	        """Self-guard: if someone deletes the stamp from the builder, this is what the adopter
  1060	        would then see -- and it would sail through. Demonstrated, not asserted."""
  1061	        prov = self._prov(True)
  1062	        with self.assertRaises(P4GateError):
  1063	            P.require_adoptable(prov)
  1064	        prov.pop(P.NON_ADOPTABLE_KEY)
  1065	        P.require_adoptable(prov)      # must not raise

  1068	class IntegralLegIsADiscriminator(unittest.TestCase):
  1069	    """2026-08-09. The integral reproducibility leg was widened once, correctly, and must not be
  1070	    widened again: its whole dynamic range is ~100x (incoherent round-off floor to fully coherent
  1071	    ceiling) and the tolerance already sits at 55% of the ceiling. A comment saying so is not a
  1072	    guard -- the previous widening was also well-commented -- so the ceiling is asserted here."""
  1073	
  1074	    def test_tolerance_stays_below_the_coherent_ceiling(self):
  1075	        """Widening toward the ceiling does not buy margin; it buys the inability to detect a
  1076	        coherent shift, which is the leg's only purpose."""
  1077	        self.assertLess(P.REPRO_RTOL_INTEGRAL, P.INTEGRAL_LEG_COHERENT_CEILING,
  1078	                        "REPRO_RTOL_INTEGRAL has reached the fully-coherent ceiling: at this "
  1079	                        "tolerance a uniform shift of every bin PASSES the integral leg, so the "
  1080	                        "leg no longer discriminates anything. See the derivation in p4_lib.")
  1080	                        "leg no longer discriminates anything. See the derivation in p4_lib.")
  1081	        self.assertGreater(P.REPRO_RTOL_INTEGRAL, P.INTEGRAL_LEG_INCOHERENT_FLOOR,
  1082	                           "REPRO_RTOL_INTEGRAL is at or below the pure round-off floor; it will "
  1083	                           "false-alarm on every correct re-run")
  1084	
  1085	    def test_the_range_is_genuinely_narrow(self):
  1086	        """The reason this cannot be fixed by picking a better number: the whole usable band is
  1087	        two orders of magnitude, so 'leave more margin' has nowhere to go."""
  1088	        span = P.INTEGRAL_LEG_COHERENT_CEILING / P.INTEGRAL_LEG_INCOHERENT_FLOOR
  1089	        self.assertLess(span, 200.0,
  1090	                        "the coherent/incoherent span grew; re-derive the argument rather than "
  1091	                        "assuming the recorded reasoning still applies")
  1092	        self.assertAlmostEqual(span, 103.4, delta=2.0)
  1093	
  1094	    def test_breach_diagnostic_separates_roundoff_from_a_coherent_shift(self):
  1095	        """The pre-specified response, DEMONSTRATED on both branches rather than described. A
  1096	        criterion written before a breach is worth nothing if it cannot actually tell the two
  1097	        cases apart -- and 'sign' was already offered once as a discriminator that could not
  1098	        (BEN-060), so this test is the check that the replacement is not the same mistake."""
  1099	        rng = np.random.default_rng(20260809)
  1100	        n = 10694
  1101	        b = rng.uniform(1.0, 100.0, n)
  1102	
  1103	        # (1) round-off tail: scattered, sign-biased at the recorded 0.4594, content-independent
  1104	        signs = np.where(rng.random(n) < 0.4594, 1.0, -1.0)
  1105	        a_round = b + signs * b * rng.uniform(0, 2e-11, n)
  1106	        d_round = P.diagnose_integral_breach(a_round, b, central=b)
  1107	        self.assertLess(abs(d_round["sigma_from_roundoff_bias"]), 4.0,
  1108	                        "a genuine round-off tail must look like the recorded bias")
  1109	        self.assertLess(abs(d_round.get("corr_reldev_vs_central", 0.0)), 0.05,
  1110	                        "round-off must be uncorrelated with bin content")
  1111	
  1112	        # (2) coherent shift: every bin moves the same way and the deviation scales with content
  1113	        a_coh = b * (1.0 + 3e-11)
  1114	        d_coh = P.diagnose_integral_breach(a_coh, b, central=b)
  1115	        self.assertEqual(d_coh["frac_positive"], 1.0)
  1116	        self.assertGreater(abs(d_coh["sigma_from_roundoff_bias"]), 50.0,
  1117	                           "a coherent shift must be many sigma from the round-off bias -- if it "
  1118	                           "is not, this diagnostic cannot do its job and must be replaced")
  1119	
  1120	        # the two branches must reach OPPOSITE verdicts under the pre-specified rule
  1121	        def proceeds(d):
  1122	            return (abs(d["sigma_from_roundoff_bias"]) < 4.0
  1123	                    and abs(d.get("corr_reldev_vs_central", 0.0)) < 0.05)
  1124	        self.assertTrue(proceeds(d_round))
  1125	        self.assertFalse(proceeds(d_coh))
  1126

   987	mixture error was measured directly against it: comparing $R_{\mathrm{glob}}\sum_p \mathrm{MC}_p$
   988	with $\sum_p R_p\,\mathrm{MC}_p$ over the twelve playlists changes the reco shape by at most
   989	$0.07\%$ in $\pT$ and $0.14\%$ in $\pPar$ (and $0.03\%$ across the low-$\pT$ ridge), with the
   990	residual $+0.12\%$ appearing as normalization rather than shape. The twelve playlists are nearly
   991	shape-identical, so a large reweighting of them is almost pure normalization. The statement above
   992	is therefore unaffected at the $14$--$30\times$ level.}
   993	
   994	\paragraph{A methodological component (estimator and iteration).}
   995	Part of the tension is regularization-dependent --- the same data, same
   996	normalization ($\Sigma\sigma$ within $0.1\%$), unfolded with a different
   997	GBDT backend moves the paper-cov $\chi^{2}$ by $\sim1$ unit while central
   998	values barely change (iteration count, by contrast, is negligible):

     1	# FINDING 2026-08-09 — `hadd` and `TParameter`: the general rule, and the complete triaged inventory
     2	
     3	**Status:** inventory complete and mechanically regenerable. Two live defects, both already known
     4	and both already handled at the read side; one OPEN scoping item (J36) which this reframing
     5	explains. No new defect found — the value here is the *criterion*, which is sharper than the trap
     6	it generalises, and the enumeration that bounds it.
     7	
     8	**Generator:** `docs/orchestration/audit_tparameter_merge_semantics.py` (332 tracked source files,
     9	C++ and Python, comments and docstrings stripped). Run with `--power` for the two live controls.
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## 1. The rule, in the form that is actually useful
    14	
    15	The version I first wrote down, and was asked to restate generally, was:
    16	
    17	> Every `TParameter<double>` in a merged file is a sum across playlists.
    18	
    19	That is **true and it is not the defect criterion.** ROOT's `TParameter<T>::Merge` defaults to
    20	mode `'+'`, so `hadd` does add same-named TParameters across all 12 playlist inputs — but for most
    21	of the fields that actually pass through a `hadd` in this repo, *adding is exactly right*. Stated
    22	as "every TParameter is a sum", the rule flags 10 of the 15 hadd-transiting fields and is wrong
    23	about 8 of them, which is the kind of rule that gets ignored after the third false alarm.
    24	
    25	The criterion that separates the real cases:
    26	
    27	> **A `hadd`-summed `TParameter` is correct for an EXTENSIVE quantity — one that legitimately adds
    28	> across playlists (POT, event counts, migration censuses) — and wrong for an INTENSIVE one (a
    29	> per-playlist constant, a ratio) or a FLAG (per-playlist 0/1, which becomes a count in [0, 12]).**
    30	>
    31	> **And a fourth case that neither form catches: two extensive fields can each merge correctly
    32	> while a quantity DERIVED from them does not.** `sum(dataPOT)/sum(mcPOT)` is not the
    33	> playlist-mixture-correct ratio, and both operands look impeccable.
    34	
    35	That fourth case is J36, and it is the reason J36 sat undetected two functions away from an
    36	explicit, correct, well-commented defence of trap #8: the trap-#8 defence asks "is this field
    37	merge-sensitive?", both operands answer no, and the question that mattered was about their
    38	quotient.
    39	
    40	The other thing the inventory shows is that **both conventions are live in this codebase and the
    41	difference is one character in a constructor in another language.** `runEventLoopOmniFold.cpp:1900`
    42	writes `TParameter<int>("hasFullEventSchema", 1, 'f')` — the PET lane hit trap #8, read the
    43	manual, and used the merge-mode argument. Nothing at any read site distinguishes that field from
    44	`hasTruthOnlyMisses` two dozen lines later, which takes the default and sums. A reader cannot
    45	recover the semantics from the artifact; only from this table or from the C++.
    46	
    47	## 2. What passes through a `hadd`
    48	
    49	Only `runEventLoop*.cpp` output is ever `hadd`-ed on this campaign (`sbatch_hadd_MEFHC*.sh`,
    50	`run_p4_merge_audit_std.sh`, 12 playlists per merged endpoint). Of the 62 `TParameter` fields
    51	written anywhere in the tree, **15 transit a merge**; the other 47 are written by analysis scripts
    52	whose output is never merged, and their default `'+'` mode is inert.
    53	
    54	| field | type | mode | post-`hadd` meaning | class | verdict |
    55	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    56	| `dataPOTUsed` | double | `+` | total data POT over 12 playlists | extensive | **correct** |
    57	| `mcPOTUsed` | double | `+` | total MC POT over 12 playlists | extensive | **correct** |
    58	| `POTUsed` | double | `+` | total POT | extensive | **correct** |
    59	| `activeUniverseTruthEntrants` | long | `+` | census summed over playlists | extensive | **correct** |
    60	| `activeUniverseTruthExits` | long | `+` | census summed over playlists | extensive | **correct** |
    61	| `activeUniverseRecoEntrants` | long | `+` | census summed over playlists | extensive | **correct** |
    62	| `activeUniverseRecoExits` | long | `+` | census summed over playlists | extensive | **correct** |
    63	| `nTruthOnlyMisses` | long | `+` | total truth-only misses | extensive | **correct** |
    64	| `activeUniverseIndex` | int | `f` | first playlist's value | identity | **correct (explicit `'f'`)** |
    65	| `activeUniverseIsLateral` | int | `f` | first playlist's value | identity | **correct (explicit `'f'`)** |
    66	| `hasActiveUniverse` | int | `f` | first playlist's value | flag | **correct (explicit `'f'`)** |
    67	| `hasFullEventSchema` | int | `f` | first playlist's value | flag | **correct (explicit `'f'`)** |
    68	| `fullPhaseSpace` | int | `f` | first playlist's value | flag | **correct (explicit `'f'`)** |
    69	| `hasTruthOnlyMisses` | int | `+` | **count of playlists with misses, in [0,12]** | flag | **DEFECT — mitigated at the reader** |
    70	| `pTmu_fiducial_nucleons` | double | `+` | **12 x the nucleon count** | intensive | **DEFECT — retired at the writer** |
    71	
    72	Plus one derived-quantity defect that no single row can express:
    73	
    74	| derived | from | verdict |
    75	|---|---|---|
    76	| global `data_pot/mc_pot` scale | `dataPOTUsed`, `mcPOTUsed` (both individually correct) | **J36, OPEN** — ratios span 0.1707–0.2371 across playlists, 38.9 % max/min−1; the merged quotient discards the mixture |
    77	
    78	## 3. The two defects, and why neither is open
    79	
    80	**`pTmu_fiducial_nucleons`** — the original trap #8. Fixed on both sides: the event loop no longer
    81	writes it (`runEventLoopOmniFold.cpp:1908`, "Do not write pTmu_fiducial_nucleons here"), and the
    82	reader refuses the merged value outright (`unfold_2d_omnifold_unbinned.py:1323-1329`, "Ignoring
    83	merge-sensitive pTmu_fiducial_nucleons metadata"), substituting the fixed tracker constant
    84	3.2353e30. Note the *shape* of that fix: writer retired, reader defended, and a `[WARN]` printed
    85	if the field is encountered. That is the right treatment and it is worth copying.
    86	
    87	**`hasTruthOnlyMisses`** — found 2026-08-09 when `p4_evidence.py` required it to be in `(0, 1)`
    88	and every one of the ten endpoints reported `12`. The check was *correct about the writer's intent
    89	and wrong about the artifact*, and it fail-closed on ten perfectly good endpoints. Mitigated at
    90	the reader: `p4_evidence.py` now records it as
    91	`native_miss_playlists_with_misses`, requires `0 < value <= 12`, and requires it to agree in
    92	direction with `nTruthOnlyMisses`. **The writer is still wrong** — a per-playlist 0/1 flag under
    93	`'+'` — and the correct repair is one character in the C++ (`'f'`) or, better, a rename to
    94	`nPlaylistsWithTruthOnlyMisses` so the merged value's meaning is in its name. That is a change to
    95	the event loop, which re-running is a multi-hour production step in another lane, so it is logged
    96	as an OPEN item rather than done here.
    97	
    98	## 4. Rules
    99	
   100	1. **When adding a `TParameter` to anything the event loop writes, classify it before you write
   101	   it.** Extensive → default `'+'`. Intensive, identity, or flag → pass `'f'` explicitly. The
   102	   argument exists; five fields in this repo already use it.
   103	2. **Name the field for its merged meaning, not its per-playlist meaning.** `hasTruthOnlyMisses`
   104	   reads as a boolean at every call site and is not one. `nPlaylistsWithTruthOnlyMisses` could not
   105	   have produced the 2026-08-09 fail-closed.
   106	3. **A reader that validates a `TParameter` from a merged file must state which convention it
   107	   assumes** — a bare `in (0, 1)` is a claim about the writer's merge mode, made silently.
   108	4. **Ask the derived-quantity question separately.** Field-by-field merge-sensitivity review
   109	   passes J36 cleanly. Whenever two merged fields are combined, re-ask the question of the
   110	   combination.
   111	5. **The general form, for the next reader:** ROOT gives every mergeable object a merge policy,
   112	   and the default is usually the one that is right for counts. Any time a per-file *property* is
   113	   stored in an object with a *count's* merge policy, merging silently converts a property into a
   114	   tally. `TParameter` is where this bites here; it is not the only place it could.
   115	
   116	## 5. Bound on this result
   117	
   118	The sweep resolves field names statically. One write site builds its name at runtime
   119	(`assemble_gbdt5d_adopted.py:120`, `f"sqrt_tr_{k}"`) and is reported separately; it is in an
   120	analysis script whose output is never `hadd`-ed. Read sites are matched by literal name and are
   121	therefore over-inclusive, which is the correct direction of error for an inventory. The
   122	"transits a `hadd`" determination rests on the claim that only `runEventLoop*.cpp` output is ever
   123	merged — established by reading every `hadd` invocation in the tracked shell corpus, and true
   124	today; a new merge of analysis-script output would silently enlarge the live set, which is the
   125	one thing here that a future change could invalidate without any test going red.
     1	# FINDING 2026-08-09 — Quantities DERIVED from merged extensives: J36 is not one site, it is nine
     2	
     3	**Headline.** J36 has been carried since 2026-08-01 as a scoping decision owed on one function in
     4	one file. It is one member of a class, and the class has **9 live members across three code bases** (8 Python + 1 C++), all
     5	computing the same thing the same wrong way: a global Data/MC POT ratio recovered by dividing one
     6	`hadd`-summed extensive by another. Nothing is fixed here — the instruction was to size the class
     7	first.
     8	
     9	**Status:** class sized, not repaired. No new *kind* of defect; a new *count*.
    10	**Generator:** `docs/orchestration/audit_derived_from_merged_extensives.py`, AST taint over every
    11	tracked `.py`. `--power` pins J36 itself as a live positive control.
    12	
    13	---
    14	
    15	## 1. Why a second sweep was needed at all
    16	
    17	`FINDING-20260809-tparameter-merge-semantics.md` swept every `TParameter` and concluded, correctly,
    18	that `hadd`'s default summing is right for extensive quantities and wrong only for intensives and
    19	flags — 12 of the 15 hadd-transiting fields merge correctly.
    20	
    21	That per-field result has a structural blind spot:
    22	
    23	> **Two extensive fields can each merge correctly while a quantity DERIVED from them does not.**
    24	
    25	`sum(dataPOTUsed) / sum(mcPOTUsed)` is a POT-weighted mean of the per-playlist ratios, not the
    26	per-playlist ratio. Both operands are impeccable. A per-field review asks "is this field
    27	merge-sensitive?", gets `no` twice, and never looks at the quotient. That is exactly how J36 came
    28	to sit **two functions away** from an explicit, correct, well-commented trap-#8 defence of
    29	`pTmu_fiducial_nucleons` in the same file: the defence answers a per-field question, and this is a
    30	two-field question.
    31	
    32	The physics, from `AUDIT-FINDINGS-20260731.md` §7 (already measured, not re-derived here):
    33	per-playlist Data/MC ratios span **0.1707 (1B) to 0.2371 (1D)**, `max/min − 1 = 38.9 %`, against a
    34	global 0.2124. Playlist 1M (18.0 % of MC POT) is over-weighted by 17.1 %, 1D+1F (26.4 %) are
    35	under-weighted by ~11 %, and the POT-weighted mean absolute mixture error is **9.4 %**. Total
    36	normalisation is **not** biased — global and per-playlist scaling agree exactly when MC rate per
    37	POT is playlist-independent — so this cannot be detected or excluded by the 2D paper reproduction
    38	at 1.011. The error is purely in the playlist *mixture*.
    39	
    40	## 2. The class, sized
    41	
    42	30 sites in 10 files carry taint from a merged extensive. Broken down by shape:
    43	
    44	| shape | n | verdict |
    45	|---|---|---|
    46	| **`RATIO_OF_TWO_MERGED`** | **8** | **the J36 class — defective by construction** |
    47	| `RATIO_COMMON_SCALE` | 5 | benign; same field on both sides, the scale cancels |
    48	| `SCALED_BY_MERGED` | 10 | benign; applying a merged total to a quantity over the same inventory |
    49	| `OFFSET_BY_MERGED` | 7 | benign; `1 ± rel_mc` style plotting arithmetic |
    50	
    51	### The 8 members
    52	
    53	Every one reads a `hadd` product (`runEventLoopOmniFold_MEFHC.root` / `..._5D_MEFHC.root` are the
    54	outputs of `sbatch_hadd_MEFHC.sh` — verified, not assumed) and every one computes the same global
    55	ratio. Post-merge semantics are identical in all eight: **a POT-weighted mean over 12 playlists,
    56	used as though it were a per-playlist correction.**
    57	
    58	| # | site | function | severity |
    59	|---|---|---|---|
    60	| 1 | `2d-unfolding/unfold_2d_omnifold_unbinned.py:123` | `get_pot_scales` | **production 2D unfolder — this is J36 as originally filed** |
    61	| 2 | `2d-unfolding/unbinned_1d_study/unfold_ptmu_omnifold_unbinned.py:44` | `get_pot_scales` | **production 1D unbinned unfolder** |
    62	| 3 | `2d-unfolding/binned_study/scripts/unfold_ptmu_omnifold_binned.py:354` | `get_pot_scales` | **production binned pT study** |
    63	| 4 | `2d-unfolding/ibu_omnifold_paired_cdelta.py:109` | `make_response_measured` | IBU/OmniFold paired comparison — feeds a published cross-check |
    64	| 5 | `2d-unfolding/unbinned_1d_study/ptmu_closure_iteration_study.py:141` | `get_pot_scale` | closure study |
    65	| 6 | `2d-unfolding/binned_study/scripts/trace_binned_omnifold.py:58` | `main` | diagnostic trace |
    66	| 7 | `nd-unfolding/make_control_plots.py:68` | `main` | control plots (ND lane) |
    67	| 8 | `nd-unfolding/plot_control_corner.py:74` | `load` | control corner plots (ND lane) |
    68	
    69	**What the count changes.** As one site in one file, J36 read as a local wart in the 2D lane. As
    70	eight, three of them production unfolders and two in a lane that had no idea it was affected, it
    71	is a shared idiom: the ratio is recomputed from scratch in every consumer rather than obtained
    72	once from a vetted helper, so there was never a single place to fix it. That is the reason it
    73	propagated, and it is the thing a repair has to address — a corrected `get_pot_scales` in one file
    74	leaves seven copies.
    75	
    76	### C++ — the unswept language, now swept (2026-08-09)
    77	
    78	`git ls-files` C++ corpus, targeted pass (`scan_cpp`): **exactly one file reads a merged extensive
    79	at all** — every other C++ occurrence is a `new TParameter(...)` *write* in `runEventLoop*.cpp`.
    80	
    81	| | |
    82	|---|---|
    83	| C++ read sites | **2** — `ExtractCrossSection.cpp:171,172` (`mcPOT`, `dataPOT`, both from `"POTUsed"`) |
    84	| C++ ratio lines | **2** — `:224` and `:225`, the identical expression `-dataPOT/mcPOT` |
    85	| **C++ defect sites** | **1** — `:225` `sum->Add(hist, -dataPOT/mcPOT)`, with `:224` printing the same value into a log line |
    86	
    87	So **the class is 9, not 8**: 8 Python + 1 C++.
    88	
    89	#### Is the C++ site in a live path? YES — determined, not left open (2026-08-09)
    90	
    91	The provenance chain, each link verified:
    92	
    93	1. `2d-unfolding/ibu_1d_projection/build_1d_ibu_inputs.py` reads **`runEventLoopOmniFold_MEFHC.root`**
    94	   (its `--omnifile` default) — the `hadd` of 12 playlists — and reads `dataPOTUsed` / `mcPOTUsed`
    95	   from it (`:371`). Both are hadd-summed.
    96	2. It **rewrites them** as a single `POTUsed` into each of `runEventLoop_proj_data.root` and
    97	   `runEventLoop_proj_mc.root` (`:430`, `:443`).
    98	3. `2d-unfolding/ibu_1d_projection/sbatch_ibu_1d_projection.sh:51` runs
    99	   `ExtractCrossSection 5 runEventLoop_proj_data.root runEventLoop_proj_mc.root`.
   100	4. `ExtractCrossSection.cpp:171,172` reads `POTUsed` from each and `:225` forms `-dataPOT/mcPOT`.
   101	
   102	So the operands **do** trace to hadd-summed POT from the merged MEFHC omnifile — the same defect,
   103	one step removed through an intermediate file, which is precisely why a same-file review would
   104	never have found it.
   105	
   106	**And its output is quoted.** The 1D IBU projection is the repo's OmniFold-vs-IBU cross-check, whose
   107	Phase-16 verdict quotes post-fix integrals (paper 3.039e-38, OmniFold-2D 3.054e-38 / ratio 1.005,
   108	IBU 3.003e-38 / ratio 0.988 on `p_T`, 2.965e-38 / 0.976 on `p_∥`) and concludes both methods
   109	reproduce the paper to ≤ 2.5 % and agree with each other to ~1.7 %.
   110	
   111	**So it is in scope. Two qualifications that bound how much it matters, and they pull opposite ways:**
   112	
   113	- **The quoted headline is integrals, which this defect does not bias** (§1: total normalisation is
   114	  unaffected; the error is purely in the playlist mixture). And both arms of the OF-vs-IBU
   115	  comparison carry the *same* global scale, so it largely **cancels** in the ~1.7 % agreement figure.
   116	- **But the note's argument is about shape at the 1–2 % level.** `app_statmethods.tex:983` argues
   117	  that a coherent 1–2 % OmniFold-vs-IBU shape difference becomes a large χ² precisely where the
   118	  flux and Muon_Energy bands dominate the covariance. A 9.4 % POT-weighted mixture error propagates
   119	  through playlist-dependent flux shape — the same channel — and is several times larger than the
   120	  shape differences that discussion turns on. It does not cancel in the paper comparison, only in
   121	  the OF-vs-IBU one.
   122	
   123	The specific 1D-projection numbers are **not currently in `docs/analysis-note/`** (checked); the
   124	note references IBU conceptually and discusses the OmniFold-vs-IBU shape difference. So the C++
   125	site is live for a repo-internal quoted cross-check, and adjacent to — not inside — a note argument
   126	it could materially affect.
   127	
   128	**Method note, because it nearly went the wrong way.** The first C++ pass reported 7 reads and 2
   129	ratios. Five of the "reads" were multi-line `new TParameter<long>(` writes whose name string sits
   130	on a continuation line. Fixing that by looking back for `TParameter<` then over-corrected to 1 read
   131	and **0 ratios** — because `GetIngredient<TParameter<double>>` is the *read* idiom and matched the
   132	write test, so a real read was reclassified and the defect disappeared from the report. Only
   133	`new TParameter` marks a construction. **Turning a false positive into a false negative is the
   134	worse of the two errors**, and it would have reported "C++ is clean" for a class we were sizing.
   135	
   136	**Bound.** Taint is intraprocedural, so a helper returning a ratio and a caller consuming it count
   137	as one site, not two; and taint arriving via a dict argument is invisible. C++ is now swept but by
   138	identifier rather than AST, so a ratio split across lines or hidden behind a helper is not found.
   139	**9 remains a floor** — but a much tighter one than 8 was, because the language that was entirely
   140	unswept turns out to contain exactly one reading file.
   141	
   142	## 2b. GATING MEASUREMENT — does `app_statmethods.tex:983` survive per-playlist scaling? **YES.**
   143	
   144	A quoted claim asserted sensitivity at 1–2 % in exactly the region where an unquantified 9.4 %
   145	mixture error lives. That had to be resolved before anything else, and it is a bounded measurement
   146	with a definite answer.
   147	
   148	**Method.** No unfolding. The mixture error acts on the MC prediction *before* unfolding, and its
   149	size there is what the claim must survive. From the 12 per-playlist event-loop outputs
   150	(`runEventLoopOmniFold_1{A..P}.root`), weighted reco distributions on the analysis' own 14 pT and
   151	16 p∥ edges:
   152	
   153	```
   154	N_glob(bin) = R_glob * sum_p MC_p(bin)      R_glob = sum(D_p)/sum(M_p)   <- what the code does
   155	N_pp(bin)   = sum_p R_p * MC_p(bin)         R_p    = D_p/M_p             <- what is correct
   156	```
   157	
   158	with the shape part taken as `N_pp/N_glob` renormalised to unit yield-weighted mean, because an
   159	overall scale is not a shape difference and is not what `χ²_shape` sees.
   160	
   161	**The mixture error is real and large in the weights** — `R_p` spans 0.1707 (1B) to 0.2371 (1D),
   162	`max/min − 1 = 38.90 %`, reproducing J36's figure exactly from the files.
   163	
   164	**And it is negligible in the shape:**
   165	
   166	| | pT | p∥ |
   167	|---|---|---|
   168	| overall normalisation shift | **+0.119 %** | +0.118 % |
   169	| shape max abs deviation | **0.073 %** | **0.143 %** |
   170	| shape rms | 0.035 % | 0.087 % |
   171	| shape peak-to-peak | 0.105 % | 0.281 % |
   172	
   173	In the cells the claim names — pT bins 2/7/10, which carry 16/11/12 % of the χ² — the shape
   174	deviations are **+0.010 %, +0.017 %, −0.033 %**. Across the low-pT peak ridge (pT ≤ 0.4 GeV/c) the
   175	maximum is **0.032 %** with a peak-to-peak of 0.029 %.
   176	
   177	**Verdict: the statement stands.** The mixture error's shape effect is **14–30× below** the ~1–2 %
   178	coherent difference the claim discusses, and ~30× below it in the specific ridge the claim
   179	localises to. `app_statmethods.tex:983` does not come out. It takes a caveat, not a rebuild.
   180	
   181	**Why so small, given a 38.9 % spread?** Because a mixture error only becomes a *shape* error to the
   182	extent the playlists differ in shape, and these twelve are nearly shape-identical in reco pT. A
   183	large reweighting of shape-similar components is almost pure normalisation — which is the same fact
   184	J36 already recorded ("total normalisation is NOT biased") seen from the other side, and it is why
   185	the residual +0.119 % lands in normalisation rather than shape. The deviation that *is* there is
   186	coherent — a monotone tilt, +0.03 % at low pT to −0.07 % at high pT — i.e. exactly the coherent kind
   187	the claim says is hard to absorb, just an order of magnitude too small to matter.
   188	
   189	**This also bounds J36 itself, and it is the first measured bound rather than an argument:** on the
   190	2D analysis, the shape consequence of the global-POT-scale defect is **≤ 0.15 %**. That is a
   191	material input to the scoping decision — it does not make the defect correct, but it does mean no
   192	2D shape statement is at risk from it.
   193	
   194	**Bounds on this measurement, stated because they are the only ways it could mislead:**
   195	
   196	- It is a **pre-unfolding** bound. Unfolding could amplify it, but a 0.03–0.15 % input error would
   197	  need ~10–50× amplification to reach the scale under discussion, and nothing in this chain does
   198	  that.
   199	- It uses the MC signal-reco sample. Background also carries `pot_scale`, but background is ~2 % of
   200	  the sample (52 626 vs 2 682 267 entries in 1A), so its contribution is subdominant to the numbers
   201	  above.
   202	- It is measured on pT and p∥, the observables the claim is about. It does not bound the 5D/ND
   203	  quantities.
   204	
   205	## 3. What is NOT claimed
   206	
   207	- **No published number is withdrawn.** Total normalisation is unaffected (§1), and no result here
   208	  is re-derived. Sites 1–4 touch published or cross-checked quantities and the mixture error
   209	  propagates only through playlist-dependent flux shape and detector conditions; quantifying that
   210	  propagation is the scoping question, and it is still open.
   211	- **Nothing was repaired.** Explicitly out of scope for this pass by instruction: size the class,
   212	  then decide.
   213	- **The benign 22 are benign by shape, not by audit.** `RATIO_COMMON_SCALE`, `SCALED_BY_MERGED` and
   214	  `OFFSET_BY_MERGED` are argued safe from the operator and the field sets, not from reading each
   215	  one's physics.
   216	
   217	## 4. Rules
   218	
   219	1. **After any per-field audit of merged metadata, sweep the DERIVED quantities separately.** The
   220	   per-field question is structurally incapable of reaching a two-field answer, and the derived
   221	   site can be in a different file, a different lane, and written by someone who never saw the
   222	   per-field result.
   223	2. **A defect found in one file is a hypothesis about the codebase, not a fact about that file.**
   224	   J36 was filed against `get_pot_scales` in `unfold_2d_omnifold_unbinned.py`; the identical
   225	   function name appears in three files and the identical computation in eight. The cheap check —
   226	   grep the *computation*, not the symbol — was never run in eight days.
   227	3. **When a derived quantity is recomputed in every consumer, the duplication is the defect.**
   228	   Fixing the arithmetic in one place cannot work; the repair has to be a single vetted producer.
   229	4. **"Scoping decision owed" is a state that hides a size.** An item parked pending scope should
   230	   carry the count of its instances, because the scope question usually *is* the count question.
